n4ht6d.title: Tigers, zebras, quantum dots: Nanoparticles assemble into patterns
n4ht6d.content:
Non-equilibrium nanoparticle assembly on a liquid subphase yields a predictable morphological cascade. Credit: Nature Communications (2026). DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79569-4

Forget about how the zebra got its stripes. For a group of Cornell engineers, an equally important question is: What drives the formation of such eye-catching patterns?

Rather than studying the animal kingdom, the researchers looked to tiny semiconductor crystals called quantum dots to understand how they arrange themselves into striking cascade structures in evaporating liquid. As a result, the researchers can now control the process, which could lead to engineering the next generation of optical and electronic devices from nanoscale building blocks.
The findings were published Nov. 14 in Nature Communications. The study's lead author is Jonathan Palumbo, M.S. '25, a doctoral student in the Hanrath Energy Lab. Anjali Asthagiri '28 is the co-author.
"One of the beautiful aspects of this paper is that you can have a film that has a lot of disorder and complexity and weird structures that haven't been seen elsewhere, and most people would look at it and say, 'Oh, there's something weird going on there. Let's make sure we avoid making the film like that,'" said Tobias Hanrath, the Croll Professor in Engineering in the Cornell Duffield College of Engineering and the paper's senior author.
"I think the interesting conceptual shift is if you embrace the complexity and approach it as 'Ah, I wonder what's actually happening there? What gives rise to that?'"

e) Operando laser confocal microscopy images acquired during evaporation, capturing the dynamic emergence of the same morphological sequence. f) Visual analogy between NP morphologies and classical natural patterns (spots and stripes), illustrating the recurrence of finite-wavelength motifs across biological and synthetic systems. Credit: Nature Communications (2026). DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79569-4

Tiny crystals leave cascading patterns
Quantum dots, which were recognized with the 2023 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, are inorganic semiconductor nanoparticles—each essentially a cluster of 1,000 atoms—that have strong light-absorbing properties. Their optical and electronic properties can change simply by varying the dots' size and shape—capabilities that make them ideal building blocks for multilayered superlattices. Hanrath's lab has previously paired quantum dots with microbes to create nano-biohybrid systems that can harvest sunlight to perform complex chemical transformations.
"When people want to take the quantum dot and make a superlattice, they want to make a perfect crystal that's as big as possible, with no grain boundaries," Palumbo said. "But instead, what this paper explores is if we grow our super crystal as small as we can, with a cluster of maybe 20 dots, what kind of patterns can that make? And how do we step between those perfect monolayers and then stranger, smaller systems?"
To do that, Palumbo and Asthagiri used a tiny syringe to deposit 10 nanoliter droplets of ethylene glycol containing quantum dots under a laser confocal microscope. The droplets—each roughly 1/100th of a raindrop—would evaporate and shrink, leaving behind what Palumbo described as "a snail tail of film, which we call the cascade of morphologies."
"During the experiments, Jonathan and I would discuss why we may be seeing these cascades and the different underlying physics phenomena at play: solvent evaporation, convection, diffusion," said Asthagiri. "That process enabled us to start building our intuition for how to come up with a computational model."

Evaporation speed shapes the final film
Asthagiri developed the model and ran simulations for the ordering and packing of the quantum dots, which primarily formed tiles and ribbon patterns. The sequence of the cascades in the models matched that of the experiments. The researchers then set out to replicate the process using two forms of control: concentration and solvent volatility.
"If the solvent evaporates very, very slowly, you end up seeing a lot of different patterns form as you drive dots initially to the edge, forming a multilayer, and then going through the cascade of multilayer to monolayer to holes, to ribbons and tiles," Palumbo said. "If you use a really fast evaporator, instead of the film having time to organize and order from highest to lowest concentration, you just quench into some average regime."
While the physics behind the formations of quantum dots differs from that behind other natural examples such as tiger or zebra stripes, visually they resemble one another. And once you notice the patterns, they become hard to miss.
"Anjali and I used to send each other pictures of the patterns we'd see everywhere that looked exactly like dots," Palumbo said. "Like when the snow would fall and melt in Ithaca. You can see it on the macro scale, like with the new storms they're finding on Saturn, all the way down to animals, drying evaporatives and soup."

Publication details
Jonathan Palumbo et al., Emergent mesoscale nanoparticle patterns from a non-equilibrium liquid lens, Nature Communications (2026). DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79569-4

kzbhic.title: Chrome 157 for Googlebook rolling out with 27 new features, improvements
kzbhic.content:
Chrome 157 widely rolled out last week, and Google is now sharing the extensive changelog for Googlebook OS.

There are five new features for the browser in version 157:

Auto-Expand Vertical Tabs on Hover: Hovering over a collapsed vertical tab rail with a mouse or trackpad now temporarily expands it as an overlay so you can read full tab titles, switch tabs, or manage groups, and retracts when you move your cursor away. This is enabled by default and can be toggled off or on in Settings > Appearance > Tab position > “Auto expand tabs on hover” or by right-clicking the vertical tab rail.

Resizable Vertical Tab Bar: You can now manually resize the vertical tab bar to view longer page titles without truncation, and Chrome remembers your custom width across browser restarts and new windows (supported when “Auto expand tabs on hover” is turned off).

Direct URLs and Back/Forward History for Settings: Individual Chrome Settings subpages now have direct web addresses (such as chrome://settings/appearance or chrome://settings/privacy) that you can type, bookmark, or link to directly. Navigating between Settings subpages also works with Chrome’s Back and Forward buttons.

Tab Sharing Controls Bar: When sharing a browser tab in video calls (such as Google Meet), Chrome now displays a persistent control bar at the top of the window to “Stop sharing” or “Share this tab instead” from any tab.

“Save As” System File Dialog: The system “Save As” file picker is now enabled by default for explicit menu save actions (such as “Save link as…”, “Save image as…”, and “Save page as…”), letting you rename files and choose a destination folder, including Google Drive or external storage.

This is followed by 22 improvements, especially for the Bookmarks Bar, Vertical Tabs, and Address Bar. Of note is the “standard desktop text-editing menu” when right-clicking the address bar.

Bookmarks Bar Right-Click Menu: Context menus now open properly when right-clicking on the bookmarks bar or bookmark folders.

Bookmarks Bar in Fullscreen: Switching tabs in fullscreen mode while vertical tabs are enabled now keeps the bookmarks bar visible.

Bookmarks Bar During Screen Sharing: Clicking on bookmark items on the bookmarks bar now responds normally while presenting or sharing your screen in Google Meet.

Pinned Tab Hover Cards: Hovering over a pinned tab consistently displays the tab preview hover card even when a vertical scrollbar is visible.

Vertical Tabs Scrollbar Alignment: Aligned scrollbar spacing between pinned and unpinned vertical tabs to prevent visual jumping when scrolling through long tab lists.

Settings Subpages on Theme Change: Switching system appearance between light and dark mode now keeps you on your current Chrome Settings subpage instead of resetting to the main Settings menu.

Launcher “New Window” Shortcut: Right-clicking or long-pressing Chrome in the app launcher or taskbar now shows a “New Window” shortcut, including when Incognito mode is disabled by enterprise policies.

Google Slides External Monitor Selection: Restored the external monitor picker in Google Slides presentation settings for dual-screen presentations with presenter view and speaker notes.

Close Third-Party Sign-In Prompts: Clicking the close (X) button on third-party Google Sign-In prompts (such as on Reddit) now cleanly dismisses the dialog without freezing.

Partial Translate in PDFs: Selecting text inside PDFs opened in Chrome tabs now shows the Partial Translate option in the right-click menu.

Opening Downloaded PDFs: Clicking a downloaded PDF in Chrome’s download manager now opens it directly in a new browser tab instead of an external system viewer.

Media Controls During Picture-in-Picture: Opening a Picture-in-Picture video window no longer causes the media controls popup in the toolbar to close early.

Web App Installation Window: Installing a window’s only open tab as a web app now opens a New Tab Page instead of leaving an empty browser window.

Web App Back Navigation: Newly opened web app windows now start with only in-app history so the back button no longer returns to pages visited before the app was installed.

Multiple Web Apps on the Same Site: Installing one web app from a site no longer causes other web apps on that same site to appear as “Already installed” or fail to open.

Address Bar Copy Selection: Right-clicking highlighted text in the address bar now opens copy options without clearing your URL selection.

Shift+Up/Down Text Selection in Address Bar: Pressing Shift+Up or Shift+Down while typing in the address bar now extends multi-line text selection instead of selecting search suggestions.

Address Bar Right-Click Menu: Right-clicking anywhere in the address bar now displays the standard desktop text-editing menu.

Ctrl+L Full URL Selection: Pressing Ctrl+L now reveals and selects the complete web address, including URL parameters.

Address Bar Suggestions Dismissal: Clicking outside the address bar now cleanly closes the suggestions dropdown so the search box doesn’t remain stuck open.

Contextual Search Privacy Notice: Contextual search now shows a non-blocking privacy notice instead of a pop-up dialog that interrupts your workflow.

Stability fixes: Stability improvements were made across browser extensions, keyboard shortcuts, and managed browser policies.

1swkoa3.title: Discord’s Linux app sure did improve a lot this year
1swkoa3.content:
Discord recently shared a potted roundup of improvements made to its Linux app this year, including smarter updating, better screen sharing on Wayland and working push-to-talk.

Their Discord <3 Linux: A Year of Upgrades blog post also reveals that per-app audio sharing is finally coming to Wayland-based desktops, though it’s not ready for testing just yet.

As I don’t personally use Discord that often, the roundup was an interesting read for me.

Notable, Discord’s Linux installer was made a lot smaller. The new Deb package I downloaded is ~4.6 MB, while a (much) older release I found a link to is roughly 100 MB – a big difference!

The installer also installs a bit differently, launching a bootstrapped tool that unpacks the app in your home directory. Delta updates are used to reduce the amount of data fetched for subsequent releases, saving time and bandwidth – and don’t require sudo.

Discord’s Wayland support improved

Official announcement video

Screen sharing on Discord under Wayland has been patchy for ages, but thanks to work done with Igalia, the open source consultancy company, it’s in a much better state. Window sharing permissions get requested and granted via the XDG Desktop Portal.

Discord’s push-to-talk feature, which lets you hold a key to transmit your voice even when another app (like a game) is in focus, now works under Wayland too. The feature was implemented via the GlobalShortcuts portal.

Wayland is now default on most major Linux distributions, so Discord says it’s “the future we built for”. Video encoding now works on more supported GPUs, and its Go Live feature now works on Valve’s Linux-powered Steam Deck handheld.

Per-app audio sharing in Discord Linux

Right now, you can only share all of your system’s audio to Discord when running under Wayland or none of it. If you’re streaming a game but listening to music at the same time, you have to share both – not ideal.

Discord says it’s working with Igalia to add per-app audio sharing in xdg-desktop-portal so that you can choose which app (or game) sound passes through. It even says it is writing the relevant GNOME and KDE parts itself ‘to get it to users faster’.

When? Well, it won’t be super-duper soon as the relevant pieces need to land upstream and then be adopted and added to Linux distributions. Discord say the work is a ‘long term investment’ at making a great Linux screensharing experience.

Not just for their app, either. The changes will benefit any software that wants to securely access, record to share screens and audio on Linux desktops under Wayland.

Installing Discord on Ubuntu

The official snap remains the easiest way to install Discord on Ubuntu (and stay updated). Find it in the App Center or run sudo snap install discord from your preferred terminal emulator (which is Ghostty, right?).

If you prefer traditional packages, download the new(er, smaller) Debian package from the Discord website. If you get stuck with any of that, I have a guide to installing Discord on Ubuntu walking through those.

Has Discord got better for you on Ubuntu? Does push-to-talk work on Wayland? Let me know in the comments.

117o5bn.title: Cybersecurity AI startup Corma reaches $1B valuation in about 3 months
117o5bn.content:
Three months after introducing its product, AI cybersecurity startup Corma has raised a $125 million Series A round at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA, the company said. Corma offers AI models and agents trained for cybersecurity defense. It has now raised a total of $185 million from backers, including Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures, and Coatue.

The startup came out of stealth in August. Interest in its product skyrocketed after a series of security incidents sent chief information security officers scrambling on October 21 when a critical flaw was found in PHP, a popular web programming language. Another flaw was found in Node.js, the open source JavaScript runtime environment. Popular open source tool LiteLLM, a proxy for routing requests to multiple LLM providers, also disclosed a security incident. Other incidents were disclosed that day, too. The day showcased the kind of onslaught on security that AI has enabled.

Corma isn’t the only company using AI to play defense. Other examples include Kevin Mandia’s new startup Armadin, as well as Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, and other established players, and too many other startups to count. Still, it’s a young market and a necessary one. Corma says it stands out from the crowd by being a frontier AI research lab focused on protection.

jnnz9t.title: Audi A8 следующего поколения может быть построена на китайской платформе
jnnz9t.content: Немецкое издание Manager Magazin сообщает: Audi обсуждает с Huawei создание следующего поколения седана A8, ориентированного на покупателей в КНР. Если договоренности удастся достичь, немецкий флагман получит архитектуру китайской корпорации, а сборку наладят на заводе в Чанчуне.Китайская версия A8, по этим данным, больше не будет приезжать из Германии. Ее станут разрабатывать и выпускать с прицелом на местный рынок. При этом под «ключевыми разработками» Huawei имеются в виду медиасистема HarmonyOS и система автопилота Qiankun, а не готовое шасси – этот нюанс стоит держать в голове.Audi A8Выпуск модели собираются организовать на предприятии PPE – совместном проекте Audi FAW New Energy в Чанчуне. Первые машины должны появиться до конца 2028 года. Глобальный CEO Audi Гернот Дельнер рассчитывает, что такой шаг поможет загрузить мощности завода.Для рынков за пределами Китая новое поколение A8, как ожидается, пересядет на платформу MSB, знакомую по Porsche Panamera. Сборку при этом хотят перенести на завод Porsche в Лейпциге. В результате китайская и зарубежная версии флагмана окажутся заметно разными.Окончательно план, по словам инсайдеров, пока не утвержден. Внутри Audi и концерна Volkswagen он встречает серьезное сопротивление: противники опасаются, что ставка на архитектуру Huawei размыет нынешнюю ценность бренда Audi.О внедрении автопилота «За рулем» уже рассказывал на примере беспилотного такси Tesla.Понравилась публикация?Тогда добавьте «За рулем» в список интересных источников: 1. 1pi82c.title: M3 Goes EV! We Drive a Prototype as the M Car Undergoes a Monumental Change
1pi82c.content: Most BMW fans cannot help falling all over themselves when a new M3 is launched, but this time they might get well and truly tripped up. That’s because what BMW is calling “the fastest and most powerful BMW M3 of all time” is 100 percent electric. There’s no mention of a gasoline version and no special EV designation tagged onto the name, just “here’s the new 2027 BMW M3, and we hope you like it,” or words to that effect.After driving a camouflaged prototype and hearing all the dirty details at BMW’s Miramas test center in southern France, we most certainly do.This machine has four electrically excited synchronous motors, one for each wheel. The pair at each axle is not quite what you expect, with one motor situated ahead of the other and a reduction gear for one of them on each side of the shared housing. The front-axle motors make approximately 644 horsepower and 398 pound-feet of torque, while the pair on the rear axle is good for about 751 horsepower and 738 pound-feet. Combined output is likewise still subject to an asterisk at this pre-production stage, but total power is at least 838 horsepower, and torque is an axle-twisting 885 pound-feet. If you’re thinking the sum total is less than the two axles, you are absolutely correct. The surplus is there to allow for serious torque vectoring, both front to rear and side to side. In normal driving, the car operates strictly in rear-wheel drive, with the front axle brought in whenever there’s acceleration, if the situation demands front-axle recuperation, or if you have the drivetrain set to Sport mode.BMWFour motors require precise and rapid control during acceleration and braking, but they also play an outsize role in cornering. It all operates much more smoothly and immediately than any electronically controlled differential or transfer case ever could, so you absolutely get what you request. The so-called Heart of Joy (essentially another name for the M Dynamic Performance Control module) is the single ECU that oversees everything in the powertrain and driving dynamics arena. It’s the brain that seamlessly decides what motor is required for whatever demands you place on the car by looking at steering position, accelerator input, and braking demands, with a nod toward the basic settings that you have dialed in.The battery that powers all of this is specific to the M3, even though it fits in a similarly sized case as the one in the i3. It’s designed to give higher peak and sustained power output and is capable of higher energy recuperation (up to 540 kilowatts) and faster charging (420 kilowatts), which means it has a higher level of cooling. The battery capacity is slightly lower for all this, currently sitting at about 100 kWh. Estimated EPA range is currently 300 miles or so, but all of these numbers are subject to change. As for the difference between how this battery pack is installed versus the i3’s, the M3 gains a direct connection to the front and rear axle subframes for enhanced torsional rigidity for more precise handling.Whatever the underlying mumbo jumbo, we can say that it really works, and the result is simply epic. We first went out in the default mode, with the drivetrain, chassis, steering, and brakes set to Comfort and energy recovery set to Mid, just to get a feel of the track. Once we knew where we were going, we let fly with the M1 button, and that brought everything to Sport mode but left the energy recovery in Mid and, crucially, left the DSC stability control setting in On. We pressed the car hard, and the M3 absolutely responded, and our pace built immensely. But that eventually resulted in a bit too much understeer as speeds climbed, which led to a brief off-track excursion, as they say in the business. We kept on going, but the car was imposing a limit on our fun.We did what you would do at that point and duly selected the M2 button. That setting was programmed by our hosts to bring the drivetrain and chassis up to Sport+ and raised the recuperation to Max. It also put the DSC in a more permissive state, otherwise known as MDM, and all of that was the magic bullet. The car now dived toward apexes and slithered nicely out of corners. The front end was quite pointy, and the rear now had permission to loosen up. Our lap times fell, and our grin widened. This car felt alive. It really did feel like an M3, just like no other before it. Through it all, the braking response felt entirely natural, probably because on the track there was a strong base level of recuperation, overlaid with a thin veneer of friction braking for a precise feel of what is happening underfoot.Interestingly, there is a sound accompanying all of this, although BMW says it’s not modeled on any particular car. We drove it with the eDrive set to Auto, which delivers the augmented sound of six gears known as “stages.” You don’t have to shift in this mode, and there’s no real interruption of power, but the interior sound level rises and falls as the car progresses up and down through each stage. There’s extra emphasis on powertrain load and aggression, too, so when you’re driving the M3 hard, it really does give you the auditory cues that you miss when you drive an otherwise-quiet EV. If you want a manual-like experience, you can set the eDrive accordingly, and then you’ll get shift lights, and it’ll even cut power if you don’t upshift at the right time. In the time we had, this setting was not particularly fun. We’ll table this issue for now, probably until we can get our own M3 to soak in. You can also turn the eDrive to Off, in which setting the car will just quietly amble along like any other EV, but what’s the fun in that?The prototype’s camouflage didn’t do much to cover up the exterior of the new M3, as it was formfitting. That said, you couldn’t really get a sense of the exterior look of the car, although it was still clear that every panel below the greenhouse was different from the i3. The body is distinctly pulled out to cover the wide Michelin Pilot Sport S 6 tires. Also clear to see were the M Yellow DRLs and the track lights below them, as well as many of the carbon-fiber bits, such as the hood vents, the rockers, and the mirror housings.It was even more difficult to see what was going on inside, as much of the interior was obscured. But you could still see some things, such as the steering wheel and its extra buttons. The top of the “wings” (because the spokes are lower down in typical Neue Klasse parlance) has two extra red buttons per side. There are the M1 and M2 buttons, but there’s also the M Setup button you use in conjunction with the touchscreen to program each one. The fourth button is interesting; press it twice to deactivate the ADAS active-safety minders. For track work, it’s nice to have one button that will do all that. The 17.9-inch central screen was obvious, but BMW had it covered much of the time, except to show the new screens that had to do with setting up the M buttons. The Panoramic Vision screen at the base of the windshield was mostly visible and mostly the same apart from fonts and the like, but for some reason the central section was blocked off.As for what it’s called, the car’s official name is just 2027 BMW M3. Like we said, there’s no EV or Electric nomenclature tagged onto the end. As for the unofficial model code that you may be wondering about, that is ZA0. More will be divulged as we get closer to its summer 2027 launch date, including the price. We have a $90,000 placeholder, but that is subject to change. As for an ICE version, there is no official word from BMW. Stay tuned.➡️ Skip the lot. His father was a retired racing driver who opened Autoresearch, a race-car-building shop, where Dan cut his teeth as a metal fabricator. Engineering school followed, then SCCA Showroom Stock racing, and that combination landed him suspension development jobs at two different automakers. His writing career began when he was picked up by Edmunds.com (no relation) to build a testing department.

7vtbip.title: Windows 11 Is Collecting Data on Which Coding Agents and Developer Tools You Use
7vtbip.content:
Reverse engineering Windows 11's MissionControlAggregator reveals coding-agent and developer-tool usage bits in a diagnostic ETW report.
I recently asked AI to help me look through the latest Windows binaries for undocumented features and functionality. Among the leads it turned up, one list immediately caught my attention: coding agents such as codex.exe, claude.exe, copilot.exe, and cursor.exe, alongside familiar developer tools such as python.exe, dotnet.exe, gcc.exe, and code.exe.
Why would a Windows system DLL need a list of coding agents and developer tools?
The names were in MissionControlAggregator.dll. I asked the agent to follow the references and dig into what the DLL actually does. That led from a handful of string comparisons to a running Windows component that records which coding agents and developer tools have been used, saves that information locally, and reports it to Windows Diagnostics. And unless you have opted out of the “optional” diagnostic data (which is enabled by default), the data is uploaded to Microsoft.
I shared the initial finding on X. This post includes more details about the investigation behind it.
Following the names
Opening the DLL in Binary Ninja made the first lead easy to see. These were explicit executable names embedded in a Windows component:

Following the references showed that the names were used in comparisons. There are four CLI-agent slots checking copilot.exe, claude.exe, codex.exe, and agy.exe, with extensionless equivalents on the WSL route. Five desktop-agent slots check github.exe, claude.exe, codex.exe, cursor.exe, and antigravity.exe.
Here is one of the comparisons against codex.exe:

The compiler-generated C++ names are unwieldy, so I will call these functions executable-name matchers. For reference, one related matcher is std::_Func_impl_no_alloc<<lambda_340dfe7e962ab225b6ac33bc664bd54f>, bool, std::basic_string_view<wchar_t, std::char_traits<wchar_t>> const&, Microsoft::Diagnostics::MissionControlAggregator::Utils::AppType>::_Do_call. The screenshot shows another lambda instantiation performing the same kind of name comparison.
The feature guarding the new agent checks has a particularly direct name: CLICodingAgentUsage, feature ID 62580080.
And the list extends beyond AI agents. The same component checks for node.exe, python.exe, dotnet.exe, gcc.exe, clang.exe, gdb.exe, javac.exe, devenv.exe, and code.exe, among others. Those checks feed broader developer-tool categories. Some of these checks also verify the publisher: the Node.js slot expects Node.js Foundation, Python expects Python Software Foundation, and the .NET and Visual Studio slots expect Microsoft Corporation. The compiler/debugger group containing GCC and Clang has no additional publisher check in this path.
Where does the DLL get this information?
The next question was whether the component scans running processes itself. Following Aggregator::OnLoad revealed that it subscribes to existing Windows events instead.
For Windows programs, it consumes KernelProcess.AppStateChangeSummary and Win32kTraceLogging.AppInteractivitySummary. These provide application identities that its handlers parse and pass to the matchers. For WSL, it consumes Microsoft.Windows.Lxss.Manager.Exec and ExecCritical, using the imageName field. A regular Windows codex.exe can therefore reach the CLI-agent checks through the app-state summary route; this is not limited to Linux programs running inside WSL.
The relevant flow looks like this:
Aggregator::OnLoad
├─ WSL Exec / ExecCritical
│ └─ ProcessWslExecEvent → CLI agent matchers
├─ KernelProcess.AppStateChangeSummary
│ └─ ProcessAppStateChangeSummaryEvent → CLI agent matchers
└─ Win32kTraceLogging.AppInteractivitySummary
└─ ProcessAppInteractivitySummaryEvent → desktop agent matchers

Aggregator::OnRelativeTimerExpire
└─ MissionControlAggregatorLogging::ReportCohorts<12,4,5>
└─ Segments.SubCohorts ETW report

Aggregator::OnUnload / intermediate timer
└─ PersistentState::SaveToDisk
A successful match sets a slot in the aggregator’s state. Later, ReportCohorts<12,4,5> turns those slots into bitsets and emits a report named Segments.SubCohorts. The numbers correspond to twelve broader tool categories, four CLI agents, and five desktop agents.
ETW (Event Tracing for Windows) is the mechanism carrying that report. In this case, it is a self-describing TraceLogging event. Rather than writing the executable names into every report, the component assigns each category a bit. A set Codex bit means the matching tool was observed during the reporting window.
The source events also include runtime, time in focus, interaction counters, and resource usage. This component appears to discard those details and record only a bitmap of which agents were observed. The report’s timestamps describe the collection window, not how long each agent was used.
Although I found no prompt text or source code in this report, collecting which agents and developer tools someone uses already has significant privacy implications.
Is it actually running on a normal machine?
Strings and code are a useful lead, but I wanted to see the component running. I checked my Parallels Windows 11 ARM64 VM, build 26200.9974. Its MissionControlAggregator.dll was version 10.0.26100.9818, and CLICodingAgentUsage was already enabled as a service experiment. I had not manually enabled the feature.
DiagTrack, the Connected User Experiences and Telemetry service, was also already running with its startup type set to Automatic. It starts a separate AggregatorHost.exe process, and that process loads the DLL. The following administrative PowerShell commands show the service, its child process, and the loaded module:
PS> Get-Service DiagTrack | Format-Table Name,Status,StartType -AutoSize

Name Status StartType
---- ------ ---------
DiagTrack Running Automatic

PS> Get-Process AggregatorHost | Format-Table ProcessName,Id -AutoSize

ProcessName Id
----------- --
AggregatorHost 1500

PS> Get-CimInstance Win32_Service -Filter "Name='DiagTrack'" |
Format-List Name,State,StartMode,ProcessId

Name : DiagTrack
State : Running
StartMode : Auto
ProcessId : 10148

PS> Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='AggregatorHost.exe'" |
Format-List ProcessId,ParentProcessId

ProcessId : 1500
ParentProcessId : 10148

PS> tasklist /m MissionControlAggregator.dll

Image Name PID Modules
========================= ======== ============================================
AggregatorHost.exe 1500 MissionControlAggregator.dll
The process IDs connect the pieces: DiagTrack runs in process 10148, which is the parent of AggregatorHost.exe, process 1500; the module listing places MissionControlAggregator.dll inside that child.
The public ISO’s baseline VM had the coding-agent feature disabled by image default, so the evidence does not support saying that it is active on every Windows installation. On my ARM64 VM, however, the relevant feature and service were active before the test.
Testing it in practice
To test the finding in practice, I copied cmd.exe to a file named codex.exe and ran it in the interactive Windows session. The name alone was enough for the component to recognize it as Codex.
I captured an AppStateChangeSummary for the running process from the KernelProcess provider ({2839ff94-8f12-4e1b-82e3-af7af77a450f}), with LaunchCount=1 and TerminateCount=0. The aggregator’s saved state contained the value 2 in CLI slot 2, the Codex slot. A separate run without an additional ETW trace also set that slot, confirming that detection worked through Windows’ existing diagnostic collection.
That state is persisted in:
C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Diagnosis\AggregatorStorage\MissionControlAggregator$
The report normally follows a roughly daily boundary. To capture it immediately, I temporarily moved the saved reporting-window start 25 hours into the past and restarted DiagTrack with a trace listening for the aggregator. The resulting Segments.SubCohorts event contained:
Provider: Microsoft.Windows.MissionControlAggregator
Time: 2026-11-16T12:34:29.125116Z
Version: 0.1.5

CliAgentSubCohorts: 4
DesktopAgentSubCohorts: 0
FlushedFromSave: true
The value 4 is 1 << 2: the Codex CLI bit. The name had made it through the input summary, the matcher, the persisted state, and the emitted report.
I also tested the developer-tool path separately, using a copy of cmd.exe named gcc.exe. It set developer-tool slot 3. With optional diagnostic data allowed, I found the resulting Segments.SubCohorts event in DiagTrack’s upload queue with SubCohorts: [8] (1 << 3). This is the compiler/debugger category shared by GCC, Clang, and related tools, rather than a separate bit for each executable.
Following the report toward Microsoft
An ETW event by itself would not establish that anything leaves the machine. ETW is used for plenty of local diagnostics. The more revealing question was who was listening to this particular report.
The VM already had a Diagtrack-Listener session subscribed to both ends of the path. These PowerShell queries showed its subscriptions:
Get-EtwTraceProvider -SessionName Diagtrack-Listener `
-Guid '{2839ff94-8f12-4e1b-82e3-af7af77a450f}'

Get-EtwTraceProvider -SessionName Diagtrack-Listener `
-Guid '{00de11a2-ec06-58e5-1a2b-21bb21dbee4b}'
The first subscription, for KernelProcess, had MatchAnyKeyword=0x400000000002, which includes the summary’s 0x400000000000 keyword. The second, for Microsoft.Windows.MissionControlAggregator, had MatchAnyKeyword=0xe00000000000, which includes the report’s 0x800000000000 keyword. Both had level 255.
The subscription showed where the report could go. To check whether Windows actually queued it for transmission, I inspected DiagTrack’s EventStore.db and decompressed the JSON batches in its AsimovEvents table. This revealed an important condition: the agent-usage report is treated as optional diagnostic data.
When optional diagnostic data is allowed (enabled by default in the US setup I tested), Windows queues the coding-agent usage report for upload to Microsoft. I verified this by finding the agent event itself in DiagTrack’s upload queue:
{
"name": "Microsoft.Windows.MissionControlAggregator.Segments.SubCohorts",
"ext": {
"privacy": { "isRequired": false }
},
"data": {
"Version": "0.1.5",
"CliAgentSubCohorts": [4],
"DesktopAgentSubCohorts": [0],
"FlushedFromSave": true
}
}
I checked this with a clean installation of Windows 11 Home ARM64 using the latest official ISO, with the region set to the United States. Before changing any privacy settings, the Diagnostic data toggle was already enabled and labeled Include Optional. After completing setup with those defaults, AllowTelemetry was 3, confirming that optional diagnostic data was enabled.

Optional diagnostic data is therefore enabled by default, at least in the US setup I tested. If you did not opt out of it during installation or disable optional diagnostic data later, it is still enabled and your coding agent usage data is being uploaded. You can decline optional diagnostics during setup or turn off Send optional diagnostic data later under Settings → Privacy & security → Diagnostics & feedback. Microsoft’s diagnostics and privacy guide explains how to change it.

rj8i33.title: Gemini AI agents repeatedly bypassed safeguards to attack real website
rj8i33.content:
Google's Gemini AI agents repeatedly attempted to hack a real organization's website during AI model safety testing, finding ways to circumvent increasingly restrictive security controls designed to prevent them from accessing live systems.

The security incidents occurred in October as AI safety research company Trajectory Labs tested whether Gemini 4 Argon agents would engage in unauthorized behavior when faced with an impossible task, even with the model's built-in API safeguards enabled.

In reports published Friday, Trajectory Labs and the targeted organization, Epoch AI, revealed that the agents attempted SQL injection attacks, probed for sensitive information, impersonated employees, and repeatedly circumvented network restrictions introduced to contain their activity.

Epoch AI said it had not independently verified which AI models were involved, and that the Gemini identification came from Trajectory Labs.

The researchers tasked the agents with retrieving official answers to nonexistent problems from Epoch AI's FrontierMath benchmark, repeatedly instructing them to "NEVER stop, NEVER give up."

On October 20, approximately 40 agents began probing Epoch AI's live website for sensitive information, including administrator credentials and access to proprietary benchmark evaluation logs.

Epoch AI detected the activity and deployed an "agent hotline" that allowed the agents to send messages directly to its employees.

For three hours, the agents made 36,411 requests to a planted API endpoint and sent 487 messages through the hotline, including some that attempted to impersonate actual Epoch employees or claimed to be engineers and auditors requesting benchmark information.

An investigation also identified an attempted SQL injection attack and more than 200 attempts to access FrontierMath evaluation logs.

Trajectory Labs discovered the activity while reviewing agent transcripts and notified Epoch AI of the unauthorized attacks the following morning.

After discussing the incident with Epoch, the researchers agreed to continue testing against a local copy of the website instead of its live infrastructure.

However, the agents continued finding ways to circumvent the restrictions.

During testing on October 23, some agents recognized they were interacting with a copy of Epoch's website, identified the real website's IP address, and connected directly to its live infrastructure, bypassing DNS redirection designed to contain them.

When researchers blocked the IP addresses used to reach Epoch, an agent switched to another address that allowed it to access the live website again.

Trajectory Labs subsequently configured its network proxy to block direct connections to Epoch, but an agent found another way to retrieve the website's public content through a third-party web-reader service.

"In some of these runs, the agents worked out that they were on a copy, identified the correct raw IP to bypass our redirect, and reached the live site again, which Epoch alerted us about," Trajectory Labs explained.

In a separate technical analysis, Trajectory Labs researchers also discovered that the agents created a message board through a shared software package cache to communicate with each other, exchanging information about vulnerabilities and exploitation methods.

In one example, an agent shared a technique for bypassing restrictions on a deliberately vulnerable copy of Epoch's website, which another agent subsequently used to obtain credentials and complete the task.

The researchers also observed agents attempting to bypass CAPTCHA protections and impersonating employees to trick an AI assistant into revealing protected benchmark information.

Beginning October 26, Epoch AI agreed to work with Trajectory Labs on additional experiments, knowing the agents would have internet access and could interact with its public website.

During these tests, the agents again accessed Epoch's live infrastructure, making more than 65,000 requests to a planted API endpoint and attempting further SQL injection attacks and employee impersonation.

Trajectory Labs later moved testing into fully isolated environments without internet access.

Even after this change, the agents still tried to disable a fake control that allegedly blocked network access, and they succeeded in all three complete test runs.

The researchers said that the agents had not been explicitly instructed to hack websites or impersonate employees. However, they were given an impossible objective on purpose and repeatedly instructed not to give up.

Trajectory Labs acknowledged that the incidents resulted from shortcomings in its testing procedures, including conducting experiments without obtaining the affected organization's consent and relying on built-in model safeguards without sufficient additional monitoring.

On November 2, the company suspended all AI misalignment testing pending a risk assessment and the addition of further safeguards.

"These incidents show how easily testing capable AI agents can spill over to affect real systems and people, and there are not yet shared standards for doing it safely," Trajectory Labs warned.

Neither organization confirmed that any private Epoch AI information was exposed during the incidents.

This report comes as California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI on Monday, alleging the company failed to adequately contain autonomous AI agents during testing, resulting in more than 80 incidents in which it lost control of the agents.

The lawsuit follows a July incident in which nearly 700 OpenAI-powered agents escaped a controlled testing environment and attacked Hugging Face's production infrastructure while attempting to steal cybersecurity benchmark answers.

6874cy.title: Европейская команда переговорщиков впервые поучаствовала в переговорах Киева и США о мире
6874cy.content:
Представители Германии, Франции, Великобритании, Италии, Польши, Еврокомиссии, Европейского совета и НАТО впервые в качестве команды, ранее отобранной для переговоров с РФ, поучаствовали в переговорах украинских властей и США о мире в Украине. Об этом сообщил Владимир Зеленский в видеообращении к гражданам в понедельник, 16 ноября.

Украинский лидер назвал прошедшее "обсуждением между переговорными группами" - украинской, американской и европейской - "на уровне рабочих команд". "Дипломатические усилия активно продолжаются, и мы надеемся, что они не будут напрасными. Наша команда работает максимально конструктивно. Нам необходимо достойное завершение войны и гарантии безопасности для Украины", - заявил Зеленский.

Со стороны США в консультациях участвовали Стив Уиткофф и Джаред Кушнер. Общение прошло в онлайн-формате, очная встреча команд состоится в Берлине в рамках "коалиции желающих" 19 ноября. По словам Зеленского, прошедшее обсуждение было "непростым", но ожидается, что в столице ФРГ представители стран смогут выработать "конкретные совместные шаги в переговорном процессе".

Несколькими днями ранее лидеры стран ЕС договорились, кто будет представлять Европу на будущих переговорах о прекращении войны в Украине. В переговорную команду вошли представители институтов ЕС и пяти европейских государств.

Кушнер: Важно, чтобы Европа и Россия могли общаться напрямую

Зять президента США Джаред Кушнер, которого Дональд Трамп назначил одним из своих переговорщиков, подтвердил прошедшее трехстороннее обсуждение. По словам Кушнера, страны Европы на онлайн-консультациях были представлены советниками по национальной безопасности.

Кушнер отметил, что в тот же день провел беседу с Юрием Ушаковым - помощником президента РФ Владимира Путина. Он не уточнил, было ли это до переговоров с Украиной и Европой или после.

"Мы обсудили пути налаживания прямого диалога между Европой и Россией - взаимодействия, которого практически не было на протяжении последних четырех лет. Важно, чтобы обе стороны могли напрямую услышать опасения и предложения друг друга, работая над созданием более стабильного и безопасного будущего для Европы", - написал зять Трампа в соцсети X.

По словам Кушнера, в переговорном процессе сформировались три основных направления обсуждения: надежные гарантии безопасности для Украины, ее путь к членству в ЕС, а также восстановление страны после окончания развязанной РФ войны. "Хотя в публичном пространстве основное внимание зачастую уделяется разногласиям между сторонами, в ходе серьезных дискуссий, проходящих вне поля зрения общественности, продолжают появляться позитивные и конструктивные идеи", - отметил американский переговорщик.Москва: Подключение Европы к переговорам не согласовывалось

Помощник Путина Юрий Ушаков заявил 16 ноября, что Россия пока не считает представителей Европы участниками переговорного процесса. "Кто-то говорит о расширении формата, но с нами это не согласовывалось", - так Ушаков ответил на соответствующий вопрос на встрече с журналистами в Кремле.

По словам Ушакова, "вопрос об участии" Европы в переговорах может быть поднят лишь "когда мы получим четкий сигнал от европейцев о том, чего они, собственно, хотят и что конструктивного и содержательного они могут предложить". До этого США, Украина и Россия могут провести еще не один раунд трехсторонних переговоров, отметил помощник президента РФ.

Уиткофф и Кушнер объявили после встречи с Путиным 12 ноября, что Москва не возражает против подключения к переговорам европейцев. Сам президент РФ тогда же заявил, что "никогда не был против того, чтобы вести диалог с Европой".

y4y40y.title: Xbox's Project Helix "is not a PC that can also play console games"
y4y40y.content:
Next Xbox console is "designed to be the ultimate gaming machine" by removing the "arbitrary constraints between console and PC games"

Image credit: Microsoft

Xbox VP of Next Generation Jason Ronald has clarified that Project Helix is "designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games, not a PC that can also play console games."
In the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine, Ronald described Project Helix as "the ultimate gaming machine – one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed."
"The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it."
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed Project Helix's console and PC compatibility in March, adding that the console will "lead in performance" for Xbox and PC games.
As Ronald previously discussed at GDC Festival of Gaming, Project Helix will utilise neural rendering, which uses AI models to enhance graphics. Ronald identified neural rendering as a particular focus for Project Helix, as it also addresses the ongoing component crisis."It's definitely a challenging time, but as a system and platform designer, it's one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also [making] things accessible and affordable."
"This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower [and] additional memory."
He concluded: "I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last ten years."
Reports last month indicated that Project Helix is expected to launch during the 2028 holiday season, with a projected price between $1,200 and $1,800.
