gh-1440988244.title: GitHub - timboat/demons-souls-recomp: Native Windows port of Demon's Souls (PS3, BLUS-30443) via ps3recomp static recompilation. Bring your own disc image; no game files included.
gh-1440988244.content:
A native Windows build of Demon's Souls (PS3, USA BLUS-30443 or Europe BLES-00932). The game's PPU and SPU code is statically
recompiled to C/C++ with ps3recomp and runs as a normal x64 program
on a PS3 runtime and a Direct3D 12 renderer. It is not an emulator.

No game files are included. This repo holds only tools, patches and build scripts. SETUP builds the game
on your PC from your own disc image.

Community Discord: discord.gg/gTvrZZ75G for questions, setup help and
screenshots. Bug reports with a REPORT.bat zip are best as a GitHub issue. Thanks to MrSuS60 for having me in their Discord, and a special thanks to zackage7 who has been an immense help in testing and polishing.
Status

The whole game is playable, with sound, music and movies, on keyboard + mouse or an Xbox controller.
60 fps is recommended (50 on a 100 Hz screen). 30, uncapped and any custom rate work too. Above 60 fps
there are still known bugs, such as the sound drifting out of sync.
No online play yet. Multiplayer comes once the game is optimised.
Plays smoothly on Windows, macOS and Linux. The Steam Deck is playable too: not perfectly optimised
yet, but very good in most areas. The full development log is docs/NOTES.md.
Android (arm64) is in an early phase. It boots into the game and plays at 30 fps on a Pixel 10 Pro XL,
with a controller or touch controls. The main target is the AYN Thor, which I don't own yet, so it is
untested there. See Android.

Hit a stutter or crash? Press F8 when it happens and run REPORT.bat afterwards
(details).
What you need

Windows 10/11 x64 with a Direct3D 12 GPU. AVX2 is used if your CPU has it (Haswell / Ryzen or newer).
About 14 GB free disk space.
Your disc image of Demon's Souls USA (BLUS-30443) or Europe (BLES-00932): a .iso, a Redump .zip, or a
dumped folder with PS3_GAME in it. An encrypted image also needs its disc key: the .dkey file from the
dump, or the "Disc Key" line on Redump's page for the disc (USA,
Europe). SETUP tells the two apart by itself. See
European disc.
Nothing else. SETUP downloads what is missing into deps\, with no installer or admin rights: portable
Python and Git, the PS3 keys for EBOOT.BIN (from RPCS3's public source, kept in
%LOCALAPPDATA%), and a portable LLVM compiler with Microsoft's SDK via
xwin. All downloads are checksum-verified. An existing Python 3.10+,
Git, or Visual Studio 2022 (Desktop development with C++) + LLVM 17+ is used instead.
A plain folder path: no [ ] or &.

Each release has one download per system: DemonsSoulsRecomp-<version>-Windows.zip,
DemonsSoulsRecomp_<version>-Linux.zip (plus the Linux setup AppImage) and DemonsSoulsRecomp_<version>-macOS.zip,
each with only what that system uses. Linux / Steam Deck and macOS (Apple silicon): see their install guides
below (Linux, macOS).
Build it (one time)

Download DemonsSoulsRecomp-<version>-Windows.zip from the newest
release (or git clone) and unpack it,
e.g. to C:\Games\DemonsSouls.
Start DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe, press PLAY, and answer Yes to run SETUP.bat.
Give it your disc image: drag it into the window and press Enter. If it needs the disc key, SETUP opens
Redump's page; copy the "Disc Key" line and paste it with Ctrl+V. Enter takes the suggested
answer to every other question.
Wait for All done, then press PLAY.

step
what SETUP does
time*

1
extracts and decrypts the game files into game/
2–5 min

2
decrypts EBOOT.BIN → EBOOT.elf and checks it is the tested version
seconds

3
fetches ps3recomp at the tested commit and applies this port's runtime patch
< 1 min

4
recompiles ~94,000 PPU functions + 12 SPU programs into port/
2–4 min

5
applies this port's edits to the recompiled code
seconds

6
compiles DemonsSoulsRecomp.exe and the launcher
10–30 min

* on a fast 16-core PC. The compiler's full output goes to logs\build_last.txt. If something fails, fix
what it says and run SETUP.bat again: finished steps are skipped.
Linux / Steam Deck
Recommended: the native Linux build, with its own launcher. The game as a Linux program drawn with Vulkan, with no Proton.
On the Steam Deck five of the seven archstones hold 60 fps; the two heaviest spots (Boletarian Palace 1-1 and
Latria's second archstone) run at 55-56, and Boletaria around 48 mid-fight
(frame rates).

Install: run linux/native/install.sh from a git clone (or from the release's Linux ZIP; the launcher's
Update button needs the clone). It opens a one-click installer window: your disc image, its disc key, then
Install.
Play: python3 linux/native/launcher.py opens the native launcher, which is confirmed to work great. It
keeps your settings, updates and rebuilds, adds the game to the applications menu, and Add to Steam makes a
shortcut for game mode (a controller works the launcher). linux/native/play.sh starts the game directly.

Details: docs/LINUX_NATIVE.md.
Alternative: the Windows build through Proton (Steam's compatibility layer), built on your PC from your disc image.
Use it if the native build does not work for you.
It plays on Ubuntu 24.04 and the Steam Deck; the Deck is not perfectly optimised yet, but very good in most areas. You need a
Vulkan GPU driver, about 25 GB free, and an internet connection for the first run.

Download DemonsSoulsRecomp-Setup-x86_64.AppImage from the newest
release (between releases: GitHub →
Actions → Linux AppImage → the newest run → Artifacts). Make it executable (chmod +x, or right-click →
Properties → Permissions → Is executable). On a Steam Deck, do this in desktop mode.
Run it. It asks for your disc image (a file picker, or drag the file in), then the disc key if needed,
and runs the same six steps as SETUP.bat into ~/DemonsSoulsRecomp (DS_HOME=/other/folder puts it
elsewhere, e.g. on an SD card). It asks before each download, including Microsoft's SDK license. The
first build takes 10–30 minutes on a desktop and 1–2 hours on a Steam Deck.
It offers to start the game; the first start sets up Proton (a few hundred MB). To play later, run the
AppImage again (it updates and rebuilds what changed) or ~/DemonsSoulsRecomp/linux/play.sh.

Settings are the same switches as on Windows, e.g. DES_FPS=60 ./DemonsSoulsRecomp-Setup-x86_64.AppImage play
(a Steam Deck defaults to 30 fps). Steam Deck game mode: add ~/DemonsSoulsRecomp/linux/play.sh as a
non-Steam game, with Start in set to ~/DemonsSoulsRecomp and no forced Proton version. From a git
checkout instead: install Python 3.10+, git, and clang + lld 17 or newer, then run
sh linux/setup.sh /path/to/image.iso and sh linux/play.sh. Troubleshooting: docs/LINUX.md.
macOS (Apple silicon)
A native arm64 build on Metal (by erikomis). It plays smoothly, but it is behind on updates: some of the
Windows and Linux features are missing.
You need about 14 GB free.

Install Apple's command-line tools (xcode-select --install), then with Homebrew:
brew install cmake ninja sdl2 glslang spirv-cross ffmpeg python@3.12 (FFmpeg is for the movies).
Get this repo (git clone, or the release's DemonsSoulsRecomp_<version>-macOS.zip) and, in its folder, run
DES_ISO="/path/to/Demon's Souls (USA).iso" mac/install.sh. A Redump image also needs
DES_KEY=<32 hex digits or the .dkey file>. It extracts the game, decrypts the EBOOT, recompiles and
builds; after a failure or a quit, run it again and it continues where it stopped.
Play with mac/play.sh. There is no on-screen keyboard yet: DES_NAME=<name> mac/play.sh names your
character. DES_FPS=30 gives the console's 30 fps (60 is the default).

mac/launcher/ has a desktop app that does all of this without a terminal (see its README). Controls,
settings and what is still missing: docs/MACOS.md.
Android (experimental)
Early phase. An arm64 build on the same Vulkan renderer as the native Linux build, packed as an APK.
It boots into the game and plays: on a Pixel 10 Pro XL (Android 17) it loads a save and holds 30 fps in game,
with a Bluetooth controller or the on-screen touch controls. The handheld it is meant for, the AYN Thor,
is untested because I don't own one yet, and other phones are untested too. No release: you build the APK
yourself, on a Linux PC or a Mac, from your own disc. Never share the APK: it contains the game's code.

Run the native Linux steps first (linux/native/build.sh venv game decrypt toolkit lift; on a Mac
mac/rebuild.sh venv game decrypt toolkit lift): they make the game files and the recompiled code from
your disc image.
Install the Android SDK with NDK r28 and a JDK 17, then run android/build_deps.sh (SDL2 + glslang for
arm64), android/build_so.sh (the game, ~10 minutes on an 8-core PC) and android/build_apk.sh install
(with the phone connected over USB, USB debugging on).
android/push_game.sh copies the game files (about 8 GB) to the phone. Then start
Demon's Souls (ps3recomp) from the app drawer.

It starts at 30 fps, with no movies, straight to the title screen. Not there yet: 60 fps, movies, the
on-screen keyboard (the character is named "Slayer"), and rumble. Details, measurements and the open points:
docs/ANDROID.md.
European disc (BLES-00932)
SETUP builds the European release too, from your own European disc image: it reads which disc it is and uses
patches/lifted-code-eu.patch, the port's edits carried over to the European EBOOT. The European game picks its
language from the system language: set PS3_LANG=fr (or de, es, it; anything else gives English) in the
launcher's Extra settings, or before PLAY.bat / linux/play.sh. Notes:

Use a separate folder for each release. Switching one folder from one disc to the other is not supported.
European saves are separate from US ones (the save folders are named after the disc, BLES00932...).
Tested on Linux through Proton: setup, a new character into the tutorial at 30 and 60 fps, and the French text.
Not tested on the European release yet: boss rush, the PC Remaster mod, and the native Linux, macOS and Android
builds.

Updating
Press Check for updates in the launcher. It downloads the newest release (no Git needed), rebuilds what
changed and reopens. Your game files, saves and settings are kept. Tick Keep my build after updates (or
set DES_NO_REBUILD=1) to play your current build and rebuild later with BUILD.bat.
Copies from before v2026.11.03.7, once: unpack the newest release ZIP over your folder, replacing files,
then press Play.
Play
Start DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe and press PLAY. It holds every option (frame rate, resolution, mods,
fullscreen, movies, god mode, recording, keys by letter, CPU pinning, GPU power smoothing) and saves them in launcher.ini.
Extra settings takes any NAME=value switch from this page or from an issue. --play starts the game
straight away, for a shortcut. Without the launcher, set the switches before running PLAY.bat.

launcher option
switch
what it does

Frame rate
DES_FPS=30|50|60|unlimited|31-240
Auto = an even rate for your screen: 60 on 60 / 120 / 240 Hz, 50 on 100 Hz, 72 on 144 Hz, 55 on 165 Hz, 75 on 75 Hz. Game speed is right at any rate. A rate that divides your refresh rate is perfectly even; others turn vsync off.

My screen has G-Sync / FreeSync
DES_VRR=1
lets a variable-refresh monitor follow the frames (vsync-off frames may tear, so the monitor shows each when it is ready); Auto is then 60 at any refresh rate. Leave it off on other screens: the picture would tear.

Resolution
DES_RES_SCALE=1.25|1.5|2|3|4
renders above 1280x720: 1.25 = 1600x900, 1.5 = 1920x1080 (a 1080p screen), 2 = 2560x1440; Sharper shadows = LD_RES_SCALE_SHADOW=1

Game
DES_GAME=game_remaster / game_mod, DES_BOSS_RUSH=1
the PC Remaster mod, your imported models (see below), or boss rush mode

Dump textures
LD_TEX_DUMP=1
saves every texture drawn, for texture packs

Skip the intro
DES_SKIP_INTRO=1
starts at PRESS START; story movies still play

Keep my build after updates
DES_NO_REBUILD=1
plays your current build instead of rebuilding

Smooth GPU power
LD_GPU_WARM=2 (1-4)
only if your PC switches itself off or restarts while the port runs (but not in other games): keeps the GPU's power draw steady between frames so a power supply does not trip. No change to the picture or frame rate; the card draws more power. If it still happens, LD_GPU_WARM=3 in Extra settings

Other switches: DES_MOVIES=0 skips movies, DES_CUT_BLEND=0 restores the original 30 fps cutscene camera,
DES_FULLSCREEN=1 starts fullscreen.
Controls
An Xbox (XInput) controller works when plugged in. A DualShock / DualSense needs Steam Input or DS4Windows.
Keyboard + mouse work alongside a controller; whichever you touch last takes over.

key
action

WASD
move

mouse (or IJKL)
camera (click into the game to capture the mouse)

left mouse / Shift
attack (R1) / strong attack (R2)

right mouse / Ctrl
block (L1) / parry (L2)

Space
roll / dash / back (Circle)

E
interact / confirm (Cross)

F / R
two-hand (Triangle) / use item (Square)

Tab / middle mouse
lock on (R3)

arrows
d-pad (switch items)

Enter / Backspace
Start / Select

Esc or F1
release the mouse (close the game with the X or Alt+F4)

Alt+Enter / F11
borderless fullscreen

F9
god mode (no death, HP/MP/stamina stay full)

Menus: the mouse is a pointer. Hover selects, left click confirms, right click goes back, the wheel
scrolls, and side buttons or PageUp / PageDown are L1 / R1. DES_POINT=0 turns pointing off;
PAD_MENU_MOUSE=0 turns the mouse off in menus.
Button icons show keys or PS3 buttons depending on what you used last (LD_TEX_KBM=0 = always PS3,
1 = always keyboard).
Mouse look follows the game's invert options. PAD_MOUSE_LOOK_SENS=0.0012 sets the sensitivity;
PAD_MOUSE_LOOK=0 restores the old stick-style mouse.
Keys go by position, so AZERTY uses ZQSD. PAD_KEYS_BY_LETTER=1 = by letter.
Change any key in the launcher: Controls, click a slot, press the key or mouse button (right-click clears
it). The button prompts and the title's PRESS ENTER KEY follow your keys.

Saves go to gamedata/, and logs to logs/; they grow ~600 MB an hour, and the previous run is kept.
Boss rush mode
Game: Boss rush in the launcher (or DES_BOSS_RUSH=1 linux/play.sh, or DES_BOSS_RUSH=1 linux/native/play.sh for
the native Linux build, DES_BOSS_RUSH=1 mac/play.sh on a Mac). Make a new character:
you skip the tutorial and start in the Nexus in soul form, with 7,000 souls and every trader there. Boldwin also
sells every weapon and shield, every armour piece and ring, every upgrade material, Turpentine and Firebombs,
priced by tier: the best weapons 40,000-75,000, top armour sets 30,000-50,000, rings 5,000-50,000, and items normal
shops sell at their usual price, so a run's boss souls buy a build but not everything.

Pick a boss: each world's archstone offers that world's next unbeaten boss and puts you at its fog gate.
After a kill: the boss's archstone offers the next boss (Fight the Tower Knight?) or Return to the Nexus?
Dying: you go back to the same boss's fog in body form.
The Nexial Binding takes you back to the Nexus and keeps your souls (its description says so too).
The run ends when King Allant dies; his fight and the ending are the game's own.
The timer at the bottom of the screen appears once you are in the game. It starts at the first fog and pauses
on loading screens, cutscenes and the title screen (and while the game is closed). Splits and the final time go to
bossrush\splits.txt and bossrush\results.txt.
Boss rush souls in the launcher (2x by default; DES_BR_SOULS=2, 3, 5 or 10): every enemy and boss gives that many times its
souls. The timer shows Souls x2 and so on when it is not 1x, so runs and videos say which they used.

It has its own saves in bossrush\, so your normal saves are never used. Play makes game_bossrush\ from your
game files the first time, in seconds and with no extra disk space (again when you change the souls setting).
Reporting stutters and crashes
Every run records frame timing (about 25 MB an hour, no visible cost; the last 10 sessions stay in perf\).

Press F8 right after a stutter or slowdown. Each press marks that moment.
After quitting or a crash, press Report a problem in the launcher (or run REPORT.bat). It packs
the session into one zip and opens GitHub's New issue page.
Pick the Stutter / slowdown or Crash / bug template, drag the zip in, and say where you were.

The zip holds a frame-pacing summary (report.txt), the recording (perf.txt), your system info
(system.txt) and the end of the game log (log_tail.txt). Your Windows user name is removed. Untick
Record frame timing (or set DES_RECORD=0) to play without recording.
Mods (optional)
PC Remaster mod by fromsoftserve (Nexus Mods, Demon's Souls mod 106): download its zip, then run the line
below. It makes game_remaster/ from hard links, so it uses no extra space and game/ is unchanged.
.venv\Scripts\python tools\install_remaster.py "path\to\the mod.zip" --apply
Texture packs:

Tick Dump textures and play; textures land in textures\dump\ as <KEY>_<w>x<h>_<format>.png.
Put an edited or larger file whose name starts with the same KEY in textures\replace\. .dds (DXT, BC7,
BC4, RGBA) loads faster than PNG.

Details are in textures\README.txt.
Models:

Export armour, weapons, characters or map pieces to glTF, edit them in Blender, and import them back.
Import writes game_mod\ from hard links; play it with Game: My models, and delete the folder to undo.
Edit the _l low-detail copy too. Rules are in models\README.txt.

.venv\Scripts\python tools\flver_tool.py export game\PS3_GAME\USRDIR\PARTS\bd_f_5010.partsbnd.dcx
.venv\Scripts\python tools\flver_tool.py import models\BD_F_5010\edited.glb game\PS3_GAME\USRDIR\PARTS\bd_f_5010.partsbnd.dcx

Packs and models are the game's art; share them only where that is allowed.
Repo layout
SETUP.bat / BUILD.bat one-time setup / rebuild
DemonsSoulsLauncher.exe the settings window (source in project/launcher/)
PLAY.bat / REPORT.bat start the game / pack a bug report
setup/ setup pipeline, toolchain finder, Linux cross toolchain
project/ CMake project
patches/ ps3recomp-local.patch (runtime, on ps3recomp @ 4e8f3ca) and lifted-code.patch (game code)
tools/ disc extraction, SPU lifting, perf report, mod installer, model tool
docs/NOTES.md development log: every fix, why, and how it was measured
linux/, mac/ Linux / Steam Deck kit and macOS build (docs/LINUX.md, docs/MACOS.md)
android/ Android (arm64) build: APK project, entry point, build scripts (docs/ANDROID.md)

Everything SETUP produces (game/, port/, deps/, .venv/, saves, logs) is git-ignored.
Never commit or share those: they are the game.
Troubleshooting

"could not get the keys … using RPCS3 instead":

The key download failed, so SETUP falls back to RPCS3; you can also run SETUP again later.
If RPCS3 then fails ("did not write EBOOT.elf"), close any open RPCS3 window and retry. Or decrypt
game\PS3_GAME\USRDIR\EBOOT.BIN by hand with RPCS3's Utilities → Decrypt PS3 Binaries; install the
firmware first if it asks.
In Windows Sandbox or a VM, RPCS3 can crash. Decrypt on another PC, copy EBOOT.elf into that folder,
and rerun SETUP.

"EBOOT.BIN is not the tested one": only the USA (BLUS-30443) and European (BLES-00932) discs, version
1.00 as on the disc, are supported.
Build tools not found: rerun SETUP or BUILD and allow the portable compiler download. Or install VS 2022
Build Tools with C++ and LLVM (winget install LLVM.LLVM), or set LLVM_DIR.
Setup seems stuck: one file can take a minute; see logs\build_last.txt. If nothing moves for many
minutes, press Enter once.
Black window or crash on start: check the end of logs\last_run_err.txt.
The game closes by itself with no message: run REPORT.bat right away. Its zip includes Windows' own
record of the crash (crash.txt), which the game's log cannot show.
Uneven frames at 100+ fps in busy areas: use 50 or 60 fps. On CPUs with two core complexes the game
pins itself to the one with the largest L3 cache; DES_AFFINITY=0 turns that off.
Something is briefly black or missing the first time you see it: its shaders are compiling in the
background. LD_PSO_ASYNC=0 waits instead.
"needs AVX2": the build was made on another PC. Run BUILD.bat on this one, or set DS_AVX2=0 b

1973t9i.title: Bond Girl Lea Seydoux Says ‘I Don’t Really Care’ Who Becomes 007's New Female Lead
1973t9i.content:
While the news of Robert Pattinson‘s casting as the new James Bond has sparked a frenzy on social media, Léa Seydoux, who starred opposite Daniel Craig in two James Bond movies, has little interest in finding out who will play the next Bond girl.

Speaking on a recent episode of The Runthrough podcast which was recorded before Pattinson was announced as the new OO7, Seydoux was asked who she thought should play the next Bond girl, or Bond woman. “I don’t really care,” she said, laughing. “I don’t really care, guys. How can you?”

Seydoux, who played Madeleine Swann in “Spectre” and “No Time to Die,” said Amazon MGM Studios’ takeover of the franchise signaled a “new era.”

“It became American. But I’m sure the movie will be great because it’s directed by Denis Villeneuve, who’s a very talented director. I’m sure he will do something great,” she said.

Seydoux previously told Variety in an interview before the Cannes Film Festival that she “was a bit sad when I heard that it was sold (…) but now that it’s Denis, I was like, Oh, at least it’s him, so it will be cinema.”

Seydoux, who worked Villeneuve on “Dune: Part 2,“ also revealed that she had sent Villeneuve a note congratulating him on his appointment. “He’s super cultured — he knows so much about cinema, but not only cinema,” she told Variety.

The actor, who’s a contender in the 2027 Oscar race with “Gentle Creature” and “The Unknown,” also weighed in on the search for Craig’s successor as the iconic British spy.

“It’s really difficult to cast James Bond, because you need to find an actor with a depth and with many layers, and I don’t think that the young generation really has that,” she said on the podcast.

Seydoux’s character played a pivotal role in Craig’s final Bond outing, “No Time to Die,” which ended with the spy sacrificing himself to save Madeleine and their daughter.

The French actor, who broke out internationally with Abdellatif Kechiche’s Palme d’Or-winning “Blue Is the Warmest Colour,” has worked with famed international auteurs including Wes Anderson, David Cronenberg and Yorgos Lanthimos.

9qb5gz.title: 'The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth' Review: Very Fun Hangout
9qb5gz.content:
“The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” gives you a highly pleasurable, shaggy heat-of-the-moment buzz. I’m not sure what I was expecting from a sequel to “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” but I dug just about every ambling, low-down minute of this one. (I realize that low-down is an ancient phrase, but this is a movie that ends with Boz Scaggs’ “Lowdown” playing over the closing credits. That’s how 1977 it is.)

The film is Quentin Tarantino, who wrote the screenplay, going wherever the day (or night) takes him. And that will do just fine. But it’s also Tarantino honed and manicured, given a polish of precision by the film’s director, David Fincher. As an artist, the hot-blooded, motormouth Tarantino is Dionysian; the rigorously controlled, ice-in-his-veins Fincher is Apollonian. Together, the two merge in a divertingly odd way. “The Further Mis-Adventures” is an enjoyable contradiction — a meticulous hangout movie. It hops from one thing to the next, but it’s disarmingly placid and even-keeled about what it’s doing. In spirit, it’s almost as if someone had slipped the movie half a Quaalude. It’s got no worries, and neither does its hero, Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt), the most sexy-cool aging ex-stuntman you’ll ever see.

“The Further Mis-Adventures” sprawls over one week in Los Angeles in the latter half of ’77 (the specificity has meaning; it’s supposed to be just after “Star Wars” has changed the force of the movie universe), and the tone is less sunlit intense than the 1969 of “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.” The counterculture has now evaporated, and everyone is stuck in a lackadaisical limbo of diversion, with one foot in the past. That doesn’t mean “The Further Mis-Adventures” is snobbish about the pop-culture era it’s rooted in. The film is brazenly and ever-so-slightly-ironically approving, whether it’s reveling in the throb of disco or the grand orchestral pomp of ELO’s “Tightrope,” smacking its lips at a tacky margarita bar that features mud-wrestling night, or opening with a last-days-of-blaxploitation movie called “Soul Brothers Die Hard!,” in which a couple of mack daddies sit around talking about the libidinous challenge of keeping their stables happy.

There’s a trick that Tarantino and Fincher spring several times here, and that’s to lure us into a piece of entertainment — a movie, a TV show — as if it were actually happening. That’s their tribute to the canny power of this stuff. Yet even as “The Further Mis-Adventures” embraces all this, you can feel a certain what’s-next? affectlessness hanging in the smoggy air. The only one who doesn’t feel it is Cliff, who lives in the eternal present. You might say that Cliff has become something of a loser. His old buddy Rick Dalton, who kept him supplied with stunt-double work, is now history (Rick has moved to Australia), and Cliff, with a slight limp and aching joints, is a man pushing 50, living with his cranky pawn-shop-owner dad (Peter Weller) in Marina del Rey, working odd jobs, driving around in his muscle-car jalopy. Yet in his slightly grizzled way he’s still a dreamboat, not to mention the most comfortable man in his own skin God ever invented.

Bringing Cliff back and expanding him into a more central presence, Brad Pitt hits the aura jackpot. With a Redford mustache and killer grin and golden sweep of honey-blond hair, parading around in gaudy short-sleeve bartender shirts with three or four buttons open, he makes Cliff high on his own supply of flinty good vibes. Cliff takes whatever comes at him, and that’s a life that suits him fine. He’s chivalrous and polite, but that’s connected to how comfortable he is with violence. He has no anxiety about it, and no anxiety about anything else. Pitt takes his own slightly seedy movie-star nobility and turns it up to full irresistible throttle. Even his voice is yummy — the sandy baritone directness of it, with that hint of a SoCal drawl. His Cliff puts everyone at ease, including the audience, but he keeps you guessing because he’s a paradox: a himbo with brains who can read anyone in the room — a sexy cowboy handyman who, if need be, will cut your throat.

The film’s opening episode is an appetizer of violence. It’s Tuesday night, and Cliff is working his shift as a projectionist at the New Beverly Cinema (the first of the film’s Tarantino Easter-egg in-jokes — there will be more, including a TV commercial for Red Apple cigarettes featuring Margot Robbie’s Sharon Tate). The theater is showing “Soul Brothers Die Hard!,” and Cliff talks along with some of the tastier dialogue as he changes reels. But his real job comes after the theater closes. That’s when he has to rendezvous with a scurvy thief (Karren Karagulian), who has brought along the twink hustler (Corey Fogelmanis) he picked up on Santa Monica Boulevard. The thief is looking to fence some items he stole from a house in the Hollywood Hills. But the robbery victim, unbeknownst to him, is one of Cliff’s old director pals. In short order, Cliff gets rid of the thief and puts the hustler on a bus back to Ohio. The shock — and joke — of it is that Cliff kills a man as casually as if he were mixing a banana margarita on his bartending night. That’s the Zen of Cliff Booth.

Fincher has referred to “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” as “‘Shampoo’ with violence” (an ace description), and that’s to say: It’s all about Cliff drifting around. It isn’t necessarily trying to be a movie story. But the film is fixated on Hollywood, to the point that each new location is identified with an onscreen title that will say (for instance) “Beverly Hills, 4.3 miles west of Hollywood,” as if Hollywood were the nucleus of the universe. What’s telling about “Cliff Booth” is that in its random anecdotal hangout way, it’s actually rooted in the world of television.

Rick moved to Australia because he’s starring in a TV series there called “Dingo Dan.” Those items stolen by the thief include a best director Oscar statuette, which implies that that trophy is a relic of a lost age. And the plot of “The Further Mis-Adventures” centers on Cliff getting summoned by Charlie Peters (Scott Caan), a garishly obnoxious star of TV Westerns and combat series. Charlie, who thinks he knows everything, does all his own stunt work (which suggests the character might be a Tarantino tweak of Tom Cruise — though the two characters, aside from being of average height, don’t have much else in common). Charlie, though, needs Cliff for something else: to get him out of an underworld jam. This is, after all, the stuntman who beat up Bruce Lee.

So Cliff meets with Charlie’s agent, the imperially tall, British, and coldly sexy Kate Crosby (Elizabeth Debicki). These two get a flirtation going — one so frosty that in spirit it feels more 2026 than 1977. You can see that there’s a mutual attraction. And you really see it after Cliff confesses his feelings, and their gamesmanship turns weirdly kinky. (The weird part is that the kink stays so casual.) But she’s classy and standoffish, and the most revealing conversation the two have is about the movies.

It’s one of those freewheeling Tarantino digressions (built on what sounds like a scrap from his abandoned script for “The Critic”), in which Kate tells Cliff that she was briefly a film critic who had gotten to know Pauline Kael (who Cliff dismisses because she didn’t like “Butch Cassidy”). Kate, sounding like a corrupt studio executive, says she now thinks of movies strictly as entertainment, and never as art. Cliff asks: Even “The Godfather”? Yes, she says, that’s just a gangster movie with artistic airs. It’s strange that the film never counters this view; it’s almost as if Tarantino agrees with it. Has he gone that far into pulp fetishization? (The author of “Cinema Speculation” is actually a great critic.) Or maybe he’s saying: Now that “Star Wars” has arrived, the movies as we knew them are dead.

I’m going on about this because I think it helps explain the enjoyably random, slightly disjunctive air of “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.” It’s the first Tarantino film that feels, in its structural DNA, like a glorified television series. At one point, the movie was supposed to be a series, and in spirit that’s kind of what it still is. Call it QT TV. The incidents hook you, but with less consequence than they’d have in a full-blown, let-it-rip Tarantino movie. “The Further Mis-Adventures” looks like a movie (Fincher gives it a stately sheen), and it’s way too violent for television. But the hangout factor, in this case, feels one small step removed from the characters-on-a-TV-series-are-your-family factor.

Driving the action forward are a pair of Filipino hitmen, the Verdusco brothers (Matt Groove and JB Tadena), who are singular in their viciousness; one employs a scary hatchet he calls Esmerelda. Scott Caan does a blustery job of playing Charlie, the blowhard TV star (I enjoyed the scene where he uses a live round of ammunition to put the fear into Timothy Olyphant as a fellow actor playing a Nazi), but given how central the character is, I wish he were less of a putz. I also wish we didn’t have to watch Roderick “Hot Rod” Harrison (Yahya Abdul-Mateen II), Charlie’s football-player-turned-actor costar, get not simply beat up but maimed for no good reason. On the other hand, I appreciated the quick reference to Cliff doing porn, which becomes a punchline to the fact that everyone he meets feels like they’ve seen him before. Speaking of porn, there’s a shoutout/tweak to PTA when “Best of My Love,” the Emotions track that opens “Boogie Nights,” comes on the car radio and Cliff flips the channel.

How is the ultraviolent climax? It’s kind of spectacular. Tarantino doesn’t use it to rewrite history this time, but in a funny way he does an instant mini version of that. What happens to Cliff in the big fight at the end should, by all rights, have eliminated him from the earth. But it doesn’t. It’s just a scratch. He doesn’t give a fuck, and he’s still there. To put it in QT TV terms: When’s the next episode?

s0nfna.title: Dean Koontz's Jane Hawk Books to Be Developed as TV Series
s0nfna.content:
Monarch Media has secured the rights to the Jane Hawk books by Dean Koontz with plans to develop them into a TV series, Variety has learned exclusively.

The search is now on for a showrunner to helm the project before it is taken out to market. Koontz is an executive producer along with Monarch Media’s Steve Barnett, Alan Powell and Vicky Patel.

“I’m a huge Dean Koontz fan, and like millions of fans of suspense readers, couldn’t wait for the next ‘Jane Hawk’ novel to come out,” said Patel. “I’m so excited to partner my love of Dean’s series with Monarch resources to create what I believe will be a compelling global hit series.”

As the books begin, Hawk is a former FBI agent and recent widow seeking answers about the death of her husband, leading her into a high-stakes conspiracy.

“Jane Hawk is a character as dear to me as if she were a real person in my life,” said Koontz. “I am therefore totally delighted that her story is in the hands of such an able and talented team as Steve Barnett, Alan Powell, and Vicky Patel at Monarch.”

The first Jane Hawk book, “The Silent Corner,” was published by Penguin Random House in 2017. Four more books in the series have followed: “The Whispering Room” (2017), “The Crooked Staircase” (2018), “The Forbidden Door” (2019), and “The Night Window” (2020). There was previously an attempt to develop Jane Hawk for TV by Paramount Television and Anonymous Content back in 2017, but the project did not move forward.

Koontz has sold over 500 million copies of his books worldwide and has been translated into 38 languages. He has hit number one on the New York Times hardcover bestseller list 14 times in his career, while 16 of his paperback books have gone number one. In addition to Jane Hawk, he has published multiple works in the Mike Tucker series, the Moonlight Bay series, the Odd Thomas series, and several more. His books have been adapted for the screen multiple times.

Koontz is repped by InkWell Management, Cheng Caplan Company, and Frankfurt Kurnit Klein & Selz.

Monarch Media previously produced the hit Richard Linklater film “Hit Man” starring Glen Powell, which debuted at the Venice Film Festival and then in theaters and on Netflix in 2023. The company is also behind the adult animated film “Tangles” starring Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Seth Rogen and Bryan Cranston, which recently premiered at the Cannes Film Festival. Their comedy feature “Babies” starring Rogen and Anna Kendrick premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September.

News of the new attempt at the Jane Hawk series comes as shows based on book characters with multiple novels to their name are more popular than ever. Just a few similar examples include “Reacher” and “Scarpetta” at Amazon, “The Lincoln Lawyer” at Netflix, and “Will Trent” at ABC.

1gak5ub.title: A “Very Human” Father-Daughter Story: ‘THR Presents’ Q&A With Myrsini Aristidou on Cyprus’ First Oscar Submission, ‘Hold Onto Me’
1gak5ub.content:
Cyprus has submitted its first-ever international feature film Oscar contender: Hold Onto Me, the feature debut of writer-director Myrsini Aristidou.

The film, starring newcomer Maria Petrova and Christos Passalis (Dogtooth), premiered at Sundance, where it won the World Cinema Dramatic Audience Award. It follows Iris, 11, whose grandfather has died, which leads to petty criminal Aris — the father she has never known — arriving in town. Can what starts out as a stubborn attempt to connect develop into a fragile bond?

Hold Onto Me is a Cyprus-Denmark-Greece co-production that takes a deep dive into a beach community and is partially inspired by the filmmaker’s personal experience. During a taping of THR Presents, Aristidou shared how “the narrative arc of all my films is sort of a love story and the disappointments that come with it.”

Hold Onto Me is based in Cyprus, but addresses universal themes. How would you describe what the film explores? And how important was it for you to show us characters who are not fully good or bad?

The subject matter is something that I care about a lot — all of us [do], I think. Our relationship with our parents matters. It is something we carry with us. We either work on it to improve it or make it better or heal it — or many people let it go as well and just move on and try not to repeat the same patterns. …

I care a lot about characters that are real, that are very imperfect, very human in their own way, and maybe even lonely in many ways.

How did you cast young Maria as Iris?

She had never done acting before, actually. Our casting director found her in Cyprus. She was younger than what I had written in the script. I wrote the script for a 15-year-old, and she was 10 and a half at the time. Yet, there was something about her. There was this innocence and authenticity.There is an emergency scene in the sea. I don’t imagine you had a big water tank that you filmed in?

It was very, very different and complicated. We didn’t have the budget to shoot in a pool. We shot in the sea. It was very cold; we shot at night. … We were splashing water with our hands.

Watch the full Q&A with Aristidou in the video above.

1k61osi.title: Еще одна звонилка или как я создал Nimbo
1k61osi.content: Время чтения7 минОхват и читатели1.3KКейсДисклеймерОсновной код Nimbo писал ИИ. Я немного правил его ручками, но больше занимался тем, как всё должно работать: логикой, интерфейсом, выбором стека и архитектуры. Я рассматривал этот проект как возможность поэкспериментировать. Хотелось на чём-то живом понять, что вообще можно собрать таким способом и получится ли потом этим пользоваться.ПредисловиеВообще-то я хотел просто играть с друзьями. Нужны были голосовые комнаты, чат, возможность показать экран, нормальный шумодав — и чтобы к железу софт был нетребовательным.В Discord мне до сих пор нравятся голосовые комнаты, но, когда заходишь провести вечер с друзьями, ощущение, будто попал на китайский базар: тут реклама, там предлагают Nitro. Плюс без обходных путей он не открывается. Надоело каждый вечер запускать ещё и запрет, а потом разбираться, почему с ним не работает твич, хотя вчера всё было нормально (ни в коем случае не критика авторов запрета, ребятам суперлайк за то, что они делают! В таком мире мы живем). В TeamSpeak не справляется шумодав, друзья слышали много лишних резких звуков. В Mumble мне не хватало привычных фичей, например возможности показать экран.Я попробовал какое-то количество звонилок, хотя и каюсь, ничего кастомного я не разворачивал. Вполне допускаю, что кто-то уже собрал именно то, что мне нужно. Но у меня сошлись все звёзды: хотелось нормально созваниваться с друзьями и было желание собрать с помощью ИИ какой-то сервис и довести его до состояния, когда друзья скажут, что готовы в него переехать. Из этого выросла моя мысль — публичная репа с сервисом, который можно развернуть у себя. Исходники и готовый клиент для windows уже лежат на GitHub в публичном репозитории, который вы сможете посмотреть и при желании покритиковать.А затея вообще рабочая?Начал я сразу с Windows-клиента. Хотелось понять, смогу ли я вообще довести свою затею до работающего состояния. В качестве стека для Windows я выбрал C++ и Qt. Главный критерий был — оставить как можно больше ресурсов игре. У меня есть друзья со старенькими ноутбуками, для которых ещё одна небольшая программа на фоне уже проблема. А шумодав и так обрабатывается локально, значит, с оптимизацией придётся потанцевать с бубном. Впрочем, я ещё подумаю, как разгрузить и этот момент.Так или иначе, C++ давал возможность очень точечно управлять тем, когда программа занимает и освобождает память. Qt же отвечал за окна, кнопки, работу с устройствами и основу интерфейса. Базовое представление о C++ у меня было, и я понимал, что в разработке с ним придётся повозиться. Но ради лёгкого клиента решил нырнуть поглубже в этот омут.Первая проба получилась. Был локальный чат, история сообщений, можно было открыть микрофон и проверить звук. В любом случае собрать EXE я смогу, а вот продумывать на нём дизайн, механики и UX будет тяжеловато, и токенов это будет есть х3. После правок нужно ждать сборку, потом раскидывать друзьям новый файл и просить его запустить. Мне хотелось быстрее видеть результат и чаще его проверять. Поэтому я заморозил этот клиент, приняв тот факт, что пилот работает, а значит, с ним можно работать. Я ушёл в веб на Vue + TypeScript. Серверную же часть я решил делать на Go, а для передачи голоса, камеры и экрана взял готовый LiveKit.ДизайнКогда начинаешь сразу делать интерфейс без холста, очень быстро упираешься в проблему чистого листа. А здесь ещё нужно объяснить нейронке, что ты хочешь, когда сам не особо пока понимаешь.Сначала я перебирал готовые киты и фреймворки, но постоянно что-то не устраивало. Начинаешь дотачивать элемент под себя, сталкиваешься с ограничениями выбранной дизайн-системы, просишь переделать ещё раз. Попыток становится больше, токены уходят, а результат всё ещё не устраивает. Я подумал, что направить ИИ будет проще айдентикой, а не готовым китом или фреймворком. Собрал то, что нравилось по настроению, цветам и оформлению. Так оказалось проще передать свой вкус и получить первый экран, который было существенно проще править дальше.У такого подхода есть своя цена. ИИ чаще плавает в мелочах: отступы, скругления, бордеры, вечно появляющиеся дивайдеры и пр. — правил изначально нет, а значит мест для нейронки, где она может уползти куда не надо, много. Приходилось давать много корректировок и быть внимательным при тестировании. Но в итоге этот подход мне показался более контролируемым. Увидел, что не нравится, оставил комментарий. От референса может остаться совсем немного или вообще ничего. Но он сделал для нас самое важное — решил проблему чистого листа.Голосовая комната в веб-клиенте Nimbo. Камера + показ экрана одного участника.Profile.nimboЕщё с самого начала мне хотелось, чтобы Nimbo был самостоятельным у каждого, кто его развернул. Я не хотел брать на себя общую регистрацию пользователей, хранить их персональные данные и администрировать чужие компании друзей. Моя задача — дать код и клиент, а дальше человек сам решает, где поднять сервер и кого туда позвать.Отсюда и профиль в файле. У человека на устройстве лежат ник, настройки, список серверов, куда его пригласили, и тех, которыми он управляет. Для каждого сервера сохраняется свой ключ доступа. Профиль можно выгрузить в файл .nimbo, защитить паролем и открыть на другом устройстве в совместимом клиенте. Сохраняются и настройки, и доступы к знакомым серверам. Общей базы всех пользователей Nimbo — нет. Профиль защищён обязательным паролем, который мы устанавливаем при первом экспорте.На самом деле порог входа для владельца сервера всё ещё высокий. Сейчас нужно арендовать VPS, заплатить за него и разобраться с разверткой. Не у каждого есть навыки или нейронка, которая поможет поднять это чудо за тебя. Участнику же проще — получил приглашение, выбрал ник и зашёл. К тому, как упростить жизнь хозяину сервера, я ещё, конечно, вернусь.Как в тест шумодава попало яблокоСначала я остановился на шумодаве RNNoise. Это распространённый вариант, голос мне нравился, задержка крохотная. Но на первых игровых сессиях выяснилось, что моя мышка прекрасно слышна — буквально каждый клик. Открываю пакетик с орешками — тоже слышно. Часть шума фильтр убирал, но резкие, звонкие звуки он не осиливает.При поиске замены пробовал Speex и другие варианты. В конечном итоге остановился на GTCRN. По моим ощущениям, в наших звонках он лучше подошёл под бытовую возню. В полной тишине отдельный щелчок ещё можно заметить, а во время игры и разговора его не слышно (за редким исключением). Голос стал чуть глуше, задержка обработки немного выросла, но в игре эта разница вообще незаметна. Плюс отдельно пришлось разбираться с тем, чтобы обработка не съедала начало и конец фразы.Чтобы сравнить фильтры на одинаковом звуке, взяли готовые записи щелчков мыши, укуса и жевания яблока и просто фразу. Сначала дали каждому шумодаву звук отдельно, затем смешали его с речью. Получилась запись, на которой можно послушать и помехи в паузе, и голос одновременно с ними.Собственно, тесты. Чем выше число в децибелах, тем сильнее подавлена помеха.Запись без речиRNNoiseGTCRNSpeexМышь, запись 13,55 дБ19,21 дБ0,33 дБМышь, запись 215,19 дБ21,13 дБ0,93 дБМышь, запись 328,82 дБ27,66 дБ1,61 дБЯблоко0,35 дБ21,29 дБ0,17 дБRNNoise на трёх мышах повёл себя очень по-разному. На одной почти не помог, на другой даже немного обошёл GTCRN. Зато с яблоком разница была большой. В нашем тесте обработка добавляла около 21 мс у RNNoise и 32 мс у GTCRN. В итоге GTCRN стал режимом по умолчанию, но RNNoise пока оставил как альтернативу. Важным нюансом является то, что всё это обрабатывается на компьютере пользователя. И это один из вопросов к будущей оптимизации.QA наше всеПозже я перешёл к клиенту на Windows. Больше всего времени там съела работа с ОЗУ. Открыл текстовый чат, посмотрел ролик, вернулся, включил и выключил камеру. Приложение стало кушать больше памяти. Сделал ещё круг — потребление снова выросло.При работе с C++ это был, конечно, ожидаемый исход. Возможность управлять ресурсами у тебя есть, но нужно пройти буквально каждое действие. Пользователь поставил ролик на паузу — думай, как выгружать это дело из памяти и что там может еще остаться. Выключил камеру, продолжая говорить — что должно закончить работу, а что ещё нужно звонку? И так во всем. Например, показательный случай был с камерой и показом экрана. Пять раз включили и выключили их в одном звонке. После пятого раза потребление разрослось до 305,8 МБ. Видео давно выключено, а программа продолжает держать память, которая понадобилась для его отправки. Оказалось, что та часть, которая отвечает за сжатие видео перед отправкой, зависала в памяти. После фикса в том же сценарии получили 30,3 МБ.С роликами в чате тот же принцип. При воспроизведении память растёт, а на паузе клиент освобождает декодер и сохраняет позицию, чтобы потом продолжить. Поэтому расход снижается уже после паузы. Мне было важно, чтобы тяжёлая часть функции заканчивала работу вместе с действием пользователя. В какой-то момент я и правда превратился в тестировщика. Нон-стопом заходил, выходил, включал, выключал, смотрел на цифры и пытался вспомнить, после какого именно клика потребление ОЗУ не вернулось к исходным значениям. Потому что все эти сценарии ИИ за меня продумать не могла. Но может я плохо просил...Спустя некоторое время голосовой звонок вообще показывал 19,9 МБ. На стенде считали частный рабочий набор — физическую память, принадлежащую процессам Nimbo. Но в реальности, вне стенда, 25–30 МБ — это наверное то, чего стоит ожидать.Настало время всё ломатьПроверка безопасности оказалась для меня одним из самых интересных занятий за всю разработку сего чуда. Я вообще люблю искать какие-то обходные пути, хаки, разбираться, что-то поломать, найти лазейку. Часть моделей я запускал локально на своём компьютере. Знакомил с нужной частью архитектуры, придумывал конкретную цель и гипотезу обхода и отправлял пару бедолаг-агентов её проверять на тестовом стенде. Оперативки немного, поэтому работал небольшими задачами. Например, так я нашел что анонимный выход мог полностью перезаписать базу. Я думаю там еще много чего можно накопать в плане безопасности. И это уже лежит пачкой задач в моем бэклоге)Что хочу сделать дальшеПервым делом — рисование поверх демонстрации экрана, как это реализовано в Zoom. Когда объясняешь другу, что нажать, чтобы игра заработала, очень хочется просто обвести нужное место. Ещё нужен игровой оверлей, чтобы видеть, кто в комнате и кто говорит. Упрощение запуска своего сервера. Было бы здорово поднять его прямо из приложения на компьютере одного из друзей и собраться без аренды VPS если железо позволяет. Клиент для Mac, возможно, для Android и более удобный интерфейс на небольших экранах. Планов, собственно, масса, потому что как продуктом мне уже нравится этим пользоваться.Как использовать?Nimbo бесплатна. Сервер, веб и клиент для Windows лежат в репозитории Nimbo. Можно взять, развернуть у себя, изучать, переделывать и делать всё, что, собственно, хочется. Код проекта распространяется по MIT. Я делаю это в первую очередь для себя и для таких же компаний друзей. Если будете делать свой клиент, мне бы хотелось сохранить совместимость с профилем .nimbo, чтобы человек мог забрать свои настройки и доступы с собой и применить в другой компании.На этом спасибо, что дочитали. Буду рад критике, мыслям и впечатлениям — и от самого Nimbo, и от этой истории.

nm9ht0.title: It Girl India Amarteifo’s Queen’s Gambit
nm9ht0.content:
India Amarteifio went to bed on May 3, 2023, a working but largely unknown young actress. The next morning — after Netflix dropped Queen Charlotte: A Bridgerton Story, a prequel in which Amarteifio plays a younger version of Golda Rosheuvel’s imperious royal — she woke up famous.

“The first thing I did that day was walk down the street with my co-star Corey [Mylchreest], and we were immediately recognized and stopped by fans,” she says. “We just looked at each other like, ‘OK, life has changed now.’ ”

Three years later, Amarteifio, 25, is still getting stopped on the street — at least three or four times a day. “People still rewatch it, or a new Bridgerton comes out and puts the spotlight back on,” she says. “I do wonder whether I’m going to be Queen Charlotte forever.”

Not a bad problem to have, considering her previous career anxiety: that her days as an actor might already be finished.

Amarteifio grew up in Southwest London, where acting classes helped burn off excess energy (“I was quite a bouncy child”). Her mother, a beautician, spotted newspaper advertisements for West End casting calls, leading to roles in The Lion King and Matilda, the latter an experience she likens to military training. She picked up representation and television work, including an episode of Sex Education, but graduated from drama school straight into the pandemic.

“It’s so silly, but I wasn’t booking anything, and I thought, ‘My time has passed at 20 years old,’ ” she says with a laugh.

Then came Queen Charlotte — and literal overnight success. The series instantly hit No. 1 on Netflix, topped Nielsen’s streaming charts and went on to surpass 80 million views, becoming one of the platform’s most popular titles.

After waiting so long for her big break, Amarteifio was willing to wait a little longer for the right follow-up. She took a long pause after Queen Charlotte, thinking about the career she wanted beyond the show that had made her famous. The offers were coming, but she was holding out for “more art house, indie, character-driven” projects.

She found what she was looking for in Clarissa, a Neon film from Nigerian twin filmmakers Arie and Chuko Esiri that opens in select U.S. theaters Dec. 11. Their reimagining of Mrs. Dalloway casts Hotel Rwanda Oscar nominee Sophie Okonedo as a Lagos society woman revisiting the summer that shaped her life, with Amarteifio taking over in the flashbacks. Ayo Edebiri and David Oyelowo round out the cast.

Cast and crew lived communally at the Esiris’ family resort in Nigeria, canoeing to work daily. “You would look down at the turquoise of the water and look up to see monkeys jumping overhead, and it was unreal,” recalls Amarteifio.

Amarteifio in Clarissa.

Courtesy of Neon

She also relished the chance to talk shop with her castmates. “I’m always just like, ‘Are you guys OK?’ ” she says with a laugh. “This industry can be so much sometimes, so I’m really interested in how people are doing and how they look after themselves. And, of course, I look at someone like Ayo and her trajectory and hope my career takes a similar form.”

The film’s festival run, beginning at Cannes and taking her to Telluride, Toronto and New York, has brought her closer to the kind of attention she wants. “People care about the work, and they want to know about how it was created rather than the focus being on what you’re wearing or who you’re with,” Amarteifio notes.

A movie musical remains on her wish list (“If you know of anyone who’s doing one!”), but otherwise she wants more of the same. Amarteifio’s fans, though, would prefer a busier release schedule.

“Sometimes when I go on Instagram, I’ll see people saying, ‘Why isn’t she working? Why isn’t she on our screens?’ and I’m like, ‘Guys, do you not think things have been coming through my inbox?’ ” she says. “I have had opportunities, but I’m thinking smarter. I can’t be seen doing random nonsense because I need to think about the impact it will have for my trajectory.”

This story appeared in the Nov. 18 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine. Click here to subscribe.

1vb4xsd.title: ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’ Review: Brad Pitt, David Fincher and Quentin Tarantino Mix a Cool Cocktail in Free-Flowing Spinoff
1vb4xsd.content:
It’s difficult to imagine a song choice more precisely capturing the essence of a movie than Boz Scaggs’ mellow yacht rock groove “Lowdown,” which kicks off the end credits of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. That might seem odd for a gritty comedy that builds to an ultraviolent climactic bloodbath, but this standalone chapter in the life of the now-retired stuntman from Once Upon a Time in Hollywood — the role that won Brad Pitt an Oscar — saunters along to its own idiosyncratic beat, running on a well-lubricated R&B engine.

The star’s golden glow and loose-limbed charisma, David Fincher’s exactingly controlled direction and the shaggier storytelling style of Quentin Tarantino’s screenplay are not always the most seamless fit. But the obvious mutual esteem and affection shared by that creative triumvirate is contagious and the movie has a good-time vibe that just won’t quit — even if it feels more stretched and less substantive than its 2019 predecessor. Still, few fans will complain, especially those who opt for the IMAX experience, before it hits Netflix on Dec. 23.

The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth

The Bottom Line

Sexy, seductive and chaotic in mostly fun ways.

Release date: Weds., Nov. 25 (in theaters); Weds., Dec. 23 (streaming)Cast: Brad Pitt, Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Peter Weller, Matt Groove, JB Tadena, Corey Fogelmanis, Karren Karagulian, Lauren Glazier, Timothy Olyphant, Nicholas HammondDirector: David FincherScreenwriter: Quentin Tarantino

Rated R,
2 hours 23 minutes

Eight years have passed since Cliff and Leonardo DiCaprio’s faded TV star Rick Dalton, for whom Pitt’s character worked as a longtime stunt double, mopped up three homicidal Manson followers — described here as “those fuckin’ hippie intruders” — in pools of their own blood. Rick is now starring in a TV series in Australia drolly titled Dingo Dan, and Cliff has aged out of the stunt game, though his is not an idle retirement.

He works as a projectionist at the New Beverly Cinema — the historic repertory house in the Fairfax district now owned and programmed by Tarantino as a 35mm stronghold — where the fictional blaxploitation film Soul Brothers Die Hard has been such a hit that Cliff can recite the dialogue along with the actors. Its cast is topped by former Oakland Raiders player Roderick “Hot Rod” Harrison (Yahya Abdul-Mateen II), who opens Fincher’s film with a quintessential Tarantino provocation, enlightening his character’s nephew about “how to keep multiple bitches turnt out.”

Cliff also mixes killer cocktails at a rowdy Redondo Beach tiki bar that features female mud-wrestling contests and picks up occasional work as “a day player” on XXX porn movies, including one currently in production titled The Sexorcist. For recreation, he participates in punishing demolition derby meets.

But Cliff’s main source of off-the-books income is as a fixer operating outside the law to solve problems for rich Angelenos in a jam. One task he’s assigned is to retrieve jewelry and a best director Oscar stolen from a married Hollywood veteran by Joey (Corey Fogelmanis), the young hustler he picked up outside Astro Burger on Santa Monica Blvd. When Joey shows up at the New Beverly with criminal associate Chicken Hawk (Sean Baker favorite Karren Karagulian) to exchange the goods for a wad of cash, Cliff turns the transaction to his advantage with brisk decisiveness and zero conscience.

Pitt’s Cliff in Once Upon a Time was very much a sidekick, a laid-back man of few words compared to Rick. This time around, he’s become a much more loquacious operator. But the film’s episodic nature — jumping around in time and neighborhood, shifts marked in onscreen text — makes the early action ambling and discursive. It takes an inordinate amount of time to settle on a central plot thread. Is it a romance? A crime thriller? A dark comedy? A hangout movie whose foremost concern is nostalgic time travel to late ‘70s Los Angeles? Actually, it’s all those things, though it can feel unfocused.

The narrative wheels kick into gear when Cliff gets a call from talent agent Karen Crosby (Elizabeth Debicki, never better), whose TV star client Charlie Peters (Scott Caan) has requested a meeting. Given that Charlie is known for doing all his own stunts — a detour into his career highlights shows B&W footage from popular series with titles like Fireball Jungle, Tom Horn: Stock Detective and Enemy Territory, along with an appearance on the Johnny Carson show — Cliff is perplexed as to the purpose of the meeting and Karen is unforthcoming with details. It’s likely she hasn’t even been let in on what Charlie wants.

Meanwhile, a pair of gangster brothers in town from the Philippines for a job, Eddie (Matt Groove) and Fernando Verdusco (JB Tadena), start making their presence felt, first with a jolt of horrific violence when they break into a family’s home in an upscale neighborhood. Even by Tarantino’s standards the brutal ugliness of that incident is shocking, made even more vicious by Eddie’s weapon of choice, a massive hammer he calls Esmarelda.

It turns out Charlie partied hard with the Verduscos while shooting in the Philippines, coincidentally where Cliff served in World War II, while the country was under Japanese occupation. On a drunken impulse, Charlie hired the brothers to eliminate a problem and although he has tried to back out of the deal, they have come to follow through and collect. That puts the TV star, Cliff and even Hot Rod in danger, since he and Charlie are shooting a private eye TV movie called Disco Kingpin.

There’s an Elmore Leonard kinship in the crime elements; Fincher takes his cue from Tarantino by making us squirm and laugh through even the most sadistic acts. But the movie lavishes just as much time and attention on Cliff’s slow-burn romancing of Karen and his playful banter with Charlie’s wife Toni (Carla Gugino), with whom he had a fling — unbeknownst to Charlie — while they were working on a Rick Dalton dud titled Salty the Talking Sea Otter. A tennis club doubles match with Cliff and Karen playing Charlie and Toni is key to establishing the latter’s significance in a tricky scenario to be revealed.

It’s no surprise that Cliff takes charge of Charlie’s predicament, never losing his cool even when he’s seriously at risk. As much as the movie is enamored with L.A., its period landmarks and the usual load of pop-culture ephemera so beloved by Tarantino, it’s also a big fat valentine to guys like Cliff, chill dudes cut from the same cloth as Steve McQueen. The film is more driven by casual vignettes than complex action set pieces, even if the spectacularly bloody final act is up there with Tarantino’s most operatic explosions of violence.

Often, The Further Mis-Adventures is so busy swooning over Brad/Cliff that it plays like episodic TV or part of a pulpy paperback series built around the lovable reprobate character. It’s less robust as a feature-length narrative, though that doesn’t make it any less entertaining. Tarantino disciples will eat it up, while Fincher obsessives should find plenty of the director’s pungent atmospherics, his technical flair and moody visual style.

Cliff’s inevitable showdown with the Verduscos seems not so much a story in its own right as a chapter in the man’s personal mythology to go along with the legends that Charlie recaps with breathless hero worship — notably that time he took down Bruce Lee. Tarantino doubles down on that here, thumbing his nose at the many people who found his irreverent besmirching of the martial arts icon insulting.

Caan is doing some of his best work, amusingly bouncing Charlie’s excitability off Cliff’s relaxed stoner gestalt or Karen’s self-possessed composure. For once using her native accent and taking full advantage of her imposing height, Debicki is in sublime command of her powers playing a savvy, languidly sensual Australian gal who is nobody’s idea of a delicate flower. Her chemistry with Pitt is off the charts.

At one point Crosby, as Cliff calls her, is seen attending the splashy premiere of Looking for Mr. Goodbar, photographed like a goddess in a fabulously draped white halter pantsuit and scarf — an unwise choice later that evening when she goes to a mud-caked figure-eight track and is surprised to find Cliff among the drivers. Even in moments that might be considered humiliating for many screen glamazons, Karen’s authority never falters. And she is equally adept at delivering a left and right hook.

Gugino also brings her A-game to a smart character who accepts her husband for the overgrown boy he is but by no means is immune to the flirty sexual frisson of a more mature hunk. The actress also looks nothing short of sensational.

There’s not a weak link in the ensemble. Abdul-Mateen is very clearly having a blast playing outrageous stereotypes in the fictional film and TV scenes within the movie, and when Rod is not on a screen or in front of a camera he carries himself with the effortless swagger of a former pro-footballer turned badass movie star.

The other vital cast contribution comes from Peter Weller as Cliff’s dad Gus, who, when not behind the counter at his pawn shop — where he teaches junkies how capitalism works — consumes an unending diet of TV, whether it’s The Rockford Files, Bonanza or Hee Haw. Father and son share an apartment in a sprawling Marina del Rey complex, where their spiky exchanges never obscure the nourishing love they get from each other. Mostly, Gus just wants Cliff to feed his cat and stop blocking the TV.

While the ‘70s New Hollywood reference is clear, Fincher and cinematographer Erik Messerschmidt — shooting on digital, a departure from Tarantino’s devotion to celluloid — perhaps lean into the dark, grubby look a little too eagerly, though the noirish aspect fits, echoed in Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross’ supple score.

Courtesy of Ren Klyce’s densely layered sound design, those orchestral interludes are woven in with a dizzying array of needle drops that make you wonder how much Netflix spent on music rights. (The unexpected use of Electric Light Orchestra’s peppy “Tightrope” over one violent sequence is inspired, and there’s not one but two Donna Summer tracks that absolutely slap.) Production and costume design from Don Burt and Trish Summerville, respectively, are a riot of period nods that never drift into kitsch.

Ultimately, however, the key ingredient binding together a movie that seldom meets an abrupt tangent it declines to explore is Pitt. His star wattage, shit-eating grin and cowboy gait — even with a limp and a body full of bones on which decades of stunt work have taken their toll — are dialed up to maximum magnetism.

1qp3ny7.title: Gabriel Iglesias Sets Fifth Netflix Special ‘Lone Star Fluffy’ For Christmas Eve Release
1qp3ny7.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Comedian Gabriel “Fluffy” Iglesias has hit on a major milestone with Lone Star Fluffy, a new hour special marking his fifth for Netflix and 10th overall.

Directed by Manny Rodriguez, the special premieres globally on December 24.

From biker bars to sold-out stadiums, Iglesias has spent 30 years turning life’s chaos into laughs. His new special brings his storytelling to Texas, taking on Lone Star rivalries, family antics and wild run-ins with a comedy legend and a pop superstar.

Produced by Fluffy Shop Studios and Triage Entertainment, the special was shot at The Tobin Center for the Performing Arts in San Antonio, Texas. Iglesias, John Bravakis and Joe Meloche served as executive producers.

For Iglesias, Lone Star Fluffy is the second of two specials to emerge from a 2024 deal with Netflix. The first, Gabriel Iglesias: Legend of Fluffy, hit the streamer’s global most watched list, ranking as its third most-watched special of 2025. His other Netflix specials include Stadium Fluffy (2022), One Show Fits All (2019) and I’m Sorry for What I Said When I Was Hungry (2016).

Ranking among the highest grossing touring comedians of all time, Iglesias is one of the few to achieve the hat trick of headlining and selling out Madison Square Garden in New York, Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and The Sydney Opera House in Australia. The fourth highest grossing comedian of 2025 according to Billboard, he continues to make the Top 10 year after year.

Iglesias is also one of the most watched comedians on YouTube with over 2.7 billion views and over 35.9 million fans across social media. In 2022, he made history as the first comedian to perform at and sell out Dodger Stadium, and earlier this year, he co-headlined the first-ever stand-up show at SoFi Stadium, alongside Jo Koy.

Iglesias is also known for starring in and exec producing the Netflix sitcom Mr. Iglesias, which ran for three seasons. In partnership with Fuse Media, he launched Fluffy TV, a family-friendly streaming television channel available on Amazon Prime, Google TV, Roku and more, in June. He is repped by CAA, Arsonhouse Entertainment and Hirsch Wallerstein Hayum.

i5ez1b.title: GTA 6 players are being abducted by aliens and knocked out by Bigfoot
i5ez1b.content:
Close encounters.

Image credit: Rockstar Games

Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.
The UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn. You'll need to have finished the game's first chapter, and it's most reliable after 2am in-game.

Grand Theft Auto VI Trailer 1.Watch on YouTube
As word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it. Follow the trail into the trees towards a blue glow, and you'll catch a UFO beaming down on a woman before it drops her and flies off. Head back to her car, as she requests, and the UFO returns for you. You apparently black out and come round three days later, and a bronze trophy called The Truth Is Out There should unlock.
You can seemingly trigger the event as either Jason or Lucia, and it isn't needed for 100 percent completion.
And that's not the only close encounter you can expect, either. YouTuber Lazarbeam bumped into Bigfoot on the afternoon of 18th November, hours before the game launched in the UK, while one Reddit user reported that they weren't quite sure what they'd stumbled on, titling their post "I think I found Bigfoot".Leonida's version of Bigfoot is actually the Skunk Ape, Florida's own swamp cryptid, and it can be found in the swamplands near Cottonmouth Lake in Mariana County as soon as free roam opens up. Listen out for a loud roar, then use Jason's tracking ability to follow it through the swamp. You may find it feeding on a deer carcass, while a second sighting has been reported south of Watson Bay.
Either way, the trail seemingly ends at a strange, human-like tree. Investigate it, and Jason blacks out, triggering a short cutscene in which the creature creeps up on him, as shown in this video. He later wakes near his vehicle, drenched in sweat. Save your ammo, though, as shooting at it won't do you any good.
Cryptids and aliens are, of course, something of a Rockstar tradition by this point. GTA 5's Mount Chiliad mystery kept players hunting for years, and Output Lag has already spotted two NPCs in a GTA 6 bar talking about goings-on there. Nobody has cracked a full Chiliad-style puzzle in the new game yet, but I'm sure that's just a matter of when, not if.
GTA 6 launched today on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, although some have been getting in on the action earlier as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even New Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first."Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

8nnzvu.title: Игроки уже нашли способ запустить GTA VI на ПК с DLSS 5 и генерацией кадров
8nnzvu.content:
Опрос

3DNews Новости Software PlayStation Игроки уже нашли способ запустить GTA VI...

реклама

Новости Software

Самое интересное в обзорах

19.11.2026 [20:49],

Фанаты не стали дожидаться действий от Rockstar Games и «портировали» на ПК в улучшенном виде криминальный боевик с открытым миром GTA VI практически одновременно с релизом игры на консолях.
Источник изображений: Rockstar Games

Напомним, GTA VI на PS5, Xbox Series X и S работает при 30 кадрах/с (и это в лучшем случае). О поддержке 60 кадров/с на современных приставках остаётся только мечтать — даже PS5 Pro для этого «недостаточно мощная».
Как подметил портал Videocardz, пользователи нашли способ задействовать в GTA VI нейронный рендеринг Nvidia DLSS 5 и функцию генерации кадров для повышения качества изображения и быстродействия игры до 60 и 120 кадров/с.

Демонстрация результата от блогера ElAnalistaDeBits

Метод предполагает запуск GTA VI на PS5, трансляцию игры на ПК с помощью карты захвата или Remote Play и интеграцию DLSS 5 посредством инструмента Veyra — для упрощения настройки предназначена утилита от моддера Phosphen.
Veyra ищет дубликаты кадров в видеопотоке с частотой 60 Гц, удаляет их и генерирует промежуточные. Другими словами, плавнее становится лишь картинка, но не игра — симуляция и отклик на действия пользователя работают при 30 кадрах/с.

GTA 6 DLSS5 1 PASS FG X6 by u/THZpr0 in DLSS

Эффект DLSS 5

Стоит отметить, что это не полноценная поддержка DLSS 5 от Rockstar. Официальная реализация использовала бы данные игрового движка, которые недоступны приложению, обрабатывающему уже готовый видеопоток.

GTA VI поступила в продажу сегодня, 19 ноября, только для PS5, Xbox Series X и S по цене от $80 до $100. Версия для ПК пока официально не подтверждена, но, по слухам, выйдет уже в первом квартале 2027 года.

xynb9g.title: 'Jeopardy!' Fan Convention Set for Washington DC
xynb9g.content:
What is Jeopardy!Con?

America’s favorite quiz show is welcoming fans to Washington, D.C., for a three-day event celebrating all things “Jeopardy!” Taking place May 7 to 9, 2027, the convention will feature live programming, engaging panels, interactive quizzes and exclusive merchandise.

Jeopardy!Con will feature behind-the-scenes sessions with iconic players from the trivia show, plus exclusive announcements and contestant casting opportunities. The weekend will also include a welcome party, closing celebration and other social gatherings.

Perhaps the most exciting aspect of Jeopardy!Con is an all-new live “Jeopardy!” competition format featuring famous players competing in front of thousands of fans. “The two-night marquee event will bring the game to life on a scale never before seen at ‘Jeopardy!,'” according to a press release.

Tickets will go on sale in early 2027, with additional programming to be announced.

“People are looking for meaningful ways to connect, and few things bring people together quite like a shared passion,” said Suzanne Prete, president of game shows at Sony Pictures Television. “For generations, ‘Jeopardy!’ has united fans through a love of knowledge, curiosity and competition. Jeopardy!Con builds on that legacy in an entirely new way, creating an unprecedented opportunity to bring fans together to celebrate the show, connect with one another and experience the franchise like never before.”

“Ever since I joined ‘Jeopardy!’ in 2021, I’ve wanted to bring this extraordinary community together in a way that’s bigger than anything we’ve done before and give fans the chance to interact with their quiz show heroes,” said Michael Davies, executive producer of “Jeopardy!” “One of the remarkable things we’ve seen through our live podcast and ‘Jeopardy!’ interactive events all over the country is just how much people want to come together and share their love of the game. Everyone on the team is incredibly excited to bring it all together next May.”
