1lc2tfr.title: Microsoft представила предварительную версию RDMA через USB4 для объединения ПК в локальный ИИ-кластер
1lc2tfr.content:
RDMA (удалённый прямой доступ к памяти) даёт одной системе возможность читать или записывать разрешённую память другой с меньшим участием операционной системы и процессора, чем при обычных сетевых соединениях. Microsoft адаптировала API Windows NetworkDirect для работы через USB4. В демонстрации используется форк llama.cpp, который распределяет выполнение модели между подключёнными компьютерами.
Практическая мотивация — модели с открытыми весами, которым требуется больше памяти, чем есть в одном настольном ПК или ИИ-системе. Разделение модели между машинами позволяет запускать более крупные нагрузки без переноса всей задачи в облако или создания серверного кластера. Совокупные GPU также вносят вклад в вычисления, хотя результат зависит от конкретных видеокарт, доступной памяти, пропускной способности и способности модели эффективно распределять работу.

Это предварительная версия для разработчиков, а не стандартная функция Windows. Для неё нужны совместимые сборки Windows, предварительные драйверы и поставщик NetworkDirect на каждом ПК. Компьютеры следует подключать напрямую в конфигурации «полная сеть»; последовательное соединение крайне не рекомендуется из-за резкого падения производительности.
Для двух ПК достаточно одного кабеля USB4 между ними. Для кластера из трёх систем потребуется два порта USB4 на каждом компьютере. Microsoft заявляет о поддержке портов 40 Гбит/с, а порты 80 Гбит/с (включая Thunderbolt 5) обеспечивают вдвое большую номинальную скорость соединения. Это скорости интерфейса, а не гарантированная пропускная способность приложений.
Есть и существенные ограничения по настройке и безопасности: инструкции требуют тестовой подписи, что влечёт отключение Secure Boot. Microsoft рекомендует использовать выделенные тестовые ПК, а не основные системы. Транспорт не переподключается автоматически при обрыве связи — приложениям нужно заново устанавливать соединение. Программное обеспечение экспериментальное и не должно рассматриваться как готовая функция ИИ для потребителей.
Анонс примечателен тем, что предлагает владельцам существующих ПК с USB4 собрать небольшой распределённый кластер. Однако технология не объединяет память физически так же, как единый чип с общей памятью, и не обещает линейного масштабирования производительности. На результаты повлияют задержка, пропускная способность передачи и программные накладные расходы. Тем не менее подход может дать энтузиастам и разработчикам более дешёвый способ тестировать более крупные локальные модели, объединяя уже имеющиеся машины.

ixkxai.title: UTA Hires Sam Yabrow As Talent Agent
ixkxai.content:
EXCLUSIVE: UTA has hired Sam Yabrow as a talent agent based in its Los Angeles office.

Yabrow joins from Buchwald, bringing nearly a decade of entertainment industry experience spanning casting and talent representation.

Clients expected to join him at UTA include Will Price (The Only Living Pickpocket in New York, The Chair Company), Igby Rigney (The Shards), Everett Blunck (The Plague, The Audacity) and Jaren Lewison (Eternally Yours).

Yabrow began his career in casting in New York before moving into talent representation at Abrams Artists Agency, later known as A3 Artists Agency. Following A3’s closure in 2024, he joined Buchwald, where he spent the past two and a half years. He relocated to Los Angeles earlier this year.

Originally from Georgia, Yabrow is a graduate of the University of Michigan.

bhnw3y.title: Украинские учебники сжигали. Экс-директор лицея в Олешках об оккупации
bhnw3y.content:
По случаю Всемирного дня ребенка, который отмечается 20 ноября, в Европарламенте состоялась дискуссия о нарушении прав украинских детей в условиях российской агрессии. Среди участников - бывшая директор Раденского лицея Олешковского городского совета Наталья Васильева, которая была свидетелем того, как российские оккупационные силы уничтожали систему украинского образования на захваченной части Херсонcкой области. О том, как это происходило, Наталья Васильева рассказала в интервью DW.

Deutsche Welle: Госпожа Васильева, когда после оккупации Олешек стало понятно, что россияне не просто захватили территорию, а пытаются установить контроль над украинским образованием?

Наталья Васильева: Буквально с первых дней захвата Олешек оккупационные власти занялись управлением образования. Они начали уверять педагогов в том, что российское образование лучше, что украинское образование не дает знаний нашим детям. И они хотят, чтобы мы открыли школы для детей и проводили обучение, но по российским стандартам.

Большинство учителей не перешли на сторону российских оккупантов, на работу никто не выходил, мы переходили на дистанционное обучение, и таким образом, поскольку у нас был интернет, работали с детьми и проводили занятия по украинским программам в режиме онлайн. Так продолжалось до лета 2022 года. Я как директор лицея ходила на работу, но потом они (представители оккупационных властей. - Ред.) приехали ко мне. Поскольку я не давала согласия на сотрудничество, у меня отобрали ключи от лицея и потом даже не разрешали заходить в помещение.

- Впоследствии школы все-таки открылись. Кто пришел туда работать?

- Школы открылись только тогда, когда оккупационные власти имели уже определенный состав людей, которые заменили украинских учителей, не согласившихся на сотрудничество. Хотя среди них было определенное количество тех учителей, которые предали свою родину. Но большинство - это были люди или вообще не причастные к системе образования, или привезенные из России.

- Что российские оккупанты сделали с украинскими учебниками и другими учебными материалами, которые оставались в школах?

- Все методические материалы они выбрасывали, уничтожали. Украинские учебники, украинский язык, литература, история Украины. Эти учебники практически сжигались. Из них устраивали так называемые "пионерские костры".

- Контролировали ли российские оккупанты, на каком языке общались дети?

- То, что дети должны были говорить по-русски, а общение на украинском не допускалось, было требованием, которое даже не обсуждалось. Поэтому дети должны были говорить по-русски, их заставлять учить и петь гимн России.

- Был ли в программе украинский язык как предмет?

- Я знаю, что позже был введен один час в неделю для предмета "Родная речь", это и был украинский язык. Что касается истории Украины, то она не преподавалась, потому что они сказали, что Украины как страны не существует, поэтому и истории Украины быть не может.

- Как готовили учителей для работы по российским образовательным программам?

- В нашей Олешковской общине они организовывали всех, кого пригласили на работу в школы, которые должны были открыть, и возили их на учебу в Краснодарский край и Крым, а потом они уже возвращались сюда, чтобы преподавать по российским стандартам.

- А как воспринимали дети это принудительное изменение образования?

- Для детей это было очень больно. Но ведь они не могут сопротивляться взрослым, тем более вооруженным. Школы были окружены российскими военными, и в учебное заведение пропускали только детей.

- Могли ли дети, остававшиеся в оккупации, продолжать обучение по украинской программе онлайн? Насколько это было доступно и безопасно?

- В то время и по сей день с интернетом довольно сложно, потому что украинского провайдера там нет с начала войны, а они своего провайдера не запустили так, как надо, поэтому со связью очень плохо. Нельзя связаться с людьми, чтобы, например, даже пообщаться. Так что с онлайн-занятиями было сложно и опасно. Родителей заставляли отдавать детей в школы, шантажировали, что иначе детей заберут в интернаты, будут штрафовать. Так что родители вынуждены были разрешать своим детям посещать школы, где преподавали по российским стандартам.

- Как вы думаете, какие последствия для детей будет иметь то, что их силой заставили кардинально изменить привычную для них образовательную среду?

- Для детей это, прежде всего, глубокая психологическая травма. Они до сих пор вспоминают эти события. А также это нарушение права ребенка знать традиции, культуру, историю своей страны, получать образование на том языке, на котором он хочет, в конце концов, права знать о своей идентичности, то, что ты - украинец. У ребенка забрали право свободно передвигаться по своей украинской земле. У них нет безопасного детства. Вот где можно купить, например, игрушки или детские книги? Куда можно поехать на оздоровление? Где тот кружок, в который ребенок привык ходить и заниматься любимым делом? Это все нарушено, просто нарушена вся жизнь.

- Что, по вашему мнению, нужно сделать сегодня, чтобы помочь детям, пережившим оккупацию? Возможно, чем-то могут помочь европейские партнеры?

- Думаю, нужно искать возможности договариваться о безопасных коридорах для эвакуации детей, которые остаются на временно оккупированных территориях. Если у зарубежных партнеров есть такая возможность, то приглашать вернувшихся с временно оккупированных территорий детей на оздоровление, чтобы дети могли как-то отвлечься от страшных событий, которые они пережили.

- Вы продолжаете сейчас преподавать?

- Нет, я уже не преподаю, а работаю детским психологом. Но три учебных заведения Олешковской общины функционируют дистанционно, и в них учатся дети, переехавшие на подконтрольную Украине территорию, или те, которые вместе с семьями выехали за границу. Они могут учиться со своими родными учителями. У них сохраняется хотя бы какое-то чувство коллектива, своего, родного, напоминающего о земле, где они родились.

8mxzql.title: Louis Garrel And Harry Lawtey Join Jeremy Allen White In Ben Stiller-Directed ‘Airman’ From Laika Live-Action And A24
8mxzql.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Louis Garrel and Harry Lawtey are set to join Jeremy Allen White in the Laika Live Action and A24 World War II survival thriller Airman directed by Ben Stiller.

Based on the New York Times bestseller The Lost Airman: A True Story of Escape from Nazi-Occupied France by Seth Meyerowitz, the film recounts the harrowing and remarkable untold story of Arthur Meyerowitz, who was shot down over Nazi-occupied France and evaded Gestapo pursuers for months before attempting a daring escape. The book was published in 2016 by Penguin.

The script is by Ben Shattuck and Stiller. Three-time Oscar winner Emmanuel Lubezki has been tapped as director of photography, Christian Goldbeck as production designer, Małgorzata Karpiuk as costume designer and Geoffrey Richman as editor.

Laika Live Action will lead production alongside A24, which will also handle domestic distribution and international sales. The film is a Le Grisbi Productions and Storyteller Productions production, in association with Red Hour Films and Nine Stories.

Stiller will produce for his Red Hour Films as will John Lesher for his Le Grisbi Productions, PJ van Sandwijk for his Storyteller Productions, Travis Knight and Matt Levin for Laika, and A24. Executive producers are Maryse Knight, Jeremy Kipp Walker and Zac Locke for Laika, Michael Lesslie and Marie Savare for Storyteller, Jake Gyllenhaal for Nine Stories and Miki Emmerich, Richard Whelan, Meyerowitz, Dan Bodansky and James Dixon. Gian Pablo Antonetti serves as co-producer for Le Grisbi.

“We’re thrilled to partner with A24, Ben and Jeremy on a film that embodies our commitment to bold, filmmaker-driven cinema,” said Matt Levin, Laika’s President of Live Action Film & Series. “Ben is an extraordinary talent with a singular creative vision, and we couldn’t be more excited to bring this incredible true story to life together.”

Stiller is represented by WME, VIE and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern. White is represented by WME. Garrel is represented by UTA and Agence Adequat. Lawtey is represented by CAA, B-Side and Goodman, Genow, Schenkman, Smelkinson & Christopher.

4hxn2a.title: The Best 2026 Games to Gift a Steam Deck Owner This Holiday Season - Steam Deck HQ
4hxn2a.content:
If you haven’t yet, follow us on X (Twitter), Mastodon, or Bluesky to know when we post new articles, and join our Reddit or Subscribe to us on YouTube to check out our content and interact with our awesome community. Thank you for supporting us!

The holidays are fast approaching, and you may be thinking about getting a new game to treat yourself, or you may be looking for some games to get for friends or family. So, I wanted to go over some games I recommend checking out, and who may enjoy them.

For this list, I am focusing on games that were released this year. There are a ton of great games to enjoy on the Steam Deck that have been released previously, but I want to focus on newer releases for this one.

Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game – For Fighting Game Fans (SDHQ Review)

Avatar Legends is a masterpiece. It takes everything that makes fighting games special and executes it at an incredibly high level, while remaining welcoming to newcomers through its outstanding tutorials and accessibility options. Combined with its breathtaking 100% hand-drawn visuals that perfectly capture the spirit of the animated series, it stands as one of the most impressive and memorable fighting games we’ve ever played.

Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse – For Metroidvania Fans (SDHQ Review)

Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse brings Castlevania back after a 12-year hiatus on an extremely high note. The peak level design and fluid combat elevate the experience even more than I remember from older games. Going with developer Evil Empire was the right choice for this kind of game, and I can easily blow off the minor issues and enjoy everything great this game has to offer.

You can get the game on Fanatical for $22.49 (25% Off) to save.

Dead as Disco – For Rhythm Game Fans (SDHQ Review)

What Dead as Disco already gets right is arguably the hardest part: it has a combat system that feels fantastic, and a musical backbone that elevates it beyond simple imitation. If you’ve ever loved the rhythm and flow of Arkham-style combat, this is a game that understands exactly why that worked – and then dares to remix it into something fresh.

Demon Tides – For Fans of 3D Platformers (SDHQ Review)

Demon Tides exceeded almost all of my expectations. The mechanics are tight and sound, with a great level of customization to modify our moveset in unique ways that cater to how we want to play. The open world and player-driven exploration make finding islands with platforming challenges more engaging, while the rewards for completing these were worthwhile and motivating. There are some minor issues here and there, but none of them take away from how well-built the game is.

Denshattack! – For Fans of Skateboarding Games (SDHQ Review)

Denshattack! surprised me in many ways. Its constant action, accessible mechanics, and vibrant, cinematic visuals create a magical experience that can’t be found regularly. Each stage offers something new, whether it be different objectives or completely different events that change how we play it out.

You can get it for $15.55 (22% Off) on Fanatical to save some money.

Dragon Quest VII Reimagined – For Fans of JRPGs (SDHQ Review)

Dragon Quest 7 Reimagined is a fantastic remake of the original that addresses many of its problems. The story has been streamlined with some great additions to make the other characters stand out more, while the combat has the accessibility settings and adjustments that the most recent games benefit from. It does feel a little too easy at times, which makes the strategic elements of battle feel less necessary, but it never fully detracts from the experience enough to regret playing.

You can get the game for $38.99 (35% Off) on Humble to save.

Esoteric Ebb – For Fans of CRPGs (SDHQ Review)

Esoteric Ebb is a tough game to pin down, but the closest I could describe it as is a CRPG with Visual Novel elements. A lot of burden is placed on the writing, and fortunately, the writing is really good. Almost all action is handled through the dialogue system, and the traditional CRPG mechanics work really well for conversations. As long as you can cope with the somewhat irritating combat mechanics and RNG, Esoteric Ebb is a fun time.

You can get the game for $21.99 (12% Off) to save some money.

Final Fantasy Resonance – For Fans of Octopath Traveler (SDHQ Review)

Final Fantasy Resonance brings Final Fantasy to the HD-2D style, and it ends up pushing what I thought this style could handle. The cinematic cutscenes elevate the fantastic story from Brave Exvius, with exceptional combat and interesting new ways to strategize. The minor nuisances from combat don’t impact the splendid experience that comes from the best HD-2D game I’ve played, and it has become one of my favorite Final Fantasy experiences.

Librarian: Tidy Up the Arcane Library! – For Fans of Casual Simulators

This is a simple game about putting the correct books away on a shelf one by one, and while it’s tedious, it’s also very calming. As we keep playing, we will get new magical powers to help us sort and put books away faster, and it becomes extremely satisfying as we complete row after row and upgrade our powers. It runs like a charm on the Steam Deck, and it’s just a treat.

Mouse: P.I. For Hire – For Fans of First-Person Shooters (SDHQ Review)

Mouse P.I. For Hire is a solid shooter with a beautiful aesthetic and interesting story, but the combat can feel a little too generic. The expressive rubber hose animation works, wonders, and the great cast help bring the characters to life in this mystery thriller, but I found it difficult to stay interested for longer periods of time because it didn’t have that spark that other big shooters have. Still, it’s a fantastic shooter nonetheless, and a perfect one to take on the go.

Onimusha: Way of the Sword – For Fans of Action RPGs (SDHQ Review)

Onimusha: Way of the Sword is an incredible Action RPG with combat that feels unmatched. The actual fighting just feels incredible between the slashing, parrying, and dodging; everything just clicks where it needs to and made me want to seek out grunts to kill just so I could get more. There are a few nuisances here and there, like with locking on, and the voice acting isn’t always the best, but the story and world are enjoyable to experience.

You can get it for $57.39 (18% Off) on Fanatical to save.

PRAGMATA – For Fans of Third-Person Shooters (SDHQ Review)

I don’t give out perfect scores lightly, and I mulled over this for some time, but there was almost no part of PRAGMATA I disliked. The story had emotional weight and surprised me with its twists, and the combination of puzzle and action in real time made fights engaging, and the temporary weapons continually made combat feel dynamic. The simple progression was enjoyable, and I felt that every single collectible I could find held meaning that made me more powerful. This is a must-have game.

You can get the game for $47.99 (20% Off) on Humble to save.

Queen’s Domain – For Fans of RPGs

Resident Evil Requiem – For Fans of Survival Horror (SDHQ Review)

Resident Evil Requiem finds a way to bring the newer and older gameplay styles that have defined the franchise into an exceptionally enjoyable experience that is perfect for fans of the series. The meshing of Grace’s slower, stealthier gameplay with Leon’s action-packed killing works wonderfully, giving us the best of both worlds.

You can get it for $48.99 (30% Off) on Humble to save some money.

TAMASHIKA – For Fans of First-Person Shooters (SDHQ Review)

TAMASHIKA is a weird, fast-paced FPS that doesn’t need an overwhelming amount of content to prove its worth. The balance of visual craziness and audio cues turns each run into a skill-driven rush to kill every enemy on screen and get to the end of the level as fast as possible. And with how tight the core mechanics are, it’s hard not to love every second of it. The game is extremely small, and I mean, only one small, procedurally-generated level, but I still couldn’t stop myself from playing that same level over and over until the next day came and I could try a completely new level to top the leaderboard.

Warhammer Survivors – For Fans of Vampire Survivors (SDHQ Review)

Despite similarities to the game that defined its genre, Warhammer Survivors found its own identity. The Warhammer references throughout the game are exciting, and fans of the series will fall in love. And no matter how simple and repetitive the gameplay loop is, it’s always exciting and never gets old.

And those are the games I recommend checking out! All of them are awesome for one reason or another, and we loved them when we reviewed them. I’m sure there are a ton of great deals to find over the next few weeks, and there will be sales for sure, but I would look at these games and consider them no matter what.

If you enjoyed this article, check out the rest of the content on SteamDeckHQ! We have a wide variety of game reviews and news that are sure to help your gaming experience. Whether you’re looking for news, tips and tutorials, game settings and reviews, or just want to stay up-to-date on the latest trends, we’ve got your back.

58z0ll.title: Hackers use autonomous AI tool Cairn to find zero-day, take over server
58z0ll.content:
Hackers used an autonomous AI agent platform called "Cairn" to discover a zero-day vulnerability in a medical imaging application and exploit it to take complete control of a server.

According to Amazon Threat Intelligence, the suspected Chinese-linked attackers simply instructed the AI agents to "obtain shell access," leaving them to independently discover and exploit the flaw.

Amazon Threat Intelligence uncovered the campaign after discovering that the attackers had left their Cairn instance publicly accessible without authentication, exposing their hacking operations.

According to the researchers, the attacks were launched by a Chinese-nexus threat actor between September 8 and 10, 2026, targeting mainly East Asian educational institutions outside China.

Cairn is a legitimate pentesting tool that can be used to coordinate multiple AI agents in cyber-operations, created for research and defense strengthening.

Gambit Security documented cases of Cairn abuse as part of a large-scale credit card stealing operation in September. More recently, Google reported it was deployed in an attack against an aerospace organization in the U.S.

During the campaign investigated by Amazon, the AI agents were not always successful. For example, a 16-hour and 148-action effort to take control of a Redis server failed.

In a separate case targeting a university GPU server, the agents tried over 30,000 credential combinations over six hours but failed to brute-force their way in.

Finding and using a zero-day

According to Amazon, Cairn's AI agents found a path traversal zero-day in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging application that uses AI to help researchers label medical images.

The flaw enabled the agents to write files to arbitrary locations on the server, and within 11 minutes, they went from mapping the application's API to exploiting the vulnerability.

In a subsequent session, the AI agents used the flaw to write a Python reverse shell to the sitecustomize.py file that automatically loads when Python starts, then triggered an API endpoint to establish root access to the server.

After discovering the zero-day, the operator provided the agents with a proxy into a second university network running the same vulnerable software and directed them to target other machines.

Amazon reported the flaw to MONAI Label maintainers, and they released a security update to address it on November 18.

The researchers attributed the campaign to a Chinese-nexus threat actor with moderate confidence, based on the language of the retrieved prompts, the activity timestamps, and the choice of targets.

Amazon also shared two IP addresses associated with the campaign, observed between September 8 and 10, 2026:

142[.]4.98.145
142[.]4.107.34

Amazon warned that AI agents can find and exploit vulnerabilities faster than security teams can react, urging organizations to rely more on automated defenses rather than manual investigations.

1jihmpt.title: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang accused of decades of bullying and workplace abuse in new investigation
1jihmpt.content:
Public humiliation reportedly considered a "rite of passage".

Image credit: Nvidia

An investigation into the workplace behavior of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who resigned recently after a series of extramarital affairs came to light, has uncovered decades of harassment, verbal employee abuse and "cultish" behaviour at the company which has long played a major role in PC gaming.
Following Huang's departure, The New York Times has published a report in which "more than a dozen" current and former Nvidia employees discussed their experiences with the former CEO. Speaking on conditions of anonymity, employees alleged Jensen Huang would verbally berate them, reportedly going as far as to say he'd rip their arms off, rip their heart out and stomp on it, or rip their head off and "pee on your brain".

Nvidia faced backlash this year when it revealed the generative AI-powered DLSS 5.Watch on YouTube

The report includes numerous examples of Huang's alleged abusive behaviour, which apparently stretches back years before Nvidia became the one of the most valuable companies in the world - years before the AI boom. It's claimed Huang on one occasion went around a room of managers telling them he'd kill them. Then, when he reached a person in their 70s, said everyone hoped they'd drop dead.Huang allegedly referred to these bouts of public humiliation as a "rite of passage" at Nvidia, when questioned by an internal HR employee whom he later fired for not being a "right fit". Huan's stance was apparently to test whether a person could handle the culture there, which is described in the report as "cultish".
It's claimed Huang's influence at Nvidia has meant other senior managers have followed his lead, including his daughter Madison, Nvidia's chief of staff, who it's said often yells at staff, including executives more highly ranked than her.
A spokesperson for Huang denied the allegations in response to a request for comment by the New York Times. The spokesperson, John Fisher, said the claims in the report were "fabrications that are now impossible to disprove specifically, and the thousands of Nvidia employees who continue to speak out for Jensen show they’re false".
Huang resigned from his role as Nvidia CEO earlier this month after a series of extramarital affairs were unearthed - one with a person US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy, and two others with Nvidia employees. The chair of Nvidia's board, Harvey C. Jones, reportedly said earlier this week that the company "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".

1sw2ref.title: Golden Globes Category Chaos: When ‘The Drama’ Is a Comedy…
1sw2ref.content:
The Drama is a comedy — or so say the backers of the film, about an engaged couple’s darkest secrets, in their submission for the Golden Globes, which requires all films be entered as either A) a drama or B) a musical or a comedy. And that’s not even one of this year’s more questionable submissions.

Other comedy entries include I Play Rocky, about the making of Rocky (which competed at the Globes as a drama); Obsession, about a young woman’s loss of agency; Tender Loving Care, about the frustrations of two young women, including the decline of one’s father; Artificial, about AI growing out of control; and Project Hail Mary, about a man sent into space against his will to try to stave off the end of the world. Meanwhile, Club Kid, about a man-child who ends up with a child — widely described as an elevated version of Adam Sandler’s comedy Big Daddy — has been entered as a drama.

Yes, all of the aforementioned musical/comedy submissions have moments of laughter and all of the dramas have elements of drama — but still, these classifications are pretty eyebrow-raising, begging the questions: What is going on? And is there a better way?

***

The first Globes were held in 1944. There were no genre-specific Globes categories until the eighth, when the lead acting categories were split into two, one for dramas, the other for musicals/comedies. The following year, the same split was implemented for best picture. That category was reunified for the 11th ceremony, but the split was brought back for the 12th and every year since, helping to attract more stars to the ceremony.

Until 2023, Globes category submissions were made by studios and reviewed by the HFPA’s reminders list committee, which rarely overturned anything, even as dramas with music passed as musicals (Ray, Walk the Line and Rocketman), dramas with few laughs passed as comedies (Ghost, The Tourist and My Week With Marilyn) and comedies passed as dramas (All About Eve, Born Yesterday, Harvey and Sunset Boulevard — all in the same year). Once in a blue moon, the committee would reject a submission (Promising Young Woman as a musical/comedy), but it usually deferred to studios’ preferences.

Frustrations burst into the open in 2015 after The Martian, a film about an astronaut stranded on Mars, was submitted and accepted as a musical/comedy. Judd Apatow, whose comedy Trainwreck was in contention that year, tweeted, “Trying to dominate the comedy category when you are really a drama afraid of dramatic competition is a punk move.” The Martian ended up beating Trainwreck for best picture, something Apatow was still smarting over when he presented at this year’s Globes: “My film Trainwreck lost best comedy to Ridley Scott’s The Martian. You know Ridley Scott, America’s favorite comedy director — director of such hilarious comedies as Gladiator, Blade Runner and Alien? I can’t wait till later tonight when best comedy is won by Hamnet.”

But ownership of the Globes had changed in 2023 (the Globes now share the same owners as THR), resulting in widespread reforms. This year’s rules declare: “Motion pictures shall be entered in the category that best matches the overall intent, tone and content of the film. Therefore, a motion picture that is primarily intended to have a serious or dramatic tone but contains comedic overtones or elements shall be entered as a drama as opposed to a comedy. Likewise, a motion picture that is primarily intended to have a comedic or satirical tone but contains dramatic overtones or elements shall be entered as a comedy as opposed to a drama.”

Once the film submission period ends (Nov. 24 this year), an eligibility committee comprising current Globes voters (the quantity and names are kept private) evaluates every submission for “potential misclassification issues.” If found, they “may contact the studio … to discuss those issues and to resolve them informally.” Eventually, the eligibility committee meets with a review committee to discuss any outstanding concerns, and those committees — or at least members of them who have seen a film in question — vote to determine if a change is necessary; two-thirds must favor a change for one to occur.

***

The Drama, starring Robert Pattinson and Zendaya, was submitted in the musical/comedy category for this year’s Golden Globes.

Courtesy of A24

Why do people try to game the Globes categories? Because the nationally telecast Globes ceremony provides the biggest spotlight for awards contenders before Oscar nominations voting (the 2027 Globes will take place Jan. 10, and Oscar nomination voting starts the next morning), making it highly valuable for a film or individual to be represented at the ceremony as a nominee or, better still, a winner.

There usually are fewer standout musicals and comedies than dramas, meaning it’s often easier to land a nom or win if a drama can pass as a musical/comedy. (This year’s aforementioned musical/comedy submissions surely wanted to get out of the way of The Odyssey.) Another motivation: Studios with multiple films prefer to not have them pitted against one another. (A24 probably wants Club Kid to compete as a drama because it already has The Invite and The Debut up for best musical/comedy, just as Neon probably wants Artificial to compete as a comedy because it already has All of a Sudden, Fjord and Paper Tiger up for best drama.)

It remains to be seen whether the Globes’ eligibility committee will overturn some of this year’s submissions. (Reports suggest it already rejected Michael as a musical/comedy.)

Moving forward, it would make everyone’s life easier if the Globes consolidated its genre-specific categories — picture, actor and actress — into single categories with 12 slots rather than divided categories with six each. Or, if the Globes prefers to continue to have multiple categories for each in order to yield twice as many winners, it might consider retaining the “drama” label for one but changing the other to “genre,” which would better describe recent musical/comedy nominees like Poor Things, The Substance and Bugonia.

This story appeared in the Nov. 18 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine. Click here to subscribe.

h9upqu.title: Том Харди, Пирс Броснан и Хелен Миррен приступили к съемкам в третьем сезоне "Гангстерленда"
h9upqu.content:
Как сообщает издание Variety, в Великобритании официально началось производство третьего сезона сериала «Гангстерленд» (MobLand). К своим ролям вернулись исполнители главных ролей: Том Харди, Пирс Броснан и Хелен Миррен.
Том Харди вновь воплотит образ Гарри да Соузы — опытного посредника («решалы»), работающего в криминальном мире. Ранее в этом году в СМИ появлялись сообщения о возможном уходе актера из проекта на фоне творческих разногласий с продюсером Дэвидом Глассером и сценаристом Джезом Баттеруортом. Источники утверждали, что Харди якобы опаздывал на съемочную площадку и настаивал на правках в сценарии. Однако режиссер Гай Ричи и руководство Paramount Studios были заинтересованы в сохранении актера в основном составе, и вскоре сторонам удалось урегулировать конфликт.
Хелен Миррен и Пирс Броснан вернутся к ролям Мейв и Конрада Харриганов — глав криминального клана, вокруг которого строится сюжет сериала.
Помимо них, в новом сезоне снимаются Пэдди Консидайн, Джоанн Фроггатт, Лара Пулвер и Тоби Джонс.

16hd8di.title: Dispatches from O'Reilly: Inside a software factory
16hd8di.content: [Ed. note: This article was originally published on O’Reilly Media’s blog, Radar. Republished with permission.]—————————-As a software engineer with more than seven years of experience before the coding-agent era, I never liked the idea of vibe coding. But I knew there was a clear line between it and using coding agents to generate clean, maintainable code. That line, where good software principles meet coding agents, is defined by software factories.That’s why, three months ago, I built my own software factory, Squid, to ship all of Decoding AI’s small and medium projects with minimal human intervention. The first version was so overbuilt I stopped using it.Meanwhile, I kept seeing people obsess over the next “_____ engineering” label, instead of focusing on actionable outcomes. Prompt engineering, then context engineering, then harness engineering. So far, so good. But in the last few weeks (July 2026 as I write this), things got off track with loop engineering and graph engineering, which already read more like marketing talk than like anything that solves real problems. Graph engineering overtheorizes how teams have built AI applications since the LangGraph era kicked off in ~2024. Don’t get me wrong. The terms aren’t wrong (Boris Cherny, who leads Claude Code at Anthropic, says, “My job is to write loops”), but we’re overexplaining intuitive things we started doing years ago.While you’re defining what counts as a loop, you’re not thinking about the processes that actually deliver software.The right frame is the software factory, which was one of the core themes at AI Engineer World’s Fair 2026, where Tereza Tížková (growth at Factory.ai) defined one as “the whole loop, the whole lifecycle of developing software with autonomy.”I bet you already have an intuitive sense of what a software factory is. In this article, I want to further formalize it and map it onto the software development lifecycle (SDLC). We’ll explore how big your software factory should be, and when to stop automating before it adds more friction than value. Most importantly, I want to highlight where the human belongs in this process, and where I believe they’ll still belong even in a world where all the code is generated by AI.So…what’s worth automating? Where does the human bring the most value? What’s worth building, and what’s worth buying?Like a physical factory, a software factory automates software creation with minimal human input. Raw work (bug reports, feature ideas, incidents) goes in. Shipped software comes out. It needs a few highly qualified people making high-leverage decisions, and defined gates that work can’t pass through without them.Factory.ai pitches “a self-improving system for your Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC).” Addy Osmani frames the stack as loop, harness, factory: “The loop is the atom”; a factory is “an org chart made of loops.” Warp’s CEO, Zach Lloyd, states that “software engineering will become factory engineering.”The software factory line. Eight stages over one shared context layer, with production signals looping back as new tasks.The factory is made up of eight stages that can be divided into three buckets:What to build. Triage/intake classifies, deduplicates, and routes incoming work. Brainstorming finds high-impact features through market analysis, user data, and technical research. Planning, the most important stage, turns that research into a polished plan, refines it by letting the agent grill you, and tracks decisions in an ADR (Architecture Decision Record) log plus a glossary. The outputs of this stage are tickets backed by documentation that a team of agents can implement, which can be tracked in plain files or a project management tool, such as GitHub Issues, Linear, or Notion.At this stage, the agent plans in read-only mode, going through the code, the AGENTS.md file, and most importantly the context layer.Actual building and checking. Implementing is a software engineer and QA agent loop that goes through the tasks and supporting documentation. Review checks the PR diff against product, architecture, and code standards. Review-CI runs the test suite, and failures trigger a fixing agent. Release handles CD to staging/production with human deployment checks.Self-improving. Monitor/incident response feeds production signals (alerts, errors, incidents) back into triage as fresh input on what to build next, closing the loop.Orthogonal to the eight stages, we have the context layer. The layer is especially important at the front of the line. Brainstorming is limited to the data it sees: user analytics, competitor analysis, research, transcripts, and documentation. At this stage, a poor context layer directly limits the space of possibilities you can explore. It has a similar impact on planning, where transforming the raw idea into technical specs and tasks depends heavily on how good the examples in the context layer are. If you want to implement a new product-recommendation feature, and you have zero examples, the LLM will just predict the most common thing to do, which often isn’t the best solution for your product.The context layer can take many forms. One strategy that is becoming increasingly popular is the LLM Wiki, a term coined by Andrej Karpathy. It’s basically a strategy to transform your data into a structured knowledge base, just by using files, instead of a database. Factory, via its AutoWiki feature, transforms popular codebases into a structured knowledge base that agents can query instead of parsing the codebase itself. LangChain recently released OpenWiki, a CLI tool to manage wikis for agent memory. If you’re curious, in this article I detail how I turn my data from Obsidian, Readwise, and Google Drive into agent memory via LLM wikis.To see where the human belongs, let’s walk through the factory with an end-to-end example. We’ll build a feature for a shopping-assistant agent on an ecommerce platform similar to Amazon’s. The scenario is that usage data says users aren’t engaging with its recommendations, and we have to ship an improvement.Brainstorm is where taste lives. Agents do the grunt work: They analyze user activity, scan competitors’ assistants, and pull research into the knowledge base. Then a member of the technical staff starts looking at the data, understands why people are not engaging with the recommendations, explores how the competition implements their solution, and proposes a fix as a feature spec. At this stage, the spec solves a business problem. It doesn’t need to prescribe a technical solution yet.Plan is where a human, with the help of the software factory, transforms the feature spec into an implementation plan. Let’s assume that we want to make a change to the recommender engine algorithm. The human chats with the knowledge base, figures out whether it’s feasible, and thinks through architecture, interfaces, data flow, cost, and latency. They then let the agent scan the codebase and grill them until the plan is properly refined into something that fits the codebase. The output is a bunch of tickets plus an ADR explaining the algorithm change and an update to the glossary.The agent can help within these two stages by quickly scanning through a ton of data and improving the plan, but the human is still central.Use the strongest model (Fable) for brainstorming and planning. These stages burn fewer tokens than implementation itself, but everything downstream depends on them. A well-written plan lets cheaper models (Opus, Sonnet) execute without reasoning their way out of dead ends. A weak plan makes them retry until the extra tokens erase the price gap.With a weak plan, I’ve watched Sonnet on high reasoning out-cost Opus on the same task: The smaller model needs more attempts to reach the same goal. Total cost is tokens × price, not model tier. So more failures equals more reasoning, more tokens, and more cost.From here on, we move into “loop” and “graph” engineering territory.A strong planning session makes cheap executors actually cheap, while a weak plan makes them expensive.Implement runs a software engineer agent that picks up every ticket that’s ready to go. As the loop is scoped to a feature, it takes only the associated tickets. After each ticket is implemented, a QA agent tries to find bugs by stress-testing the application. As agents tend to have a positive bias towards their own work, the split between the software engineer and QA agents matters. As Addy Osmani puts it, the model that wrote the code is “way too nice grading its own homework.” This loop, at solo scale, can be as simple as a bunch of terminals pulling tickets. At larger scale, it runs on remote agents working 24/7.The loop only works if agents can interact with the app. The QA agent needs one command that starts the whole stack reproducibly. From there, it drives the app in the browser, calls the data or fine-tuning pipelines, or hits your server’s API. Whatever your app’s interface is, the agent needs access to it, the same way a human user would.The key idea is to integrate feedback loops as natively as possible into your software factory. Ideally, you want multiple levels, depending on how expensive it is to run them: linting, unit tests, integration tests, and end-to-end tests. When the loop keeps failing, the root cause is almost always missing plumbing, not the agents.Review has three steps. Step one checks the product and architecture requirements against the ticket and the ADR. Any discrepancy becomes a new ticket passed back to the implement loop. Step two ensures code quality (modularity, naming) and guards against AI slop such as verbose comments or cryptic function names. Step three looks at the CI/CD pipeline. At every step, any failure auto-creates a task picked up by the software agent.Not every project needs all three steps. The “factory” ends with a PR that you as a human need to review and merge. But in reality, if you spend enough time creating a strong plan, the PR that reaches you is usually ready to ship as-is.The dynamics between what humans and agents own in the software factory line.So where does the human belong? You’re indispensable during brainstorming and planning, and you return for the final check. Agents own everything in between. OpenAI took this to the extreme: ~1M lines and ~1,500 merged PRs over five months with zero hand-written lines. Their framing is “Humans steer. Agents execute.”With my first Squid version (my own software factory), I got greedy and chased full autonomy: big remote workflows, parallel agents, and one grand pipeline running end to end. It worked, until something went off script. Which it usually does. I couldn’t debug it, couldn’t halt it mid-run, and couldn’t redirect it without throwing the run away. It was a big monolith that took me too far out of the loop, and I couldn’t control it.I realized you need two options. The first is granular commands that let you grill your plan, implement a specific task, or review one particular step. The second, for when you’re comfortable giving the agent 24/7 autonomy, is an end-to-end command that chains all the smaller ones into a fully autonomous graph, such as one big /plan and /implement-review-all command. Basically, each step is a “loop,” while the whole pipeline is the “graph” of your software factory. Still, note how planning and the rest are split into two different commands, as planning is, and always will be, human-driven (at least if you want the result to stay aligned with what you actually want).Bottom line. You need to be able to step in, halt it, redirect it, and interrupt it, while still having the option to go fully autonomous.The bottleneck is me, and that’s by design. To be honest, I’ve worked mostly solo since the AI coding agent boom, and I don’t understand who the people shipping 100 features in parallel are. Most of my features (per project) build on one another, which makes them impossible to parallelize. As the project grows, you can find more and more independent features that can be implemented in parallel, but I still believe that number is limited.That’s why, when I parallelize, I only use local agents, each running in an isolated codebase via work trees. So far, I’ve never felt the need for 24/7 remote agents, or wanted the overhead of managing them.A big team can justify more automation, but it has to earn it. So as with any other software product, start small, start by automating the most time-consuming bottlenecks, and add complexity gradually as people get comfortable with the system. Don’t be like me, with my Squid experiment.In all scenarios, you’ll start with a prebuilt coding harness. The most popular vendor-locked ones are Claude Code and Codex. Or go open source with OpenCode or Pi, which took off thanks to its minimalist, extensible architecture that lets you easily build on top of it.But picking a harness isn’t the same as knowing how to configure it and wire it into your software factory. That’s why everyone needs to know, at least intuitively, how a coding agent works under the hood: the agent loop running in your terminal, what changes when it runs remotely, how you evaluate it, and which context engineering strategies keep it cheap without making it dumber. If you want to learn more about building a coding agent from scratch, consider exploring my open source course on GitHub. Even if you never plan to build your own harness, that intuition is what lets you become a power user.For a small team, you’ll get extremely far just by defining a set of skills and agents that encode your process on top of the coding harness (a.k.a. your software factory). To keep it simple, this is what I did with Squid, which I use to implement all my projects.There are other off-the-shelf “software factories” powered just by skills and agents defined in .md files, such as Matt Pocock’s skills repository or the BMad method.But remember that the factory is mostly about processes, not tools: A factory that doesn’t fit how your team already works adds friction, never gets adopted, and ends up useless.You cross the buy line the moment engineers you don’t personally supervise run agents. Observability, tracing, cost tracking, and pay-per-token billing stop being optional and become someone’s full-time job. Agent swarms wired into Linear, Slack, and CI across distributed infrastructure are a logistical hell that isn’t your product. That’s when it makes sense to look into off-the-shelf solutions such as Factory.ai (that comes with the Droid agent), or Warp’s Oz. In Warp CEO Zach Lloyd’s words, “Most of the factory is not necessarily a new interface. It is an integration into people’s existing workflows.”At the other end of the spectrum, you cross back to building when the platform’s constraints cost more than the team it would take to replace it, as OpenAI’s report on its Codex-built product shows.The smallest builds, the middle buys, and the largest builds again.Someone is already coining next quarter’s “_____ engineering” term as we speak. But the software engineering processes you use to output real code won’t change that often. That’s why you should be open-minded but at the same time focus on actionable outcomes, not on overthinking how to label things.As Zach Lloyd suggests: Find one “annoying part of your job” and build the smallest loop that handles it.The harsh reality is that software factories are just at the beginning. They’re far from perfect, and especially far from being fully “autonomous.” Usually, when someone claims they’ve cracked the software factory problem, they either haven’t tested the idea enough or are trying to sell it to you. I’m confident we’ll reach the point where almost the entire software development lifecycle is automated (with the exception of brainstorming and planning), but at the moment we’re still figuring things out.But here’s what I’m wondering:Which stage of your factory still needs you the most? 17g04i0.title: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Hunts Down $21M in Box Office Previews
17g04i0.content:
Logo text

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is ready for battle in its opening weekend at the box office.

The sixth film in the Lionsgate franchise grossed $21 million in Thursday previews before hitting 4,018 North American theaters on Friday. This gives it the second-best previews figure for the franchise, behind only the $25.2 million that 2013’s The Hunger Games: Catching Fire collected and besting the $19.7 million that the original Jennifer Lawrence-led film The Hunger Games earned when launching the franchise in 2012. The first Hunger Games went on to gross $152.5 million domestically in its debut frame, while Catching Fire holds the top-grossing launch in the series by opening with $158.1 million.

Lionsgate had projected The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping to gross north of $80 million, but other sources expected that it would open much higher and potentially earn between $100 million and $130 million, which now appears the more likely outcome. Adapting author Suzanne Collins’ prequel novel that was published last year, director Francis Lawrence‘s movie carries a production budget of roughly $150 million as it revitalizes the franchise in telling a story set 24 years before the events of the original 2008 book.

In the new film, Joseph Zada stars Haymitch Abernathy, providing the backstory for the character whom Woody Harrelson brought to life in the first four movies. The cast for Sunrise on the Reaping also includes Mckenna Grace, Whitney Peak, Jesse Plemons, Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, Elle Fanning, Kieran Culkin and Maya Hawke.

Elle Fanning in The Hunger Games: The Sunrise on the Reaping.

Courtesy of Lionsgate

The Hunger Games franchise’s five films have surpassed $3.3 billion at the global box office, with the series coming off of its lowest-performing entry with 2023 prequel The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes. Starring Tom Blyth, Rachel Zegler and Hunter Schafer, that one disappointed in opening to $44 million domestically before ending its run with $166.4 million domestically and a global sum of $361.8 million.

Sunrise on the Reaping holds a 67 critical score on Rotten Tomatoes as it lags behind the franchise’s first four movies but bests the 64 percent approval for Songbirds & Snakes. In his THR review, chief film critic David Rooney wrote that the new film “delivers on emotion and brutal spectacle.”

The weekend’s competition includes Amazon MGM Studios’ I Play Rocky going wide after two frames in limited release for Peter Farrelly’s origin story of the 1976 Oscar-winning Rocky. Also fighting for attention spans this weekend is the highly anticipated video game Grand Theft Auto 6, which launched Thursday after a 13-year wait since the franchise’s last title.

f6s7wg.title: The 10 Coolest Cars We Saw at the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show
f6s7wg.content: Tesla RoadsterEric Stafford|Car and DriverIt’s one thing to see the Tesla Roadster through your smartphone screen; it’s another thing to see it about six feet away. While we’re highly skeptical that Tesla will ever publicly sell the thruster-equipped version that flew through the air and did a barrel roll, it’s more likely that a similar-looking, street-legal version will eventually reach production. Haters gonna hate, but the Roadster looks pretty damn cool, like Lamborghini designer Fabrizio Giugiaro was hired to style his version of the Lotus Esprit S1 that James Bond drove in The Spy Who Loved Me. Consider us shaken, not stirred.Read the Reveal StoryWidebody Bugatti EB110Eric Stafford|Car and DriverBeing in the same room as a Bugatti EB110 is about as common as being in the same room as Sir Anthony Hopkins. Like meeting the actor who famously played Hannibal Lecter, meeting one of the most iconic supercars ever made is unnerving. Now, you may have noticed that this example isn’t exactly all original; instead, it has been modified by Phiaro Inc., and it features a custom widebody kit as well as a chameleon-like paint job. The best part? Its modifications are completely reversible. Let’s just say it drew a crowd.Read Our Original ReviewAdvertisement - Continue Reading BelowGenesis GV90 NeolunEric Stafford|Car and DriverGenesis is going after the throats of luxury stalwarts like BMW, Mercedes-Benz and—dare we say—Bentley with the new GV90. The one you see here is the top-of-the-line Neolun model, and its most distinctive feature is these gigantic coach doors. Inside are four VIP-grade seats that treat passengers to an opulent cabin awash in rich materials and front seats that swivel 180 degrees to create a mobile lounge (this configuration is only accessible when the 657-hp EV is parked). The GV90 Neolun also has a veneer wood floor and 24-inch wheels that remind us of the iconic monoblock wheels made famous by Mercedes-AMG and Brabus. Few SUVs turn our heads, but Genesis appears to have another game-changer on its metaphorical hands.Read the Reveal StoryToyota Crown Signia GT-S ConceptEric Stafford|Car and DriverWe spotted this beautiful wagon-like Toyota Crown Signia from across the convention center’s south hall. Among a sea of generic crossovers, this low-slung longroof is an ode to an age when most Americans didn’t lust after the elevated seating position of a semi-truck. Of course, if you haven’t noticed, this isn’t exactly a production-spec Crown Signia. If you read our recent SEMA coverage, you may recognize it as the GT-S concept. Along with being lowered by five inches and wearing flared fenders that resemble the Mustang GTD, it has custom one-off coil-over dampers, 21-inch HRE wheels, and brakes from a Lexus RX500h F Sport. To all that, we say, “Hell yeah, brother!”Read More About ItAdvertisement - Continue Reading BelowHyundai ElantraEric Stafford|Car and DriverLet’s take a break from the world of flying cars, Bugattis, and fanciful electric SUVs to enjoy something that most people can afford: the new eighth-generation Hyundai Elantra. If its disorienting front lighting, heavily creased bodywork, and broad haunches intimidate you, we’re sure there’s a safer-looking alternative in Toyota’s showroom. But whatever you may think about the new Elantra’s styling, it definitely attracts attention. And Hyundai is hoping it’ll do just that to new customers who are looking to join the brand’s family tree. The nonhybrid version seen here draws power from a humble 147-hp four-cylinder engine, but the lineup will add a more powerful hybrid model sometime next year. While pricing is still TBD, we expect that it’ll cost around $25,000 to own the most interesting car in your cul-de-sac.Read the Reveal StoryRam 1500 Rumble Bee Foose EditionEric Stafford|Car and DriverIf you’ve ever watched an episode of Overhaulin’, a TV show that lasted for 10 seasons on TLC, then you’ve heard of custom car designer Chip Foose. Now, he has teamed up with Fox Factory Vehicles to create this even more muscular version of the new Ram 1500 Rumble Bee street truck. Along with unique wheels and body graphics, the interior has been restyled with diamond-stitched seats and Foose branding. The truck itself has a lowered ride height with an aftermarket coil-over suspension, and its supercharged V-8 is available with either 705 or 1000 horsepower. That’s a lot of horsies, and they’ll cost customers a lot of cash, with the Rumble Bee Foose Edition starting at $154,990.Read More About ItAdvertisement - Continue Reading BelowAcura Nexera ConceptEric Stafford|Car and DriverThis was one of the few concept cars at the show, but the Acura Nexera was first revealed back in August during Monterey Car Week. Still, the futuristic concept is really cool to see in person, especially with its dramatic glass canopy. Plus, how many times have you seen an Acura with butterfly doors? While the Nexera doesn’t preview an upcoming production model, it does provide a glimpse of Acura’s next-generation design language. Will the new 2028 RDX feature an active rear spoiler, carbon-fiber accents, and lighting that glows through the bodywork? Probably not. However, we can expect to see some of the Nexera concept’s interesting styling influence the brand’s next-gen compact SUV.Read the Reveal StoryAcura Integra Type S Heritage EditionEric Stafford|Car and DriverIf you’re old enough to remember Acura’s legendary DC2 Integra Type R, you’ll definitely appreciate this new Integra Type S Heritage Edition. Not only does its Blazing Phoenix Yellow call more attention to itself than Big Bird starring in an old-timey picture show, but it also honors the OG Type R, which also wore a shade of Phoenix Yellow. The modern-day throwback sport compact packs the same 320-hp turbo four and six-speed manual as other models, but this one alone has copper-colored wheels and a titanium shift knob from the Honda Civic Type R. To get one in your driveway, you’ll need to be lucky enough to score one of the 700 limited copies for the U.S. market, but the asking price is a reasonable $58,995.Read More About ItAdvertisement - Continue Reading BelowDodge Charger Super BeeEric Stafford|Car and DriverHave you been waiting for Dodge to stuff a Hemi V-8 in the new Charger? Well, you’re going to have to keep waiting for a while. However, if you’ve been hoping that the Brotherhood of Muscle will make a gas-powered Charger that’s set up for quick lap times, the new Super Bee variant should help you scratch that itch. Along with exclusive aero bits, stronger brakes, and wider summer tires, this track-focused Charger features an enhanced high-output Hurricane twin-turbo 3.0-liter straight-six, which is good for 600 horsepower (50 more than normal). The reimagined “Super Bee” logo on the rear quarter panel is one way to separate it from its siblings, but it also has an entirely different front clip that features new headlights and more open space to inhale engine-cooling air. If you’re wondering how much it costs, so are we, so stay tuned.Read the Reveal StoryChevy Silverado 1500 ZR2Eric Stafford|Car and DriverLike many of you, this was our first time seeing the new Chevy Silverado 1500’s new off-road-focused ZR2 variant. It’s a big truck, so big that we initially thought it was the HD version. Among the many changes to the newest generation of Chevy’s bestselling full-size pickup truck are all-new small-block V-8s. The ZR2 seen here is powered by a 481-hp 6.6-liter that helps churn massive all-terrain tires, which now stand 35 inches tall for the first time on a half-ton Silverado. The Ford F-150 Raptor-rivaling ZR2’s other party tricks include trick Multimatic DSSV spool-valve dampers. Inside, it includes GM’s first use of forged carbon fiber (neat!). If you want the most badass version, you’ll want to opt for the Bison Edition that adds beadlock-capable wheels, unique bumpers, and even more underbody armor. The cost of admission for the regular ZR2 is just under $80K, while the Bison starts even higher.Read the Reveal Story Eric Stafford’s automobile addiction began before he could walk, and it has fueled his passion to write news, reviews, and more for Car and Driver since 2016. His aspiration growing up was to become a millionaire with a Jay Leno–like car collection. Apparently, getting rich is harder than social-media influencers make it seem, so he avoided financial success entirely to become an automotive journalist and drive new cars for a living. After earning a journalism degree at Central Michigan University and working at a daily newspaper, the years of basically burning money on failed project cars and lemon-flavored jalopies finally paid off when Car and Driver hired him. His garage currently includes a 2010 Acura RDX, a manual '97 Chevy Camaro Z/28, and a '90 Honda CRX Si.

1ug7lj7.title: Бренд Volga пересмотрел цены на две из трех своих моделей
1ug7lj7.content: Возрожденная марка Volga переписала прайс-листы на две из трех своих моделей. Седан C50 и кроссовер K40 прибавили в стоимости, а флагман K50 пока держится в прежних рамках.Первым движение цен заметил «Автостат»: аналитики изучили сайты официальных дистрибьюторов бренда. Сопоставив старые и новые прайсы, «Рамблер/авто» выяснил масштаб – плюс 60 000 рублей к каждой комплектации, причем у обеих моделей.Седан C50 и кроссовер K40: новые ценыНачинается линейка C50 с исполнения «Стандарт»: 2,0-литровый турбомотор на 150 л.с., ценник – 3 059 000 рублей. Еще недавно за такой автомобиль просили 2 999 000. Шаг выше – «Комфорт» с 200 л.с.: 3 309 000 против прежних 3 249 000 рублей.За топовый «Премиум» с тем же двигателем 2.0T на 200 сил теперь нужно отдать 3 459 000 рублей – раньше было 3 399 000.Кроссовер K40 предлагается в четырех исполнениях. Самый доступный вариант – «Стандарт» с 1.5T на 147 л.с. за 2 909 000 рублей, до повышения – 2 849 000. Комплектация «Комфорт» с тем же мотором стоит 3 209 000 (было 3 149 000).Дальше в списке – «Комфорт» с 2,0-литровым агрегатом на 200 л.с. за 3 659 000 рублей вместо 3 599 000 и «Премиум» с тем же 2.0T за 3 959 000 вместо 3 899 000. Как и у C50, доплата везде одинаковая – 60 000 рублей.Флагман K50 не подорожалЕдинственная модель, которую пересмотр цен не затронул, – кроссовер K50. Его вилка осталась неизменной: от 4 349 000 до 4 799 000 рублей.По сути, стартовая версия флагмана по-прежнему дороже самого оснащенного K40, так что иерархия в линейке сохранилась. Правда, разрыв между моделями немного сократился.Тем, кто присматривается к машинам марки, «Рамблер/авто» советует заранее оценить финансовую нагрузку с помощью калькулятора автокредита. Больше деталей о старшей модели – в обзоре нового кроссовера Volga K50: комплектации, модификации и цены.О том, как за последнее время подорожали новые машины в России, «За рулем» уже рассказывал.Понравилась публикация?Тогда добавьте «За рулем» в список интересных источников: 1. Откройте https://google.com... 2. Поставьте галочку напротив нашего изданияГотово – остаемся на связи! «За рулем» теперь можно смотреть на RuTube

a0si8q.title: Tracy Oliver & Issa Rae Drama ‘Open’ Lands At HBO
a0si8q.content:
EXCLUSIVE: In a competitive situation, HBO has landed Tracy Oliver and Issa Rae‘s provocative drama Open for development.

The deal, which is said to include penalty, caps a lengthy sales process that started in August when the open marriage drama was taken out by Paramount Television Studios, quickly garnering seven offers.

The field was eventually narrowed down to three suitors, HBO, where Rae has a long history, PTVS sibling Paramount+, and Peacock, where Oliver has a Bel-Air spinoff in the works.

Interestingly, HBO and Paramount+ both competed for Open up until the Oct. 6 completion of the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger, which saw them become corporate siblings at the combined Skydance company, with HBO/HBO Max Content chief Casey Bloys and his team taking charge of both. HBO stayed in the race alongside Peacock, eventually winning the project.

Open is co-written by Rae and Oliver a decade and a half after they worked together on Rae’s Web series Awkward Black Girl, which inspired Rae’s acclaimed HBO comedy Insecure. In Open, when a married couple who did everything “right” opens their marriage to save it, the decision sends shockwaves through their Houston friend group, igniting affairs, exposing secrets and forcing everyone to confront the lies holding their relationships together.

Oliver will serve as showrunner on the potential series, which she executive produces alongside Rae and Jax Clark via Rae’s Hoorae banner, E. Brian Dobbins for Artists First and David Becky and Jonathan Berry for 3 Arts Entertainment.

Open stems from the first-look deal Rae has with PTVS, which will serve as co-studio alongside HBO. In early 2027, PTVS is slated to merge with the larger Warner Bros. Television Group into Warner Bros. Television Studios.

The deal extends Rae’s streak of every series she has created/executive produced to date being on HBO or HBO Max, this being her first drama. She is writer and executive producer on HBO’s untitled Male Friendship comedy pilot, starring Shane Paul McGhie and Dasan Frazier.

Rae co-created, headlined and showran HBO’s Insecure, which earned 14 Emmys and a Peabody over its five-season run. She went on to executive produce HBO’s A Black Lady Sketch Show, on which she also performed, and HBO Max’s Rap Sh!t. Rae is repped by CAA, 3 Arts Entertainment, and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller.

Oliver is writing and executive producing Hilary, a Bel-Air spinoff headlined by Coco Jones as Hilary Banks, which is in development at Peacock. She also is co-writing with Scott King a romantic comedy movie for Universal, with Keke Palmer eyed to star.

With the 2017 Girls Trip, Oliver became the first Black woman to write a film that grossed more than $100 million. In TV, she created and exec produced the series First Wives Club and Harlem. Oliver also has in the works The Wedding Date, a movie for Netflix based on Jasmine Guillory’s book, Girls Trip 2, The Blackening 2, the holiday film Deck the Y’alls starring Octavia Spencer and Jessica Chastain as well as thriller drama series Paper Gods at Netflix and Not a Happy Family at Starz. She is repped by CAA, Artists First and Myman Greenspan Fox.

vchas.title: Peak Halftime Show: The A-List Machine Eventizing Pro Games
vchas.content:
Nearly 73,000 fans inside Rio De Janeiro’s Maracanã Stadium rocked out to Ricky Martin and Brazilian DJ Pedro Sampaio on Sept. 27, when the duo performed their song “pikito pikito” live for the first time. But they weren’t headlining a concert — they were playing a halftime show.

The NFL has long held global ambitions, but this is the year it leaned into music to serve as a sort of cultural diplomacy. The Rio game, between the Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys, may be the best example, combining a global superstar in Martin with a local talent. “There was a lot of preparation and many hours of rehearsals leading up to the performance,” Martin tells The Hollywood Reporter, “but it was one of those experiences where everything came together beautifully.”

He adds, “These are memories I’ll carry with me for a long time.”

Puerto Rican singer Ricky Martin performs during halftime of the game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Dallas Cowboys at Maracana Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

Buda Mendes/Getty Images

In fact, the NFL has seven halftime shows planned this season, kicking off with the Jonas Brothers in Melbourne on Sept. 10, running through The Warning in Mexico City on Nov. 22. It’s also part of a concerted effort to elevate games into cultural events. Just look at Nov. 25, when U2 will perform during a halftime show for Netflix’s Thanksgiving Eve game at SoFi Stadium between the L.A. Rams and Green Bay Packers. “There’s really this gathering momentum about how we can further eventize some of the parts on our schedule and our calendar,” Hans Schroeder, executive vp and chief media officer of the NFL, told reporters in October.

The league is leaning into halftime shows as the sports world overall has been more heavily embracing music programming in games. FIFA for instance, had its first World Cup Final halftime show this summer, with Coldplay’s Chris Martin curating a lineup that included BTS, Madonna and Justin Bieber. The NCAA, meanwhile, tapped EDM act The Chainsmokers to play a “bridge show” between the two Final Four games. The NHL has dug in, too, tapping Benson Boone to headline the first intermission during this year’s Winter Classic on New Year’s Eve.

Madonna performs alongside Ronaldinho and Ronaldo during the FIFA World Cup 2026 final match between Spain and Argentina at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19, 2026.

Catherine Ivill – AMA/Getty Images

“The NFL and all these leagues understand that to grow the game internationally and even domestically for the younger generation, they need to find organic ways to get those eyeballs,” says Tyler Stimmel, a booking agent in UTA’s music brand partnerships division. He handled booking on many of the NFL’s international events this year, including Jonas Brothers, Burna Boy in Paris, The Warning and Drew Baldridge in Munich.

“It all stems from the younger generation,” Stimmel says, pointing toward a recent USC Annenberg study that suggested nearly 80 percent of Gen Z respondents in a survey suggested they’d go to a sporting event because of concerts and other brand activations rather than because of the game itself. It’s beneficial to the talent, too, with international acts getting a shot to play before a wide swath of stateside NFL fans who otherwise likely wouldn’t have been exposed to their music. The agent adds, “We live in a highly saturated pop culture ecosystem the NFL wants more ways to cut through. “Music is the most natural way because we already know where to put the show, and you can pick a booking to tap into a version of culture that people within the region can easily relate to.”

In the U.S., that means working with such partners as Netflix to create more event-sized moments, like having U2 perform. “Netflix has leaned in because they see the success of Super Bowl and the Super Bowl halftime show, and it draws more eyes and it brings more attention and it brings more people, and not necessarily all avid football fans,” says Jon Barker, senior VP of global event production and operations for the NFL. “Now we’re tapping into casual fans, now we’re tapping into new fans, and it’s just one more element that opens another door for somebody to walk into the ecosystem of football and participate.”

Unlike the Super Bowl, which is booked by Jay-Z’s Roc Nation (next year’s headliner is Jay-Z himself), the league books its other halftime shows itself, though Barker notes that there is close coordination with its media rights partners. “It gets a little complicated, to be honest with you, in trying to find the right balance,” Barker says of the booking process. “Who is touring and is available? Who can put on a show that can fill a stadium? Who will translate well and do well on television? Who is the right act for the audience that’s inside this area, and who is the right act that will attract new fans that will be interested in what we’re doing?”

Burna Boy performs on stage during the halftime show at the NFL game between Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints at Stade de France on October 25, 2026 in Paris, France.

Catherine Steenkeste/Getty Images

Stimmel, for his part, describes the process as sophisticated, saying the NFL has heavily relied on its regional offices throughout the world, identifying artists who are a major draw in each market but who can pull viewers from several verticals. “Burna Boy in Paris in particular is one that checks off a lot of those boxes,” he says. “He was one of the first Nigerian artists to sell out Stade de France, so we know he is popular there, but he can draw from Africa, North America.”

While the increased bookings may bring in more younger viewers, they may not always be a popular offering to older fans, who might prefer to see just a traditional halftime report with pundits rather than a concert. Stimmel acknowledges that critique but adds that “they want this to appeal to everyone, but the leagues are recognizing that in order to sustain the sport, it has to appeal to younger fans.”

NFL exec Barker says the league isn’t done expanding its halftime ambitions, noting that while “there’s probably a limit and the right balance, I don’t think we’re there yet,” even if it maintains the Super Bowl as the ultimate showcase.

From the league’s point of view, the performances are ultimately about growing the game — and reasserting the league as the most culturally relevant piece of American pop culture. “The way that we think about music is the same way we think about art, the same way we think about fashion,” says Barker, adding that the more ways “we can open to bring somebody in and show them the sport, the better off we all are.”

Halftime show past and future: U2 played the Super Bowl in 2002. The band is booked for a Nov. 25 NFL game, when U2 will perform during a halftime show for Netflix’s Thanksgiving Eve game at SoFi Stadium.

Al Bello/Getty Images

This story appeared in the Nov. 17 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine. Click here to subscribe.

i19cid.title: AMDLSS5 2.5: нейронный рендеринг в стиле DLSS 5 для Radeon с новым движком и генерацией кадров Neural Apex
i19cid.content:
Вышел AMDLSS5 2.5 - бесплатный мод, приносящий нейронный рендеринг в стиле DLSS 5 на видеокарты Radeon. Обновление работает на собственном движке и добавляет поддержку новых игр, включая Baldur's Gate 3, Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, The Last of Us Part I и Batman: Arkham City.
Главное нововведение версии - новый нейронный движок Vulkan, построенный на рантайме DLSSNR-AMD от Mochizuki. По словам автора, сеть стала примерно на 60% быстрее, а игры работают примерно на 10% быстрее, чем в версии 2.0 (на примере Resident Evil Requiem на RX 9070 XT), при этом потребление видеопамяти снизилось примерно на 0,5 ГБ.

Кроме этого, в мод интегрирована генерация кадров Neural Apex от Apex Compute с коэффициентом от 2x до 6x. Она работает вместе с нейросетью даже в играх, у которых нет собственной генерации кадров. Оверлей показывает задержку ввода бирюзовым цветом, а включать и выключать функцию можно без перезапуска игры. Разрешениетеперь можно выбирать прямо в меню (от 540p до 1440p), а интерфейс переведён на 17 языков.

Перед запуском стоит учесть несколько моментов. Первый запуск в каждой игре занимает время: движок подготавливает шейдеры (в том числе после обновления драйвера), и жёлтая строка «Preparing neural engine... NN%» показывает прогресс - игра при этом не зависает. Собственное сглаживание игры (FSR/DLSS/XeSS) рекомендуется отключить или выставить на 0, так как оно добавляет шум, который нейросеть усиливает, вызывая мерцание и шлейфы; вместо него лучше использовать фильтры мода.
Среди подтверждённых рабочих GPU - RX 9070 XT, 9070, 9070 GRE, 9060 XT 16 ГБ и RX 7800 XT. Остальные карты RX 7000 (RDNA 3) находятся в бете, а RX 6000 и старше не поддерживаются. Скачать мод можно бесплатно на GitHub. Автор просит при сообщениях об ошибках указывать видеокарту, версию драйвера и игру. Проект не связан с NVIDIA, AMD или Apex Compute.

1hqg6un.title: Аналитики: стартовые продажи GTA VI стали лучшими в истории индустрии развлечений и уже принесли Rockstar более двух миллиардов долларов
1hqg6un.content:
Опрос

3DNews Новости Software PlayStation Аналитики: стартовые продажи GTA VI стал...

реклама

Новости Software

Самое интересное в обзорах

20.11.2026 [19:57],

Разработчики из принадлежащей Take-Two Interactive студии Rockstar Games не спешат делиться информацией об успехах амбициозного криминального боевика с открытым миром GTA VI, однако успехи, похоже, не заставили себя долго ждать.
Источник изображения: Rockstar Games

Хотя GTA VI вышла лишь накануне, в продаже игра находится почти пять месяцев — с 25 июня, когда Rockstar Games объявила об открытии предзаказов: стандартное издание стоит $80, а за полное просят $100.
Согласно обновившемуся в последний раз трекеру аналитической компании Sensor Tower, по состоянию на финальный день предзаказов продажи GTA VI на PS5, Xbox Series X и S превысили 24,58 млн копий, а выручка 2,36 млрд.

С большим перевесом (75 % на 25 %) самой популярной GTA VI оказалась на PS5 — 18,44 млн копий и $1,77 млрд выручки. Показатели издания для Xbox Series X и S втрое скромнее — 6,15 млн копий и $588 млн выручки.
Источник изображения: Sensor Tower

До тех пор, пока Rockstar Games и Take-Two Interactive не поделятся официальными результатами GTA VI, прогнозы от Sensor Tower остаются наиболее близкой к реальности картиной произошедшего.
Если информация Sensor Tower подтвердится или будет хотя бы недалека от истины, то запуск GTA VI станет самым успешным в истории не только видеоигр, но и развлекательной индустрии в целом.

GTA VI вышла 19 ноября только на PS5, Xbox Series X и S, а до ПК, по слухам, доберётся в первом квартале 2027 года. В преддверии релиза новинка заслужила звание самой высокооценённой игры за всю историю.
