1q9d25u.title: How to Get Started Making a Difference as Tax Rules Change
1q9d25u.content:
Rick Baker is a wealth management expert by profession, advising many of Hollywood’s A-list on managing the money and portfolios for the long term in a volatile industry.

For Baker himself, the concept of wealth management means giving some of it away through a scholarship program that he launched more than 10 years ago in his hometown in rural Alabama. On the latest episode of Variety‘s “Strictly Business” podcast, as we ease into the winter holidays, Baker offers an inspirational story of how those with means can get started making a difference in the lives of others. And Sean Weissbart, a tax expert and partner at Blank Rome in New York, explains some significant changes to charitable giving federal tax rules that take effect for 2026.

LISTEN to the full “Strictly Business” podcast here

Baker’s own life has been a fist-pumping story of a person from humble means seizing the opportunity through education after he received a scholarship to Alabama’s Auburn University. That set him on a path to building a tony wealth management practice in Beverly Hills over the past 35 years and counting. Baker has never forgotten the hard times he experienced growing up on a small farm in Crossville, Ala.

“I grew up in rural Alabama with two parents who were Depression kids. My dad could not read or write,” Baker says. “I was fortunate enough to get an academic scholarship to Auburn University, and then later I attended the Wharton Business School. During that path, I learned firsthand how important education was. And so I decided to go back and start giving back in my hometown of Crossville, Alabama. A very, very rural community, about 3,000 in population. It has one red light that’s actually not even a red light. It’s a blinking yellow light. And I go back and I try to do things that will change that community and make it better and just pay it forward.”

The foundation issues scholarships for secondary education tuition. It also has a mechanism to support local youth for food, housing and transportation costs that can stand in the way of the student attending school. Baker can’t hide his emotion in explaining what it means to be able to help remove even small obstacles to achievement for underprivileged kids.

“I remember what it was like in rural Alabama and not having anything. I remember what it was like. And I never forget that because there’s such a thin line between being mega rich and mega, mega successful and not having anything — being the guy that’s struggling from paycheck to paycheck. It’s a thin line,” Baker says. “And we just have to remember that if we are fortunate enough to be able to do something for others, we need to do that because it could easily be taken away.”

Weissbart, in a separate conversation, weighs in with perspective on the new charitable giing tax rules for 2026 and beyond that were enshrined by Congress in last year’s so-called Big Beautiful Bill.

“There are a whole new set of rules that were enacted in 2026 that changed the landscape for how one goes about getting an income tax deduction for charitable giving,” Weissbart says.

Among them is a stipulation that the first half-percent of an individual’s adjusted gross income “is not eligible to be deducted as a charitable deduction,” he says. Translation, per Weissbart: A half-percent of a person’s adjusted gross income is taken off the top of any tax deduction for a charitable donation. For a person making $500,000 a year, one-half percent is $2,500. Therefore, if the person makes $10,000 in charitable donations, only $7,500 qualifies for a write-off.

After a roller-coaster week on Wall Street that saw the Anthropic IPO generate enormous wealth and a bumper crump of multimillionaires (at least on paper), Weissbart notes that stock gifts to charity can be a great offset to support a worthy cause and avoid high capital gains taxes.

“We’re talking about a very, very significant savings that actually mitigates the loss of that asset on your balance sheet,” he says.

(Pictured: Wealth manager Rick Baker with students at his hometown high school in Crossville, Ala.)

Can I play without figures? Yes: without a real portal, a menu with every figure opens when the game asks for a Skylander. Their progress is kept in files in Documents\Skylanders\Figures, and one button swaps back to the Skylander you played before.
Can I play with a friend? Yes, two players on one PC, as on the console: the second player opens the portal menu on their controller (Guide, or Back + Start) and puts their Skylander on. L3 + R3 sorts out which controller plays which player. Online play isn't there yet.
How do traps and villains work without the toys? Through the portal menu too: when the game wants a trap, the menu opens on the right element, and the villain vault and swapping villains in work as on the console.
Which game do I need? Does my Wii or PS3 copy work? Your own copy of Trap Team on Xbox 360: for now the European Xbox 360 disc (which one exactly), as an ISO or an extracted folder. The setup takes the game's data from it; nothing of the game comes with this. Wii, PS3 and other versions are different programs and don't work.
Is this an emulator? No. The game's code is recompiled into a Windows program, so it runs natively: higher resolutions, 60 FPS and more, a settings menu, the portal menu. Emulators like Dolphin or Xenia run the original game instead; both are fine ways to play.
Does it run on Linux, Steam Deck, Mac or Android handhelds? It's made for Windows (64-bit) and tested there. Wine / Proton may work but isn't tested much; Mac, Android and ARM handhelds aren't supported.
Is it safe? All of the source is here on GitHub. The setup isn't signed, so Windows may warn before it runs (what to click).
Was AI used? Yes, almost all of the code was written with Claude; see How it was made.
Getting started
The easy way: install Core of Light
and show it your disc. It downloads this game, sets it up and keeps it up to date, and does the same
for the other five games.
On its own:

Download TrapTeamRecompSetup-<version>.exe from the Releases page.
Run it and pick your disc, as an ISO file or an extracted folder. It checks the version and takes
what it needs.
Start the game from the desktop or the Start menu.

What you need:

Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a graphics card with DirectX 12
your own Xbox 360 disc of the game (which one)
a controller (Xbox or compatible); keyboard and mouse work too. A real Portal of Power is optional.

Tested on a Ryzen 5 5600 with a Radeon RX 6800 XT (32 GB RAM, Windows 11): a steady 60 FPS at 2x (1440p). Without the frame cap the hub runs at about 133 FPS at 2x, with the native 3D picture on.
The setup isn't signed, so Windows may say "Windows protected your PC": click More info, then
Run anyway. No admin rights needed.

What you get

A sharper picture: 1x, 2x or 3x the console's 720p, the 3D scene drawn at the full 720p instead
of the console's smaller size, sharpening (AMD CAS, or FSR 1 when the window is bigger) and 16x
texture filtering, with the presets Performance, Quality, Best and As on the console.
Bloom and motion blur can be turned down.
60 FPS, or 30 as on the console, or 144 and more. The game keeps its normal speed.
Ultrawide: a wider window shows more to the sides, and the HUD moves out to the edges.
No portal needed: when the game asks for a Skylander, a menu with every figure opens by itself,
in the game's own look. A real USB portal works too, or both at once.
Traps without the trap slot: when the game wants a trap, the menu opens on the right element.
A caught villain talks from your PC's speakers, as from the Traptanium portal.
Your figures keep their progress (level, gold, hats, upgrades) in files you can back up, and
each one is backed up before the game first saves over it: the portal menu puts an older version back.
Quick swap: one button puts the Skylander you played before back on the portal.
A shorter Skylander intro when a figure comes in, if you like (in the settings).
Skip any movie: Start ends the movie that is playing (F4 > Game: off, or A instead).
A settings menu in the game: graphics, frame rate, language, portal, controls, and Extras
(no health loss, full gold, always crit, elemental power everywhere, gold and XP multipliers; off by
default, and Show cheats hides the lot).
Achievements.
A Discord status: the game, your Skylander and the level, while the Discord app runs. F4 > Game turns it off.
HD texture packs work too (how).
Languages: English and German; French, Spanish and Italian as well.

Its settings in Core of Light, the same pages as in the game's own menu (F4). The game's own pictures aren't shown here: they're Activision's.

Controls
The game plays as it always did. On top of that:

Controller
Keyboard

Portal menu (put figures and traps on)
Guide, or Back + Start
F6

Take figures off
Back + Y
F5

Settings
Back + RB
F4

Achievements
in the settings, under Game
F7

Which controller plays which player
L3 + R3
F9

The settings menu shows the keyboard keys for the game itself under Controls.

How far it is
Chapter 1 and the Skylanders Academy play, with traps, the villain vault and swapping villains in,
and in automated test runs all 26 story levels load without a crash. Nobody has played the whole
game to the end yet. If something breaks further in, please tell
me.
What's tested (as of 2026-11-12):

Every story level loads
all 26, by script

Played by hand
with a real portal (below); Chapter 1 by script

Real USB portal
an older portal from before Trap Team: the light, quick swaps, and the message to lift a figure off

Traps
the trap slot and the villain's voice with the built-in portal, by script; a player's Xbox 360 Traptanium portal

Two players
player 2 joins, by script

Graphics
D3D12 and Vulkan, by script

What's being worked on, for all six games and the launcher: the roadmap
board, and docs/roadmap.md for this
game. Questions and ideas: Discussions. Known bugs and the details:
docs/STATUS.md.

Help
The setup says it's the wrong disc. This port is made for one version of the game (see
Which disc). If you have another one, open an issue with the message (it names the disc's title, region and hash).
It runs slowly. Press F4, go to Graphics and pick Performance, or a lower internal resolution.
Voices are missing with headphones. If Windows has your sound output set up as 5.1 or 7.1, the game sends surround sound, and voices on the center channel (in Spyro's Adventure all of the movies' voices) don't reach headphones. F4 > Game > Sound output: Stereo mixes everything down to two channels; so does setting the output to Stereo in Windows' sound settings.
Where are my saves and figures? Saves in Documents\Skylanders\Trap Team, figures in
Documents\Skylanders\Figures (shared by all six games). Core of Light can export all of it for a
new PC.
Why are there no screenshots of the game? They'd show its artwork, which belongs to Activision. The picture above is its settings page in Core of Light, the banner our own drawing.
Which disc
The European Xbox 360 disc (PAL, title 41560911). Its SHA-256 is in
docs/game/default.xex.sha256; the setup, the game and the launcher
check it. Another pressing with the same code (another language set, for example) works as well: they also compare the code part of the file (docs/game/default.xex.code). Other regions usually have other code and don't work yet.
Reporting a problem
Open an issue with the Problem form:
what you did and what happened. It helps a lot to attach the report from Core of Light (LB, the
launcher's settings, > Report a problem, or the question it asks after a crash). That's one text
file on your desktop with the latest logs and settings, your Windows user name taken out. Without
the launcher, the logs are in the logs folder next to the game's exe.

Why this exists
I wanted to play the Xbox 360 Skylanders games on my PC with just a controller, no emulator, and
with a nicer picture. That's really all it is: a private fan project. It's public in case someone
else wants the same.
How it was made
To be upfront about it: almost all of the code here was written by Claude in
Claude Code, the recompile setup, the fixes, the portal menu, the launcher and the installer, and
most of the docs too. I decided what to build, said what was broken and played the games a lot. If
AI-made projects aren't your thing, that's fair.

For developers
The game's Xbox 360 code is recompiled to x86-64 with ReXGlue
(no CPU emulation); the graphics go through Xenia's D3D12 path. This repository holds only our own
code: the recompiled game code is made on your PC from your disc's default.xex when you build.
Building needs Windows, Visual Studio 2022 (C++ workload and C++ Clang tools), CMake, Ninja, just,
Git and Python 3, and the extracted disc in rom/ (rom/README.md). Steps:
docs/development.md, then just play-release. just package-installer builds
the setup. All docs: docs/README.md.
The banner and the button at the top are drawn by Core of Light's tools/make_banner.ps1.
Credits

The players who report bugs and bring ideas: many of them are in the games now. Who brought
what: Made with the players.
GiantsRecomp, SSARecomp
and SwapForceRecomp: this project is scaffolded
from them; app, portal, menus and tooling come from there.
GiantsRecomp by TheBiemGamer brought
Skylanders Giants to PC first and is the template these ports started from.
ReXGlue, the static recompilation SDK, here in a
fork with our fixes on top.
skylanders-portal by TheBiemGamer:
the portal (software and USB), its overlay and the figure catalog, here in a fork with the
shared portal and settings menus on top.
morpheus284: the stone frame around the menus, cut from his Core of
Light artwork, and the banner at the top, made from it (CC BY 4.0).
Laytonator2: the PlayStation button prompts, drawn in the PS3's
style (CC BY 4.0).
Figure save-data decoding builds on public reverse-engineering of the Skylanders NFC format,
among others SkyReader.
extract-xiso is included (prebuilt, unmodified)
for the installer (installer/extract-xiso.LICENSE.txt).

Skylanders is a trademark of Activision. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by
Activision.
License
The code and documentation in this repository are released under the MIT license. That
doesn't cover the game or its data, which you need to own and supply yourself, or the third-party
components in thirdparty/, which keep their own licenses.

wu3tt8.title: Tech Stocks End Dismal Week On Harsh Note; Nasdaq Slides Another 5% And Is Now Flat For The Year
wu3tt8.content:
A massive AI correction wreaked more havoc on Wall Street, ending one of the worst weeks in recent memory for the stock market and erasing all of the Nasdaq‘s gains for the year.

About $4 trillion in market value was wiped out across the AI sector, with Sandisk, Micron, Seagate, Applied Digital, Broadcom, Nvidia, Dell, AMD and Meta all taking big hits. The Nasdaq fell 1,261 points, or 5%, logging its seventh straight down day, the longest losing streak it has had since 2020.

The Dow and the S&P 500 fared a bit better, but still slipped 2% and 4%, respectively.

The selloff in tech coincided with two major developments in AI earlier in the week: Anthropic‘s IPO and a leadership change at Nvidia.

After raising a record $81 billion in going public Thursday, Anthropic fell back near its $83 opening price mark. Earlier in the week, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, was ousted after admitting to multiple affairs, including one with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence agencies of being a Chinese spy. The scandal is likely to disrupt the AI sector for some time due to pending investigations into the affair and also a complex web of investments making Nvidia not just the leading AI chipmaker but a key investor in many emerging companies.

Against the gloomy backdrop, core Hollywood companies fared slightly better, even if it wasn’t a banner day. Disney, Skydance and Netflix all shed between 2% and 4%. Comcast, buoyed by strong internet demand from Grand Theft Auto VI, finished up a fraction.

1ltpi00.title: У Land Rover Defender появится младший брат и станет самой дешевой моделью марки
1ltpi00.content: Компактный электрический «мини-Defender» появится на рынке в конце 2027 года – об этом сообщил генеральный директор Jaguar Land Rover Баладжи. Модель встанет ступенью ниже нынешнего Defender и окажется самым доступным автомобилем в линейке британской марки.Электрический «мини-Defender»В основе машины – модульная EMA, рассчитанная как на полностью электрическую версию, так и на гибрид. По предварительным данным, у «мини-Defender» будет два электромотора и привод на все колеса, а длина кузова превысит 4,5 метра.Официального имени пока нет: машина, по данным компании, находится на поздней стадии разработки. Окончательное название модели еще не утверждено.Китайские производители, кстати, резко сокращают циклы разработки – глава марки говорил об этом отдельно. Jaguar Land Rover тоже ищет способы ускориться, однако качеством жертвовать не собирается: каждому Defender положено минимум два зимних и два летних испытательных цикла. За последние два года инженеры закрепили жесткий стандарт, общий для всех моделей семейства.Электрический «мини-Defender»Из-за компоновки батареи и шасси у «мини-Defender», скорее всего, будет меньше хода подвески, чем у классического Defender. На деле это означает более скромный внедорожный потенциал.Тем не менее глава компании обещает, что новинка сохранит фирменную проходимость и будет лидировать в своем классе.Квадратный силуэт внедорожника отрицательно скажется на запасе хода. Зато «гены» Defender бренд сохраняет намеренно, чтобы машина не превратилась в обычный кроссовер.О том, какие Range Rover Sport сейчас продают в России и по каким ценам, «За рулем» рассказывал.Понравилась публикация?Тогда добавьте «За рулем» в список интересных источников: 1. Откройте https://google.com... 2. Поставьте галочку напротив нашего изданияГотово – остаемся на связи! «За рулем» можно читать и в MAX

yfpt3e.title: CMA Awards See Big Ratings Bump With Taylor Swift's Return to the Show
yfpt3e.content:
The CMA Awards‘ producers knew it; they knew her. What they undoubtedly knew was that a performance by Taylor Swift would bring a ratings bonanza to the 60th annual telecast, with the only question being how big a boost. It was a substantial one, as ratings released Friday showed the 2026 show being up 26% in total viewers and an even more impressive 55% gain in the key 18-49 demo, versus the previous year’s tallies.

With help from Swift’s performance of a “I Knew It, I Knew You”/”Our Song” medley, the CMAs had their highest overall viewership in seven years, ABC announced. The show drew 7.62 total viewers, versus 6.03 million in 2025, for that 26% increase. The 18-49 share of the audience, where the 55% growth was found, had the telecast earning a 1.01 rating, compared to a 0.65 share last year.

Not every bit of that increase necessarily had to do with Swift. America has certainly been high on Ella Langley, who did at least as well as anticipated in the awards, sweeping nearly every category she was up for to win a record six CMA Awards. Her “Choosin’ Texas” song is currently enjoying its 28th week atop Billboard’s Hot 100 chart, an all-time record — although Langley chose to sing a different song on the telecast, her latest single, “Loving Life Again.” (The singer’s performance of the then-new “Choosin’ Texas” on the CMAs last year has been cited by her label as giving the hit its biggest turbo boost.)

Also possibly a factor in viewer anticipation for the show was the promise of a Dolly Parton tribute. The show opened with host Lainey Wilson and Vince Gill dueting on “I Will Always Love You,” a scaled-down but still very well-received homage, in comparison to the all-star Parton tribute special the Country Music Association and ABC put on in October. Other stars on the show included country drawing powers like Kacey Musgraves, Miranda Lambert, Tucker Wetmore, Chris Stapleton, Megan Moroney, Luke Combs and what turned out to be a controversial hard-rock salute to Brooks & Dunn.

But without a doubt, the increase would not have been in such remarkable double-digits range without Swift. A previous Variety report, “Taylor Swift’s CMA Return Helped Disney Sell More Ads,” noted that ABC even re-opened its previously closed advertising space for the three-hour telecast after Swift officially signed on with a performance.

The superstar had announced that she would be attending the show as soon as the nominations came in, with Swift landing one for her Disney/Pixar “Toy Story 5” closing theme song. But the fact that she would be performing was not revealed until days before the show. Swift last performed on the CMA Awards telecast in 2013; she last made an appearance on the show in 2016.

Swift made her performance an all-star affair, beginning the number with a pre-taped and highly choreographed trip through the backstage area that had her meticulously interacting with Brooks & Dunn, Lainey Wilson, Eric Church, Sugarland, Little Big Town and Brad Paisley, all of whom she has some kind of history with. Then, with a symbolic toss back and forth with Bill Anderson, the longest-serving Grand Ole Opry member, it kicked to the live performance and she took to a “Toy Story”-themed set to complete the number, with Keith Urban on ganjo, throwing in a snippet of her first country No. 1 from 20 years ago, “Our Song.”

Later in the show, she presented a lifetime achievement award to Brooks & Dunn.

The CMAs telecast on Wednesday evening was preceded the night before on ABC by a preview show, “Darius, Dolly and 60 Years of Celebration: Countdown to the CMAs with Robin Roberts.” That Tuesday broadcast picked up 2.99 million total viewers, getting a 0.29 rating among adults 18-49 and a 0.38 among adults 25-54.

The CMAs marked Swift’s first public performance of “I Knew It, I Knew You,” after she’d previously sung it at the Motion Picture Academy’s governors ball and at private awards-circuit showcases. It may not be the last the public sees and hears of Swift doing it. She was just nominated this week for a Grammy for song of the year for the film theme, and is hoping to be nominated for a best song Oscar for the first time. It’s likely both Grammys producers and Oscar producers will be hoping for their own Swift mashups, although a possible nomination for the Academy Awards is still two months away.

10n9fy7.title: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ Begins Global Weekend With $76M Running Cume  – Update
10n9fy7.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Lionsgate‘s sixth Hunger Games move, The Hunger Games: The Sunrise on the Reaping, is off to a strong start with $24.6M through Thursday night. Add that to the expected $51M Friday, which includes $21M in previews, and the global running cume is around $76M. Already, that’s close to toppling the previous $100.1M worldwide start of 2023’s The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes.

The fifth Francis Lawrence directed movie in the Suzanne Collins franchise has opened to No. 1 in 66 out of 67 markets to date with another 17 territories set to bow this weekend. It would not be shocking if the movie files a global opening plus-or-minus $200M global.

On Wednesday, the Joseph Zada, McKenna Grace, Elle Fanning, Jesse Plemons, Glenn Close, Kieran Culkin ensemble pic bowed in France to No. 1 with 154,000 admissions or $1.4M, which was +157% ahead of Songbirds & Snakes.

In Scandinavia, Norway on Wednesday, Sunrise opened to No. 1 with $494,000, marking the largest opening day in the Hunger Games franchise locally. Sweden opened to No. 1 with $459,000, coming in +31% ahead of Songbirds & Snakes.

Belgium bowed to No. 1 as well with $343,000, the largest opening day locally for the feature take of the Collins’ novels.

On Thursday, Haymitch set down in Australia with a No. 1 $1.5M opening for the day, +137% ahead of Songbirds and Snakes. Germany was also No. 1 with $1M, +83% ahead of Songbirds & Snakes.

Lionsgate distributes their movies in Latin America with partner IDC. The series has always called at the B.O. there and combined all markets did close to $3M at No. 1. Of that, Mexico minted $1M, +107% ahead of Songbirds and Snakes, while Brazil grossed $679,000.

Italy’s first day was also molto bene, +79% ahead of Songbirds & Snakes, for a No. 1 of $680K.

In Scandinavia, Denmark bowed to No. 1 with $461,000, +65% ahead of the previous 2023 chapter. Finland was also No. 1 with $205,000 +36% higher than the Tom Blyth and Rachel Zegler starring installment.

Netherlands charted No. 1 yesterday with $412,000, +66% over Songbirds & Snakes.

In the Middle East, Sunrise on the Reaping bowed to first place in all markets with a combined $390,000. The UAE opened to $129,000, +135% ahead of Songbirds & Snakes. Saudi Arabia opened to $126,000 was also +155% ahead of the last Hunger Games movie.

The net production cost of Sunrise on the Reaping is $150M, with a majority of that financed via foreign sales. The U.S. marketing spend is $60M, sources say. Lionsgate also directly distributes the movie in the United Kingdom.

dqxc4t.title: GTA 6 Coffee Break walkthrough
dqxc4t.content: Coffee Break is the thirty-first mission in GTA 6.GTA 6’s Coffee Break mission sees Jason and Lucia take a moment to plan their next move after their robbery spree in Port Gellhorn. The pair need to earn (or steal) some money before they head back to Vice City. Coffee Break will unlock multiple main and side missions in order to pull this off.For everything you need to know about GTA 6, bookmark our GTA 6 Guide Hub for walkthroughs, top tips and more.Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to check out our complete walkthrough hub, featuring beginner tips, navigation experience explained, GTA 6 cheats, and more.GTA 6 Coffee Break walkthroughCoffee Break is a very straightforward mission, with just a few things to do. From where you start the mission outside the Motel, walk with Lucia towards the motel kitchen, which is located in the southern corner of the property at the mission marker.As you walk to the kitchen, you’ll speak to Wyman, who mentions the Mud Club and its off-road dirt races. This introduces one of the activities you’ll be able to explore later, and point you in the direction of a significant side mission thread.Once you’re inside the kitchen, Lucia will sit down at a table. Head over to the coffee machine and purchase a coffee for Lucia. This starts a cutscene in which Jason and Lucia discuss their plans to leave Port Gellhorn and move back to the big smoke, Vice City, to do this, they’re going to need some serious cash.Here you’ll introduced to several potential jobs that can help the pair raise enough money for the move. Don’t worry about which one you select, as all four opportunities will be marked on your map and can be completed in any order. You can also earn cash via the methods you’ve already been using, like shopping shops, and selling cars.GTA 6 Coffee Break rewardsCompleting Coffee Break unlocks free character switching between Jason and Lucia, allowing you to play as either protagonist outside of specific mission restrictions. This also means that you can free roam as a pair. Alexa, play Hot Together.It also opens four follow-up missions that you can tackle in any order: Thrillbillies, Hit Avery Pawn, Hit Kingpin Bowling and Impounded Vehicle.These jobs will help Jason and Lucia raise the $15,000 they need to fund their move to Vice City.The next main story mission is Afternoon Delight, and it’s a belter.

1qvhai6.title: Cops Are Pushing Extremely Corny ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Slop
1qvhai6.content: Listening to the in-game radio stations while you cruise around in Grand Theft Auto VI, you might hear a recruitment ad for the Vice City Police Department, which makes no secret of the kind of maladjusted psychos it's looking for.“Have you always dreamed of abusing your power without consequence?” one spot begins. “Well, now you can, when you join the Vice City Police Department, VCPD. You’ll have fun learning the ins and outs of applying excessive force.” The commercial goes on to suggest that cadets will be trained in racial profiling and planting evidence.Given that blistering analysis of American law enforcement, you might imagine that actual cops aren’t big fans of the latest GTA title, which was released after a 13-year wait on Thursday. Yet as millions of gamers have started to explore every stash house and back alley in the sun-drenched wilderness of a fictionalized South Florida, even police departments have attempted to exploit this monocultural mania to elevate their public messaging or recruit new officers.It’s a curious strategy given that the series rewards theft and drug dealing while enticing you to run over pedestrians, but evidently the mere presence of law enforcement in the games (as the primary antagonists, mind you) was enough to inspire waves of AI slop celebrating the thin blue line.An Instagram channel of the San Diego Police Department, for example, on Thursday posted an AI-generated image of an SDPD cruiser set against a sunset over the San Diego Bay. Its neon pinks and purples match the saturated aesthetic of GTA, and in case there was any doubt what the department was going for, the nonsensical phrase “Join San Diego PD VI” appears at the top. “Want to drive a police car, we can make that happen!” reads the caption. “Apply Now!”Another police department in Washington state shared GTA-like imagery on its Instagram page, encouraging viewers to try “the real-life version” of GTA VI by pursuing a career in law enforcement. “No cheat codes,” the caption advertised. “No respawns. Just real people, real challenges, and a career that makes a difference.” A wave of self-serious GTA slop also flooded the feeds of police departments in Canada, from Edmonton to Toronto—though the Calgary Police Service tried something more lighthearted by having one of their traffic officers react to clips of dangerous and illegal driving maneuvers in the game.Among police departments that were not seeking to add to their ranks through GTA VI fever, many posted content aimed at reminding people that laws exist in real life. “Keep It In The Game VI,” advised a typical post on the Instagram account of the Glendale Police Department in California, complete with a GTA-fied police cruiser and view of the city. “Follow posted speed limits, respect the law, and keep your wanted level at ZERO!” the caption warned. The Denver Police Department, in similarly scolding fashion, informed followers: “Grand theft auto is still illegal.”The communications teams for these agencies should have perhaps reconsidered trying to farm engagement and clout from the massive success of GTA VI. As many commenters are noting, the game portrays cops as corrupt and quick to violence. Players have discovered that the Vice City squad will brutalize you if you start filming them during a questionable arrest. One clip showed a cop pulling his weapon on a character who had done nothing worse than stand in the street to take a selfie.A certain dose of this authoritarian cruelty ought to appeal to the right-wing cranks upset that GTA VI is too “woke” when it comes to gender, race, and politics overall. It’s a little different when the most visible villains of the game are choosing to overlook its vicious take on their profession in order to spam epic social media posts.Fox News, just for comparison, dutifully took the tired law-and-order line on GTA VI, with talking heads aghast at kids’ exposure to virtual gun violence (never mind actual gun deaths in the US) and an atmosphere of moral depravity. Elon Musk famously declared that he couldn’t play GTA games because they compelled you to shoot cops.Both stances, however insincere, suggest a modicum of regard for law enforcement that the police departments themselves immediately jettisoned in favor of GTA cringe. They of course won’t win any cool points for it, but at least this way they can pretend to connect with the general population.More baffling still is that the Russian army has generated its own GTA VI recruitment ads to blast out on its Telegram channel, and NATO has trumpeted its defensive security alliance with military-industrial GTA sludge, boasting that “even the best gamers would have a challenge” eluding fighter jets and submarines. Trying to parse Vice President JD Vance’s depiction of a Trumpian “golden age” with GTA graphics is a fool’s errand. In the most dystopian development of all, a US Army battalion in Georgia granted 43 eligible soldiers four days off to play the new GTA in return for reenlisting for another two years of service.What do any of these institutions or their missions have to do with a video game where you rob convenience stores in flip-flops? Doesn’t matter. When the zeitgeist is this all-consuming, you fire up ChatGPT and find an angle, no matter how confusing. Surely someone, somewhere, will be tricked into thinking you have anything to do with it.

gh-1463022818.title: GitHub - noxgp/fnaf1-ps-vita: Unofficial PS Vita port of Five Nights at Freddy's using data from the Android 2.0.7 release.
gh-1463022818.content:
FNaF 1 for PS Vita
An unofficial PS Vita port of Five Nights at Freddy's using the supported Android 2.0.7 data revision.
The port uses a game-specific native runtime written in C, with GXM rendering and a custom audio mixer. The Windows Data Tool prepares assets and compiles selected rules and layout data from your Android copy.
This repository contains no game files. You need your own legally obtained copy of the FNaF 1 Android APK.
Release: v0.1.0-beta.1 · Vita application version: 00.17 · Title ID: FNAFSCN01
Features

Nights 1–5, Night 6 and Custom Night
All four animatronics, the power outage and Freddy's outage attack, rare events and phone calls
Cameras with room effects and the office perspective effect
Subtitles in 11 languages, including Japanese, Chinese and Korean
Touch controls and physical buttons
Extras as local switches (no store purchases)
Saves to ux0:data/fnaf1/progress.sav

The touch screen works for the doors, lights, camera map and monitor bar, and for Freddy's poster nose.
In Extras, Unlimited Power, Fast Nights and Radar disable progress and stars for that run. Plushies don't.
Installation
You need a Vita with homebrew support and VitaShell. You also need a Windows PC with Python 3.11+ and FFmpeg. Linux and macOS are not supported in this beta.

Get the APK. Use the FNaF 1 Android APK from your own purchase. Only one data revision is supported. The tool checks the SHA-256 of res/raw/application.ccn against this value:
70a1ec40284d4f5232d0ecedcbd94a68c51cd937983ad17d2cbf329aad35b6d4
Build the game data on your PC. Download the Data Tool ZIP from Releases, extract it and run:
py -3 -m pip install -r requirements-assets.txt
py -3 prepare_assets.py --apk "C:\Games\your-copy.apk" --ffmpeg "C:\Tools\ffmpeg.exe"
If FFmpeg is on your PATH, you can also drag the APK onto Prepare-Game-Data.cmd. The tool needs about 2 GB of temporary space and the Windows fonts consola.ttf, tahoma.ttf, YuGothM.ttc, simsun.ttc and malgun.ttf (use --font-dir if they're elsewhere). It creates prepared/fnaf1/.
Copy the data to the Vita. Copy the fnaf1 folder to ux0:data/, so you end up with ux0:data/fnaf1/game.version, ux0:data/fnaf1/public-ui.version and ux0:data/fnaf1/ui/subtitles.idx. Watch out for a nested fnaf1/fnaf1 folder.
Install the VPK. Install the VPK from the Releases page with VitaShell. The first launch prepares sounds and textures, so give it a moment.

The prepared folder contains the game's files. Keep it for yourself. Don't upload it or attach it to anything.
Upgrading from the private 00.16 build
Keep ux0:data/fnaf1/progress.sav and progress.bak, and don't uninstall the game. The public build loads its menu graphics from the data folder, so prepare a UI-only update into an empty folder:
py -3 prepare_assets.py --apk "C:\Games\your-copy.apk" --ui-only --output "prepared-ui/fnaf1" --ffmpeg "C:\Tools\ffmpeg.exe"
Merge it into ux0:data/fnaf1/, then install the new VPK.
Known limitations

Beta. The 00.17 build has passed the local tests and full data preparation, but hasn't been tested on a real Vita yet. See testing.
AI and RNG. Starting AI levels come from the supported game data. Edge cases and balance still need comparison with Android.
The perspective effect is a native approximation.
Menu labels are in English.
Loading. The first time a camera is opened, its image depends on memory card speed. A jumpscare may briefly wait to load the first time.
No vibration on the handheld, because the Vita has no rumble motor. Vibration targets supported paired controllers.

Building from source
The build needs a native Windows VitaSDK with libvita2d, libogg, libvorbis and zlib. Run prepare_assets.py with your APK first, because the build uses headers generated from your game data (Git ignores them).
py -3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt
./scripts/build.ps1 -SdkPath "C:\VitaSDK"
The script runs the Python tests and the ARM core, renderer, reader, audio and UI checks, then writes the VPK to out/. The VPK only contains files from an allowlist: the executable, Vita app metadata, original launcher artwork and license notices. The Python format tests work without game data.

xwc9oq.title: ‘Michael’ Won’t Compete at 2027 BAFTA Awards After Not Submitting
xwc9oq.content:
The highest-grossing biopic ever made is sitting out one of the biggest stops on the road to the Oscars.

“Michael,” Antoine Fuqua’s billion-dollar portrait of the King of Pop, will not be submitted for the 2027 EE BAFTA Film Awards, Variety has learned exclusively. That takes actors like Jaafar Jackson and Colman Domingo, along with the film’s entire craft team, out of the running before longlist voting begins.

According to sources with direct knowledge, producer Graham King, Fuqua and various stakeholders made the call after consulting with Lionsgate, international distributor Universal Pictures and the film’s other partners. The sources cite “multiple factors” behind the decision but declined to say what they are.

Representatives for Lionsgate, Universal Pictures and GK Films declined to comment.

Sources tell Variety that Lionsgate supports the filmmakers’ decision.

Earlier this month, the organization sent film voting members its Recommended Viewing Groups for the 2027 awards, which divides every entered film into 15 groups. Each member is randomly assigned one. The British Academy encourages voters to watch as many entries as they can but asks those short on time to prioritize their assigned group and the films in their specialist craft category. “Michael” isn’t in any of them.

BAFTA’s Stage Two entry and deadline passed Nov. 19. A draft list of entered films goes out to entrants and members Nov. 26. The final list will be published on Dec. 4, the same morning Round One voting opens to set the longlists.

Among the films that entered are “The Odyssey,” “Artificial,” “Behemoth!,” “Project Hail Mary,” “Wuthering Heights” and “The Social Reckoning.” The year’s other box office heavyweights, “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” are also in the mix, along with two music documentaries, “Epic: Elvis Presley in Concert” and “Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger.”

It’s an unusual move for a film that has spent the fall building an awards case.

The 80th BAFTA Film Awards reclaim its traditional spot ahead of the Academy this season. Last year, the British Academy announced nominations five days after the Oscars did, breaking a pattern that had held since 2001. This time, longlists arrive Jan. 7 and nominations Jan. 19, two days before the Academy unveils its own on Jan. 21. The London ceremony follows Feb. 21, three weeks ahead of the March 14 Oscars at the Dolby Theatre. For voters on both sides of the Atlantic, the BAFTA ballot is the first real read on the Oscar race, especially given the Academy’s large international voting bloc.

It’s also a departure from producer King’s own playbook. “Bohemian Rhapsody,” his last music biopic, won Rami Malek the BAFTA for leading actor on the way to four Oscars, which he repeated.

King has criticized the British Academy before. After February’s ceremony, Tourette’s syndrome campaigner John Davidson involuntarily shouted the N-word while “Sinners” stars Michael B. Jordan and Delroy Lindo presented the night’s first award, and the BBC aired the slur despite a two-hour tape delay. Both organizations apologized.

“For years, BAFTA and the BBC have repeatedly displayed cultural insensitivity and tone deafness,” King said at the time in a statement posted to his GK Films’ Instagram account. “Their inability to take accountability for their actions or inactions is reckless and unacceptable.”

The sources did not say whether the episode factored into this year’s decision.

The news also comes after the Golden Globes rejected the studio’s bid to place “Michael” in the comedy or musical categories, a submission that came with a letter from Fuqua, pushing the film into the more crowded drama race. An FYC screening at the DGA reportedly drew a standing ovation.

At the Gotham Awards on Nov. 30, Fuqua, King, Jaafar Jackson, Colman Domingo and Nia Long will accept the Musical Tribute Award.

The commercial case was settled months ago, with a sequel currently in development.

“Michael” opened in April to $97 million domestically and $217 million worldwide, a record debut for a music biopic. In July, it became the first biopic to cross $1 billion globally. It’s Lionsgate’s biggest release ever, topping the $865 million of “The Hunger Games: Catching Fire” and the studio says it’s the first film from an independent distributor to reach the milestone.

The critics’ reception was much harsher than audiences’. The film currently holds a 38% score on Rotten Tomatoes. However, viewers have consistently singled out Jaafar Jackson’s star-making turn as his uncle; audiences gave it an A- CinemaScore.

Written by John Logan, “Michael” traces Jackson’s rise from the Jackson 5 in the 1960s through the Bad World Tour in the late 1980s, closing before the first allegations of misconduct became public in 1993. Jaafar Jackson leads a cast that includes Domingo as Joseph Jackson, Long as Katherine Jackson, Miles Teller as attorney John Branca and Mike Myers as record executive Walter Yetnikoff.

Skipping BAFTA doesn’t affect the film’s Oscar eligibility, and the Globes, Critics Choice Awards and guild circuits remain in play. But it gives up one of the season’s biggest televised platforms, along with one of the few chances for a breakout performance to reach an international voting body before Oscar nominations voting opens.

Whether the decision ultimately costs “Michael” a trip to the Oscars remains to be seen.

18glpxc.title: Bassam Tariq On Exiting Marvel’s ‘Blade’: “Life’s Too Short To Make Sh** Films”
18glpxc.content:
Bassam Tariq was once attached to direct Marvel’s Blade with Mahershala Ali, but eventually exited the project.

In a new interview, the Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother director reveals why he decided not to helm the superhero movie.

“Life’s too short to make shit films, so that was my big lesson: I have to have full control over my script,” Tariq told The New Arab. “If we disagree, it’s between them and me. It’s quite sad because we had such high hopes for what we wanted to build.”

Tariq told the publication that he found it “funny and strange to start casting and building without a proper script.” What complicated things is trying to explain to actors who their characters and didn’t want to disappoint them if they didn’t live up to the expectations.

“That’s also very dangerous because if the text comes and it doesn’t add up to what you were saying, your credibility gets completely shot. All I have is my integrity, and I’ve been thinking about that a lot,” he added. “If you’re the bearer of bad news to your actors, but you’re not the one making any of these decisions — and it’s actually coming from a corporate entity — that’s not a great way to be a director. I know some people can take that and run with it, but I learned I was losing credibility with my actors, and it wasn’t a healthy way to operate as a filmmaker.”

The silver lining in walking away from Blade and the film never getting made was that some of the costumes for Blade were eventually repurposed for Sinners.

“That was awesome. I was so happy that that’s the film we got out of it, because Sinners feels so much bolder than what we could have accomplished. Also, it felt so singular for Ryan Coogler, who has been building all these IPs for other people,” Tariq said. “Now he’s doing his own in such an unapologetically beautiful way, celebrating so many different facets of blackness, being an immigrant and the transcendence of music.”

Although Tariq didn’t direct Ali in the Blade adaptation, they finally worked together on Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother.

“I’m blessed that Mahershala came along on this journey with me. The fights, I didn’t expect him to nail it on the first try. I think it was unexpected for him too, since he’d never done it before,” Tariq said. “What really blew me away was how he conducted himself with other actors. Sometimes actors can get greedy and want to make sure they give their best performance when the cameras are on them, and not be present when they aren’t.”

ula30m.title: ‘Yellowjackets’ Creators on Closing Their Survival Story, Killing Characters and Thoughts on Spinoffs: “This Was Meant to Be the Final End”
ula30m.content:
Logo text

[This story contains mild spoilers from the premiere of Yellowjackets season four.]

The end is near for Yellowjackets. The fourth and final season of Showtime‘s hit survival story has begun, and the weekly drop of final episodes will send viewers on a wild ride as they ruminate on life, death — and the meanings behind those bizarre post-Yellowjackets dreams. If it’s any consolation, the creators have those dreams, too.

“Life just keeps getting wider, and the show has been part of that. It’s been an expression of that width and an agent in creating that width,” Bart Nickerson, chatting with his co-creator wife, Ashley Lyle, tells The Hollywood Reporter of the last near-decade making the hit Showtime series. The pair initially planned for five seasons, but when the Paramount renewed Yellowjackets for a fourth and final season, the creators pivoted.

“For us,” says Lyle, “it was about storytelling momentum and, with the uncertainty of the industry right now, let’s just finish a story if we can. We took a good, hard look at it. If we had felt like we couldn’t get it done, we probably would have taken the chance. But it felt like we could.”

What they deliver is what viewers have been waiting for when the survivors of the Yellowjackets plane crash that began the series are rescued and returned home in the season four premiere. Following the teens as they reassimilate into life in New Jersey — while learning how to live with the murders and cannibalistic acts they harbor; the things they did to survive those months in the wilderness — delivers a fascinating watch and full-circle return to where this story began.

Below, Lyle and Nickerson dive into making the final season and what to expect, including the pain of killing off characters while always knowing who would survive in the end. They also explain why they aren’t interested in spinoffs — because they’re ending the story with a period, not an ellipses: “We do feel like this closes the book, and I think that’s important. I think that’s part of the contract with the audience — that you’re telling a complete story.”

***

We have been waiting for this rescue season. When we spoke with you two way back in the beginning of all of this, in your heads, you had envisioned Yellowjackets as a five-season show, and here you are ending with four seasons.

ASHLEY LYLE Twist!

How big of a pivot was this to wrap up the show earlier than you planned?

LYLE Ultimately, as we were breaking this season, we realized that it was workable. It came down to: Do we potentially overstay our welcome? Of course, when you’re making television, there’s always a risk that you will not get another season. So we realized at a certain point that there was a much more high-octane version of this season that could accomplish all the things that we really hoped to accomplish when we first conceived of the show.

Coming off of the third season, we always knew we wanted to get the girls back home. Then we always knew in the adult timeline that we wanted things to start turning in on itself amongst these women in their relationships. And it did feel like we had hit that pivot point at the end of season three. So we just ended up going full steam ahead; burden the hand. The ability to tell a complete story, to finish it on our own terms, is something we’re incredibly grateful for. We hope everyone feels a sense of satisfaction with this final season.

Given the narrative of viewers dropping off after two seasons of a show, did you feel like season three was the hardest point to keep your audience, and did that affect what you wanted to do going into four?

BART NICKERSON To be honest, I didn’t know that was a thing — that audiences drop after two season. I think, in some respect, through the entire run of the show, there is, as it turns out, a gift in being, tremendously insecure and scared. (Laughs.) Every script we’ve ever written, even if we’re just going to our writers group, you have so much of your personal self-worth and the quality of that script, you kind of live and die on every piece of feedback. Although it sounds insane, the stakes of making a season of television are almost a little intellectual — you don’t ever stand in front of the audience and hear them reacting to your thing. Because the stakes are always so high, it wasn’t about: How do we keep this going? Or: People didn’t like this, how do we address that? At the end of the day, you just have to make the story you’re trying to make for better or for worse. And some may say for worse! (Laughs.)

LYLE I don’t really understand the metrics of how they’re counting viewership at this point. I’m not sure anybody does. I think they said season three was the most watched, but some of that, I’m sure, is people catching up on Netflix. For us, it was about storytelling momentum and, with the uncertainty of the industry right now, let’s just finish a story if we can. And we took a good, hard look at it. If we had felt like we couldn’t get it done, we probably would have taken the chance. But it felt like we could.

The Yellowjackets after rescue in season four.

Darko Sikman/Paramount+.

As the storytellers, you have a huge ensemble. So many stories to tell. What were some of the biggest challenges knowing that this was it? That you had a finite number of episodes left.

NICKERSON Yes, just that in and of itself [is the challenge]. We love television. We love telling television stories, and we love our characters and want them all to have a full, complete arc. Then there is the reality only having so many pages and so many minutes on screen. So it’s about how to be as efficient as possible, and that has always been a challenge. We’ve always wanted each episode, each season, each scene to have a beginning, middle and an end. So it’s about, how do you tell these stories with efficiency but also arc? That has always been an incredible challenge.

Did it leave more things on the cutting room floor? Anything you can share now that didn’t work or make the show?

LYLE Not necessarily in a macro sense for this season. Every episode, we’re always over time. We’ll sit with the editors and pull out 10 seconds at a time to get it under 60 minutes. You’re always cutting. That was the case in season one. That was the case in season two. Sometimes you go back and go, “Remember when that scene existed?” And the fact is that it was sort of telling you that it didn’t need to be there. So I think the process kind of works itself out as you go.

Does it leave more room for spinoffs?

LYLE That’s a question for Paramount Skydance!

NICKERSON Having one less season [I don’t think changes that], because we came to an end that was meant to be the final end. There are always ideas you haven’t had yet. So, never say never. But there isn’t something where it’s like, because we had one last season, we could come back and revisit that.

Do you two feel like you are closing the Yellowjackets book with this ending? No ideas for a tangent or a right turn in any way?

LYLE We do feel like this closes the book, and I think that’s important. I think that’s part of the contract with the audience — that you’re telling a complete story. I suppose in this day and age, there’s a never-say-never quality to this question, but at the same time, we wanted to tell a complete story. We wanted it to feel like the audience had been on the full ride. And hopefully, that there’s a lot of emotional satisfaction in the resolution that we find.

NICKERSON At the end of the day, there’s a level on which, if you’re telling a story about survival, you’re telling a story about death, and that means there has to be an end, because that’s what you’re confronting — the end-end. And, what does it mean when it’s over? I don’t think it would be possible to tell a satisfying ending if it didn’t feel like the ending … of everything … ever. (Laughs.)

You come out swinging with the season four premiere jumping right into the rescue timeline. You could have built your way up to it. Can you talk about why you wanted to lead with it, and fill in the gaps from the past as the season goes?

LYLE That is a storytelling paradigm we’ve always been drawn to: not necessarily the “what happens” but the “why.” That was a big part of season one with the question of whether or not they engage in cannibalism. There were people who said, did you ever consider teasing that out? And we’re like, “No.” We wanted to put it in the pilot, because to us, the most interesting thing wasn’t whether or not they’d do it. It was, why did they do it? How did they get there? What is the context for it?

Similarly, with this season, it was a clearing of the decks, a reset in a way that could set up this season as a standalone season. And again, it wasn’t if they get rescued, it’s how and why, and what happens in the aftermath?

We would talk in the writers room, now that we’ve got four timelines or (let’s just make things a little more complicated for ourselves!), in terms of post-rescue, pre-rescue and present day. And it felt like what happened in the interim between Natalie’s distress call and them getting rescued could serve much more effectively as a little bit of mystery. Because to us, the more important emotional heartbeat of this season was going to be the post-rescue: how they were coping with and the different ways they would personally strategize how they would handle the reintegration. That was a much more interesting question for us at this point.

So much has happened to these characters over the course of the series, but it’s also been almost a decade since you two started developing this show. Do you feel like you also have grown with the show, in terms of how you wanted to end it and what you want to say in the end?

NICKERSON Speaking for myself, yes, tremendously. It would be difficult for me to fully articulate what I mean, but so much of this story is a result of stuff that’s been churned up and has continued to churned up. I always say the best compliment that people will give us about the show is, “I just started watching Yellowjackets. My dreams have been so messed up!” This idea that there is a deepness to the show.

I’ve had some bizarre dreams while watching these screeners!

NICKERSON (Laughs.) That’s been our life for nine years! Just weird dreams. (Laughs.) I feel like life just keeps getting wider, and the show has been part of that. It’s been an expression of that width and an agent in creating that width.

This show is about surviving and about death. There have been so many big deaths along the way. We still feel Juliette Lewis’ exit and last season, you took so many of them away! Fans are always reacting. How much did you take the fans into account when you thought about who is going to survive this season?

LYLE We didn’t. I don’t think we can, because, ultimately, if we were trying to please some segment of the audience, we’re going to displease another. We have to write it for ourselves and use that as a guiding light and principle. It’s a fool’s errand to try to do fan service, especially when you’re planning how to end a show.

NICKERSON The first time we met with Julie Plec, who gave us our first job in television, it was a couple days after a big character death in Vampire Diaries. It was like, “Oh, my God. I can’t believe you killed this person!” She got very serious and was like, “It’s my job to service the story before I service what the fans think they want.”

Because, ultimately, when I’m rooting for a character, I have this relationship with them. I’m not really thinking about the story. I’m thinking about the character and my relationship to them. In order to give the fans something of value, you have to keep your eye on what you’re trying to build and not necessarily on how it’s going to be received.

Tawny Cypress and Melanie Lynskey in season four.

Darko Sikman/Paramount+

Your characters are like your babies. Is there a death that still sits with you or any character you wish you still had around to play with?

LYLE I think that speaks to what Bart was saying. They’re all difficult. But one that always comes back around as being rough for everybody involved on set was when we killed Coach Scott last season. Steven [Krueger] knew very early on — we go way, way, way back. He was like, “It’s time. I’m surprised I lasted this long.” There are moments where, man, you miss the character, you miss having that actor on set. But at the same time, it had to happen.

NICKERSON And that’s one of the moments I am most proud of. Every time we watched, it was such an incredible performance by both of them [Krueger and Sophie Thatcher]. It was amazing. The whole thing to watch the Natalie character born in this ultimate sacrifice that she’s making for somebody else, but it’s also a grisly, violent act. I so miss that character. But, what are we doing if it’s not trying to create those moments?

I know those calls to your departing actors have been difficult along the way, but I imagine dying in the final season is different. You probably get some cheering. It’s like a badge of honor.

LYLE It’s easier the last season!

Did you always know who would be the final girl(s), or did it change along the way?

LYLE It didn’t change.

NICKERSON My only hesitation is that, on the path, you investigate different things. But, no, it was at the beginning. At the beginning, this was how we were going to do it.

LYLE We kicked the tires a lot. But we really ended up in the place we thought we would.

NICKERSON Yeah. Some of the particulars changed. Ultimately, the meaning of it has, for me at least, shifted. But yeah, we actually did end up where we thought we would.

I know you can’t talk spoilers. But is there anything you want to tease… will dead characters return? Will we ever see that lost episode? Any surprises in store?

NICKERSON We’re not allowed to say! We want to reveal everything. We just want you to see it!

You have always talked about having big beats you knew you wanted to hit throughout the show: Pit Girl, the scientists, rescue. Anything you can’t wait for us to see, in broad terms?

NICKERSON I don’t think it’s a spoiler to say that them coming back to New Jersey has always been a huge thing we wanted to do, and, in some sense, is the show.

LYLE There are a few things. There’s a scene in episode five that we’ve been talking about for many seasons.

NICKERSON Oh yeah, that is going to be really good! We’ve been talking about for a really long time.

There have been more than one scene that made your actors unwell — and even had them throwing up. For example, the Jackie feast … the Pit Girl reveal. Was there any filming experience in this final season that’s comparable to that?

LYLE I think they toughened up a little bit.

NICKERSON I mean, eating Jackie was rough. That was a tough day!

LYLE That was really, really rough. I don’t know that we could ever top that, in terms of torturing our actors.

NICKERSON Because that thing [Jackie’s edible body] looked good. I mean, not tasty, but, oh man. Just to have what they were going to eat like around is tough.

LYLE There was a moment on set this season when Melanie [Lynskey] brought her daughter to set and sort of regretted it immediately. Like, “Oh, just kidding! Go into the trailer.” I was like, “That’s not real. It’s okay!” She seemed fine. I mean, we don’t have to pay for her therapy! (Laughs.)

***

Yellowjackets is now streaming the first episode of season four on Paramount+ Premium.

sbhtag.title: Chris Columbus: Home Alone Reboot Can't Happen Without Catherine O'Hara
sbhtag.content:
Chris Columbus didn’t know a new “Home Alone” was coming.

The director of the 1990 original spoke with Variety minutes before news broke that Disney is developing a new installment with Macaulay Culkin. According to sources, Columbus had no knowledge that the project was in development or about to be announced. When asked about the franchise’s future, his answer was that any return faces a steep climb without Catherine O’Hara.

“Catherine, as I’ve always said, is 50% of ‘Home Alone,’” Columbus says. “There’s the yin and yang of ‘Home Alone’: Catherine O’Hara and Macaulay Culkin. Without those two in the film, there is no film, because they create the emotional epicenter of that film.”

O’Hara, who played Kevin McCallister’s mother, Kate, died Jan. 30 at 71.

As reported Friday, Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg are shaping the script with Culkin and will produce through their Point Grey banner. The project is in early development at Disney, and plot details and casting remain under wraps. According to Deadline, the film grew out of a pitch Culkin made to Disney film chief David Greenbaum, told from the point of view of an older Kevin as a father.

When Variety followed up after the announcement, Columbus declined to comment further.

Columbus, who is set to receive a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in December, was particularly warm about his former star’s return to the role in a McDonald’s holiday commercial released Nov. 17. “I love Macaulay’s McDonald’s commercial,” he says. “Macaulay is a great actor, and I hope to work with him on something. Maybe it’ll be ‘Home Alone’-related, maybe it won’t.”

He leaves the door open to a return built around the original ensemble.

“I think you potentially could still entertain the idea of doing another ‘Home Alone’ with the cast,” Columbus explains. “Not any of these ridiculous follow-ups to the first. And I only say ridiculous because it’s weird with filmmakers. They don’t understand why that cast works so well. It’s always about the cast. It’s like ‘The Goonies.’ It’s about the cast.”

The franchise continued without Culkin and Columbus in “Home Alone 3” (1997), “Home Alone 4” (2002), “Home Alone: The Holiday Heist” (2012) and Disney+’s “Home Sweet Home Alone” (2021).

But Columbus says O’Hara’s death has changed what a reunion could be. “It was really about Catherine and Macaulay, if anyone ever wanted to do a sequel,” he says, “and unfortunately that can’t happen now.”

He also makes the case for the film’s burglars, Harry and Marv, played by Joe Pesci and Daniel Stern.

“Let’s not downsize Harry and Marv,” Columbus says. “Daniel Stern and Joe Pesci are the ultimate comic duo for that particular film. Everyone has tried in subsequent sequels to be as funny or as interesting as Dan and Joe, and they just had a chemistry that is undefinable. So you can’t do that.”

Columbus, who also directed 1992’s “Home Alone 2: Lost in New York,” has long been skeptical of revisiting the property. In 2020, he told Insider that Disney’s planned reboot was “a waste of time” and that “nobody got in touch with me about it.” That project became “Home Sweet Home Alone.” Last year, he told Entertainment Tonight that another “Home Alone” would be a “mistake.”

Rogen also has a personal connection to O’Hara. She played studio executive Patty Leigh in his Apple TV comedy “The Studio,” a role she still held when she died. O’Hara also spoke at Culkin’s own Walk of Fame ceremony in December 2023.

Columbus is next set to direct “Gremlins 3,” which is scheduled to begin shooting early next year. He executive produced Robert Eggers’ upcoming horror film “Werwulf,” which Focus Features opens Dec. 25.

hs4yq6.title: GTA 6 Breakfast Run walkthrough
hs4yq6.content: Breakfast Run is the thirtieth mission in GTA 6.In this Breakfast Run, Jason (who is finally out of bed) and Lucia embark on a seemingly chill breakfast trip that quickly turns into a robbery spree across Port Gellhorn.This guide, like all our GTA 6 walkthroughs, is totally spoiler free. We’re just here to describe mechanics. Cool momments, needledrops and more will be left for you to find out.Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to check out our complete walkthrough hub, featuring beginner tips, navigation experience explained, GTA 6 cheats, and more.GTA 6 Breakfast Run walkthroughTo start Breakfast Run, you first need to complete the Slam Dunk mission in Chapter 2: Paradise Lost.Once you’ve finished, wait for Jason to call. This can take around half a day of in-game time, you can either skip time, by going back to the motel, or simply explore the area, there are plenty of side missions you can pick up during this time.Eventually, the icon at the motel will light up, meaning you can begin the mission by returning to Jason.After a cutscene showing Jason recovering from his injuries, the pair decide to head out for breakfast. Your first destination is Hank’s Waffles. But, sadly, you aren’t going there for something to eat.Kick down the door and draw your weapon and aim it at the staff to threaten them. They’ll open the cash register and place the money on the counter. Move around the diner to threaten all the patrons, if you don’t they can attack you during this sequence. Collect all the cash you can and continue to the next robbery before the time runs out.The rest of this mission is a montage of Jason and Lucia turning over businesses around the area. Their next stops are a liquor store and a thrift store. Each of these areas follow the same idea: threaten the staff, collect the money from the register and return to the car. There’s a timer in each of those, too, so keep an eye on them.During one of the robberies, the person behind the counter will attempt to shoot Jason, at which point you’ll have to make it out of the shop alive. He simply can’t spend any more time in bed.After all this carnage, it’s time to escape the police. You only have a two-star wanted level, so this shouldn’t be too hard. Once you’ve escaped, a cutscene takes you and Jason back to the Motel.GTA 6 Breakfast Run rewardsCompleting Breakfast Run unlocks the Trust trophy.After Breakfast Run, you can once again play as Jason in the open world.This leads directly into Coffee Break, the next mission in GTA 6’s second chapter. This mission doesn’t have a mission title pop up the corner, but the in-game mission list does count it.

1dk8no0.title: Hello Sunshine's Lauren Neustadter Exiting at End of Year
1dk8no0.content:
Lauren Neustadter, president of film and television at Reese Witherspoon‘s Hello Sunshine, is set to step down from the company at the end of the year, the collaborators announced on Friday. Her exit comes after Hello Sunshine let go of about 50% of its staff last month after Witherspoon and Mediawan partnered to buy the company back from Candle Media.

“Lauren’s taste, passion and leadership have been integral to Hello Sunshine’s film and television success,” Witherspoon said in a statement. “I’m so proud of what we accomplished together and grateful for her partnership and the lasting foundation she built around telling powerful, complex female-driven stories that resonate.”

Neustadter added in a statement, “Building Hello Sunshine alongside Reese and our incredible team has been the privilege of a lifetime. I’m deeply proud of all the shows and movies we’ve made, the doors we’ve opened for new voices, and the ways we have put women in the spotlight both in front of and behind the camera. I am grateful for every moment of it, and I will always be cheering for Hello Sunshine.”

Neustadter joined the company in 2017, and has served as executive producer on series including “The Morning Show,” “Big Little Lies,” “Little Fires Everywhere” and “The Last Thing He Told Me.” She oversaw adaptations of books from Reese’s Book Club including “Tiny Beautiful Things” and “Daisy Jones & the Six.” She also worked on feature films including “Where the Crawdads Sing” and TriStar’s upcoming “The Nightingale.”

Neustadter started her career as a film executive at Miramax and Twentieth Century Fox, then became an executive at FOX network, where she oversaw “Brooklyn Nine-Nine,” “The Mindy Project” and “Lethal Weapon.”

Hello Sunshine plans to focus on premium film and television and Reese’s Book Club, as well as expanding into new storytelling formats and distribution models.

The news was first reported by the Hollywood Reporter.

1oghamr.title: 'Forever' chemicals? Don't be so sure, says engineer
1oghamr.content:
Mohammed Almafrachi Ph.D. '26, water system treatment manager for Baltimore City's Water Facility Division, leads UMD engineering students on a tour of the Ashburton filtration plant, which processes up to 165 million gallons of drinking water a day. The city has partnered with UMD researchers to test different methods of lowering PFAS levels in the water. Credit: John T. Consoli

Inside the disinfection room of Baltimore's Ashburton water filtration plant, 14 University of Maryland students clad in hard hats peered up at six towering vats of bleach used to treat water that flows from the distant Liberty Reservoir into the facility, killing bacteria and other pathogens before it's routed to the region's kitchen sinks.

But bleach can't conquer per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances—commonly called PFAS—a class of synthetic chemicals. Resistant to grease and water, they gave us nonstick cookware, waterproofing technology, durable medical devices and firefighting foam. But these substances' ironclad chemical bonds, which earned them the nickname "forever chemicals," have a darker side linked to deadly cancers, infertility, and immune and developmental damage to infants and children.
They might also be called "everywhere chemicals" because they are widely found in basic items like clothes, cosmetics and pizza boxes, as well as soil, air and drinking water.
"PFAS—this guy doesn't care about anything," said Ashburton plant manager Mohammed Almafrachi, Ph.D. '26, as he led the UMD students through the facility last Tuesday. "We can add whatever chemicals we want to the water, but he's going to stay here."

Guangbin Li, UMD assistant professor of civil and environmental engineering, and Deneen Gordon, division chief of the Baltimore City Department of Public Works Laboratory Operations Division, investigate water samples at the Ashburton filtration plant. Credit: University of Maryland

A research partnership targets PFAS
Not if Guangbin Li, UMD assistant professor of civil and environmental engineering, has anything to say about it. Although one government study detected PFAS chemicals in nearly half of the nation's tap water, the PFAS expert envisions a day when the stubborn chemicals can be curbed to the point of eliminating health risks.
For the past two years, he and his students have collaborated with Baltimore's Department of Public Works, which oversees the city's water system, to study PFAS interventions; city officials have provided water samples and data to Li's team, while he has shared his technology with water engineers.
"People call it forever chemicals, but scientifically it's not forever," Li said. "We still have a ways to go, but we have the technology to destroy them."

A sponge for stubborn chemicals
While many scientists have attempted to lower PFAS by converting it with aggressive heat or electricity to carbon dioxide—nontoxic, but still a gas that contributes to climate change—Li's method uses micrometer-sized adsorbents like carbon that soak the PFAS up like a sponge and lock it in place. The resulting solids either remain safely buried in soil for years or can be removed from treated water after a few hours to a few days.
By experimenting with different chemical combinations with which to arm the adsorbents, Li's aim is to build a kind of super sponge that ensnares not one but the majority of the most dangerous PFAS and converts them into recyclable materials.
At the same time, his research has led him to question the promises of other scientists using similar methods. While some claim that current soil-based adsorbents can trap certain PFAS for up to 100 years, Li has found that the true number could be less than 20 years.
"We should be prepared for a future of these chemicals coming back to us sooner than we think," said Li, who recently published his findings in Environmental Science & Technology.
Bringing lab research to Baltimore's plants
The Ashburton plant, a large, labyrinthine building erected in 1956, processes up to 165 million gallons (625 million liters) of drinking water a day for consumers stretching from Towson to Columbia, Maryland, but it was never designed to treat PFAS. Li is working with Almafrachi—his former student who runs the Ashburton facility as well as the city's other two filtration plants—to identify opportunities for modifications and pilot programs introducing new adsorbents.
"He has all the scientific and engineering knowledge of PFAS, and we have the operational knowledge," said Almafrachi, who as a UMD doctoral student designed a chemical catalyst that adsorbs PFAS. He calls the collaboration between the university and his team "Terps helping Terps."
Meanwhile, through his connections to Almafrachi and other Baltimore engineers, Li appreciates the chance to expose his students to the real-world infrastructure challenges facing the city, which houses one of the nation's oldest filtration systems.
"We have fancy technology in our lab, but it's still a lab," he says. "There's a gap, sometimes huge, between it and the real, full-scale system that students see on the tour."

Publication details
Liu Jiang et al., Biological Aging as an Overlooked Factor Controlling the Effectiveness of Colloidal Activated Carbon for PFAS Removal in Subsurface Environments, Environmental Science & Technology (2026). DOI: 10.1021/acs.est.6c06602
