11za2ay.title: Tom Jackson Dies: Broncos Alum & ESPN Hall Of Fame Broadcaster Was 75
11za2ay.content:
Tom Jackson, a former Denver Broncos player and an NFL analyst for ESPN, has died. He was 75.

Jackson’s family told ESPN that he passed on Friday, in what his longtime co-host Chris Berman called an “unexpected” death, having previously spoken “at length” with Jackson on Tuesday.

“He was a vital 75,” said Berman on ESPN‘s Sunday NFL Countdown. “Tom was poignant. He was active. This is a shock.”

Berman added in a statement released by ESPN, “All of us are stunned. I’m stunned, we’re stunned and you’re stunned. We’ve lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet, Tom Jackson.

“I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown,” he added. “It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week.”

RELATED: ‘Madden’ Sparks Backlash From Raiders Owner Mark Davis Over Father Al Davis’ Portrayal: “That Hurts”

In honor of the Broncos “Orange Crush Defense” linebacker, the entire Countdown crew wore orange ties during Sunday’s show.

Born April 4, 1951 in Cleveland, Ohio, Thomas Louie Jackson was recruited by University of Louisville head coach Lee Corso, playing college football for three seasons from 1970-72, during which he was a two-time Missouri Valley Conference player of the year.

RELATED: NFL 2026 Schedule With Time, Dates & Where To Watch & Livestream All Football Games

During the 1973 NFL Draft, Jackson was selected 88th overall by the Broncos, where he played a 14-year career as linebacker, helping lead the team to play Super Bowl XII and Super Bowl XXI.

Jackson went on to work for ESPN Studios in 1987, paired with Berman on Sunday NFL Countdown and NFL Primetime. His years of broadcasting experience as an NFL analyst earned him the 2015 Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award from the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

2fvetj.title: Стало відомо, чого Польща очікує від зустрічі НАТО після вторгнення російських ракет
2fvetj.content: НАТО має посилити протиповітряну оборону Польщі та східного флангу після вторгнення російських ракет у повітряний простір країни.Про це сказав у ефірі Polsat News заступник міністра оборони Павел Залевський перед вильотом до Брюсселя, передає "Європейська правда".Політик представлятиме Польщу на засіданні Північноатлантичної ради у понеділок.За його словами, Польща не має наміру подавати пропозицію про застосування 4-ї статті НАТО, яка передбачає спільні консультації держав-членів, коли, на думку будь-якої з них, її територіальна цілісність, політична незалежність або безпека перебувають під загрозою."Немає потреби застосовувати цю четверту статтю. Ми саме в рамках Північноатлантичної ради хочемо обговорити те, що сталося. Ми хочемо представити військові подробиці подій п’ятниці", – пояснив політик.Північноатлантична Рада – найважливіший орган прийняття рішень НАТО. До її складу входять представники всіх держав-членів Альянсу (зазвичай це посли при НАТО, але за потреби також міністри закордонних справ, оборони або глави держав і урядів)."Ми хочемо представити нашу політичну інтерпретацію цих подій, а також викласти пропозицію щодо того, як НАТО має посилити дії на східному фланзі та як має зміцнити протиповітряну оборону Польщі та східного флангу", – додав заступник міністра оборони."НАТО має посилити протиповітряну оборону Польщі та східного флангу. Це головна мета, заради якої ми попросили скликати цю раду", – наголосив він.На запитання про те, яке посилення може бути запропоновано в Польщі, заступник міністра згадав нещодавні слова міністра оборони Владислава Косіняка-Камиша." Ми говоримо тут про літаки AWACS (літаки раннього попередження – ред.), ми говоримо тут також про дуже серйозні авіаційні можливості, але не тільки про це. Про деталі, крім тих, які представив прем’єр-міністр Косіняк-Камиш, я наразі не хочу говорити", – пояснив Залевський.Він, однак, визнав, що необхідно переглянути чинні норми щодо дій бойових літаків. Йдеться про те, щоб пілоти НАТО могли швидше приймати рішення про збиття небезпечних об’єктів.Як повідомлялося, 20 листопада на тлі інциденту з порушенням повітряного простору Польщі уламки невідомих об’єктів виявили в трьох місцях в Люблінському і Підкарпатському воєводствах.За даними воєводи Підкарпатського воєводства Терези Кубас-Хул, 20 листопада під час російських ударів по Україні до Польщі залетіла одна крилата ракета та два реактивні дрони, хоча раніше посадовці повідомляли про падіння двох ракет та одного безпілотника.Згодом стало відомо, що пілот шведського винищувача Gripen, який патрулював небо над Польщею під час порушень повітряного простору у п’ятницю, отримав дозвіл на збиття російської ракети, але не зміг цього зробити через складні погодні умови.Підписуйся на "Європейську правду"!Якщо ви помітили помилку, виділіть необхідний текст і натисніть Ctrl + Enter, щоб повідомити про це редакцію.

22213s.title: Russia Starts Towing Ship Hit by Drones in Baltic, Finland Says
22213s.content:
Nov. 22, 2026

Finnish Border Guard

A Russian rescue vessel on Sunday began towing a Russian-owned cargo ship that was struck by drones in the Baltic Sea out of Finnish waters after two days of firefighting, Finland's coast guard said.
The Finnish military has said the strike on the Sparta II on Saturday was likely carried out by Ukraine and that the vessel later drifted into Finnish waters.
The 16 crew members were evacuated onto a nearby Russian ship. One crew member was slightly injured.
"Thermal cameras show that some containers are warm, but the vessel is stable enough for towing to begin," Finland's coast guard said in a statement. It said that responsibility for the rescue will transfer to Russia once the ship leaves Finnish waters.
Pictures and video released earlier by the Finnish coast guard showed several vessels spraying the Sparta II with water cannons during the night in a bid to put out the flames and cool down containers stacked on its deck.

In a rare instance of cross-border collaboration, out of the seven vessels helping to fight the fire, two were Russian, two were Estonian and the rest were Finnish. Preparations were also underway to make it possible for Russian vessels to tug the Sparta II away.
Estonia and Finland are members of NATO and steadfast supporters of Ukraine and often at odds with Moscow on other issues. Finland shut all of its land border crossings with Russia in 2023. Estonia will shut its own from Dec. 1, for six months, on security grounds.
Bound for Kaliningrad
The ship, bound for the Russian exclave Kaliningrad, was damaged in international waters west of Russia's Gogland island, Finland's Defense Forces have said, corroborating an account by Russian officials.

"Smoke is still coming from the vessel, and there is clearly still heat on board," Jukka-Pekka Lumilahti, Sea Safety Officer and Commander of the Maritime Rescue Sub-Centre in Helsinki for the Finnish Border Guard, told a press conference on Sunday.
New drone attacks possible 
Kyiv has sent waves of military drones towards the Leningrad region on Russia's northwest coast this year, including some that strayed into the airspace of nearby Baltic countries, leading to fears that the war was spilling onto NATO territory.
The risk of further attacks in the Gulf of Finland, a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea, cannot be ruled out, Estonian Navy Commander Ivo Vark told public broadcaster ERR on Sunday.
Finland's military said last week it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the same area during Ukrainian drone attacks.
The Sparta II is a 121-meter Russian-flagged cargo vessel owned by Russian shipping company Oboronlogistika that left St. Petersburg on Friday, according to LSEG data.

Oboronlogistika provides logistics services for the Russian Defense Ministry, according to the company's website.
The vessel is subject to U.S. sanctions, according to the U.S. Treasury Department.
Lumilahti said one concern was the weather, with rain, sleet, and stronger winds expected on Sunday night and Monday.

112ljva.title: Путин согласен на гарантии безопасности Украине по образцу пятой статьи устава НАТО, пишет WP
112ljva.content:
Президент РФ Владимир Путин в частном порядке согласился, чтобы США и европейские страны предоставили Украине гарантии безопасности по образцу статьи 5 Североатлантического договора. Об этом в воскресенье, 22 ноября, сообщил колумнист американской газеты The Washington Post Дэвид Игнатиус со ссылкой на источник, близкий к переговорам. При этом Путин выдвинул условие, что войска НАТО не должны размещаться на территории Украины.

Россия в рамках такого потенциального соглашения получит ослабление санкций, однако ограничения будут восстановлены, если Москва вновь сосредоточит войска для возможного вторжения, пишет WP. По информации издания, Вашингтон в обмен на отказ от размещения баз НАТО в Украине предложил Москве отвести свои силы от границы после прекращения огня. Если же российские войска вновь перейдут в наступление, силы альянса немедленно войдут на территорию Украины.

Собеседник журналистов также рассказал, что представители США и Европы обсуждали механизмы контроля за соблюдением Россией договоренностей и способы организации оперативной связи на случай нового кризиса. Российские власти пока не комментировали публикацию The Washington Post.

Разногласия США, РФ и Украины вокруг статьи 5 НАТО

19 ноября спецпредставитель президента США Дональд Трампа  Джаред Кушнер сообщил, что Вашингтону удалось добиться от Москвы согласия на предоставление Украине гарантий безопасности по модели статьи 5 Североатлантического договора. После этого замминистра иностранных дел России Сергей Рябков заявил, что в Кремле не согласятся ни на какие договоренности, предусматривающие фактическое или частичное членство Украины в НАТО. "Поиски какого-то, в кавычках, креативного решения в этой сфере - это неприемлемый для нас вариант", - подчеркнул российский дипломат.

Статья 5 Североатлантического договора гласит, что вооруженное нападение на одного члена НАТО должно рассматриваться как нападение на всех членов и приводит в действие обязательство каждого члена оказать ему помощь. Ранее президент Украины Владимир Зеленский выражал сомнение, что Киев и Вашингтон одинаково трактуют содержание этой статьи. По его словам, она предполагает присутствие на украинской территории определенных сил стран-партнеров.

g1gy4g.title: Interstellar solar sails hit a bizarre problem at 75% of light speed
g1gy4g.content:
Reaching another star will require spacecraft capable of traveling far faster than anything humanity has built so far. Conventional rockets powered by chemical fuel simply cannot achieve the enormous speeds needed to cross the distances between stars within a practical amount of time. One promising alternative is the solar sail, a vast, lightweight reflective surface that uses the momentum of light to propel a spacecraft through space.
Some proposed interstellar missions would take this concept even further by using powerful lasers to push sails to extraordinary speeds, potentially reaching a substantial fraction of the speed of light. However, new research suggests that this approach comes with an unexpected complication. At extreme speeds, some of the very light driving the spacecraft forward could begin acting against it.
In a recent paper available on arXiv, Chao Shen and Jiaze Li of the Harbin Institute of Technology investigate how light interacts with a rapidly accelerating solar sail. Their findings reveal a surprising source of resistance that emerges as the spacecraft approaches 75% of the speed of light.
How Light Can Push a Spacecraft Through Space
Although light has no mass, it carries momentum and can transfer that momentum to objects it strikes. This creates a tiny pushing force known as radiation pressure. Under ordinary conditions, the effect is extremely weak, but in the vacuum of space, a large reflective sail can gradually build up speed as light continues to strike its surface.
For spacecraft traveling between stars, powerful lasers could provide a much more concentrated source of light than the Sun. By directing an intense beam at a sail, engineers hope to accelerate extremely small probes to speeds that conventional propulsion systems cannot approach.
The researchers examined three ways that photons, the individual packets of energy that make up light, transfer momentum to a sail. These interactions are incident light (that raw momentum of the photons hitting the sail), specular reflection (momentum imparted when photons bounce perfectly off the sail), and diffuse scattering (momentum from photons that are absorbed by the sail then reemitted in random directions).

According to the study, these three contributions affect the sail's motion with different levels of efficiency. Incident light provides the strongest contribution in the researchers' breakdown, followed by specular reflection and then diffuse scattering.
A Strange Problem Emerges Near the Speed of Light
The situation becomes considerably more complicated once a solar sail reaches relativistic speeds, meaning speeds high enough that the effects predicted by Einstein's theory of relativity become important.
As the sail accelerates away from its laser source, it experiences an increasingly strong Doppler effect. This is the same basic phenomenon that changes the apparent pitch of a passing ambulance siren, except that light experiences a change in frequency rather than sound.
For the accelerating sail, the incoming laser light becomes progressively redshifted, meaning its frequency decreases from the sail's perspective. As a result, the light transfers momentum less effectively, reducing the thrust generated by all three contributions examined in the study.
In other words, the faster the spacecraft travels, the less effective its laser propulsion becomes. Even with a powerful beam continuously striking the sail, gaining additional speed becomes increasingly difficult.

Various concepts for interstellar exploration have been proposed over the years, including Breakthrough Starshot, which envisioned using powerful lasers to accelerate tiny spacecraft toward nearby stars. The new findings highlight another challenge that such ambitious missions would need to consider.
At 75% of Light Speed, Light Starts Working Against the Sail
The researchers identified an especially unusual effect once the sail reaches approximately 75% of the speed of light.
At this point, a phenomenon known as relativistic light aberration changes how the scattered light is distributed. Relativistic aberration describes how the apparent directions in which light travels are altered by motion at speeds approaching the speed of light.
From the viewpoint of an observer at rest on Earth, the diffusely scattered light becomes increasingly concentrated in the spacecraft's forward direction. Because emitting light carries momentum, the sail experiences a corresponding recoil in the opposite direction.
This means that diffuse scattering (admittedly the weakest of the three forces) begins producing drag rather than helping propel the spacecraft forward.
The result is a striking paradox: some of the light intended to accelerate an interstellar spacecraft actually begins resisting its motion.
Importantly, this does not mean the spacecraft suddenly stops accelerating or that its entire propulsion system begins pushing backward. The laser still generates a positive overall force, allowing the sail to continue gaining speed. However, the additional resistance reduces the efficiency of the system, making further acceleration more challenging.
Advanced Materials Could Help Overcome the Challenge
The study focuses specifically on the forces produced by light and does not attempt to model every obstacle a spacecraft would encounter during an interstellar journey.
For example, the researchers do not include resistance from interstellar gas and dust, which could become important at extreme velocities. They also leave out the thermal challenges associated with directing extremely powerful lasers at a thin sail. If the material absorbs too much energy, intense heating could damage or even melt it.
Another important simplification is that the calculations treat the sail as an idealized mirror. Real spacecraft would need materials capable of reflecting laser light efficiently while remaining lightweight, durable, and stable under extreme conditions.
Engineers are already exploring advanced metamaterials and photonic crystals that could help address these demands. These specially engineered materials can be designed to interact with particular wavelengths of light in ways that ordinary reflective surfaces cannot.
Intriguingly, such materials might even turn some of the relativistic effects identified in the research into an advantage. By carefully controlling how light scatters from the sail, future designs could potentially generate forces that automatically correct its orientation and position, helping it remain aligned with the laser beam throughout acceleration.
The Long Road to Interstellar Travel
Despite the promise of laser propulsion, humanity remains far from building and testing a complete solar sail system capable of reaching another star.
The physics becomes increasingly complicated over such enormous distances and at such extraordinary speeds. Additional effects, including the curvature of spacetime, would also need to be considered in a more complete description of an interstellar journey. These effects were simplified out of the new analysis.
Nevertheless, understanding how light behaves when it interacts with a spacecraft traveling at a significant fraction of light speed is an important part of making interstellar exploration possible.
If humanity eventually sends robotic probes to another star, success will depend on solving countless engineering and physics challenges. Knowing that light itself can become an unexpected source of resistance gives researchers one more piece of the puzzle, and potentially a better understanding of how to design spacecraft capable of making the journey.

gh-148203956.title: GitHub - ArnoAnsems/CatacombGL: CatacombGL is a source port with OpenGL graphics for Catacomb 3D (1991), The Catacomb Abyss (1992), The Catacomb Armageddon (1992) and The Catacomb Apocalypse (1993).
gh-148203956.content:
Introduction
CatacombGL is a source port of Catacomb 3D and the Catacomb Adventure series. These games were originally developed for MS-DOS. Catacomb 3D: The Descent was developed by Id Software in 1991. The Catacomb Adventure series was developed by Softdisk Publishing in 1992-1993 and consists of The Catacomb Abyss, The Catacomb Armageddon and The Catacomb Apocalypse. The original games visualized their 3D graphics in 16 colors and a 320x200 pixels view window. The main goal of the CatacombGL source port is to utilize OpenGL to improve the visual presentation of the Catacomb 3D games.
Main features:

Runs native on Windows 7/8/10/11 and Linux.
Hardware accelerated 3D rendering via OpenGL, supporting widescreen resolutions, a customizable field of view and an uncapped frame rate.
Player, projectile and monster movement with floating point precision.
Configurable mouse and keyboard controls.
Supports all four Catacomb 3D games as included in the Catacombs Pack from GOG.com.
Supports The Catacomb Abyss version 1.13 (shareware).

Current limitations as of version 0.5.7:

No support for game controllers.
No backwards compatibility with saved games from the original DOS game.

How to install
CatacombGL does not run standalone, but requires the original game data (levels, pictures, sounds, etc) to be present on the system. The Catacomb Abyss game data can be obtained legitimately and free-of-charge by downloading the 1.13 shareware version. Various websites offer the shareware version for download, see for example https://archive.org/details/TheCatacombAbyss. Alternatively, the game data can also be obtained by buying the Catacombs Pack from gog.com, see https://www.gog.com/game/catacombs_pack. The differences between the shareware and commercial versions are purely cosmetic. The Catacombs Pack is required in order to run Catacomb 3D (The Descent), The Catacomb Armageddon or The Catacomb Apocalypse.
The CatacombGL.exe (Windows) or CatacombGL.a (Linux) can be run from any location. When started, a selection screen with an overview of all the supported games is shown. In case the Catacombs Pack was installed via the GOG installer (Windows), the game data will be auto-detected. Otherwise, it is possible to manually browse to the folder which contains either the Catacombs Pack or the shareware version.
How to build on Linux
With the following steps, CatacombGL was built on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS:

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install build-essential cmake cmake-data
sudo add-apt-repository universe
sudo apt-get install libsdl3-dev

Ccmake gui is optional (sudo apt-get install ccmake-curses-gui)

General Linux compilation instruction:
git clone https://github.com/ArnoAnsems/CatacombGL
cd CatacombGL
mkdir build
cd build
cmake ..
make -j3

With the following steps, CatacombGL was built on RaspberryPi:

sudo apt-get install git build-essential cmake-curses-gui libsdl3-dev
git clone "https://github.com/arnoansems/catacombgl"
ccmake
Configure and generate the build via the CMake GUI
make -j3

Controls
The keyboard and mouse controls for moving, shooting, etc. can be customized via the in-game menu. The following keys are reserved and cannot be customized:

ESC - open/close the menu
Function keys - various shortcuts, such as F3 for saving the game and F4 for restoring the game
Numerical keys - read scrolls
Backspace - cheat codes in Armageddon and Apocalypse
Tilde (~) - show log

Command line parameters

--descent Skips the game selection screen and starts Catacomb 3-D THe Descent.
--abyss Skips the game selection screen and starts Catacomb Abyss (registered version).
--armageddon Skips the game selection screen and starts Catacomb Armageddon.
--apocalypse Skips the game selection screen and starts Catacomb Apocalypse.
--abyss_sw13 Skips the game selection screen and starts Catacomb Abyss shareware v1.13
--ini Loads the ini file from the specified location.
--log Stores the log file into the specified location.

Additional notes

The original Catacomb 3D allowed the player to reconfigure movement and action keys, but CatacombGL ignores those settings. Instead, CatacombGL has its own keyboard/mouse configuration, which is shared across all four games.
High scores achieved in Catacomb 3D are not stored in the GOG folder, to avoid file access issues. Instead, CatacombGL stores the high scores in %appdata%\CatacombGL\CONFIG.C3D (Windows) or ~/.config/CatacombGL/CONFIG.C3D (Linux).
To aid in navigating through narrow corridors, CatacombGL allows the player to slide along walls in Catacomb 3D.
The automap can be opened via a configurable key, with the default being the 'O' key. The automap can be visualized in four different styles, which is configurable via the Video menu. The "original" style is based on the Catacomb 3D debug automap. Pressing the Ctrl key in the original style automap will cycle it through several different view modes, just like in the original Catacomb 3D. Only locations that were visited by the player are shown on the automap. The automap can also be opened via a cheat code, which is F10+O in Catacomb 3D and Abyss, or Backspace+O in Armageddon and Apocalypse. When this cheat code is used, then all locations are shown immediately.

License
CatacombGL is licensed under the GNU GPLv3 license. See gpl3.txt for details.
CatacombGL would not have been possible without reusing code that was generously made available by various other projects, namely:

Catacomb 3D, developed by Id Software. The source code was published by Flatrock Software under the GNU GPLv2 license, see gpl2.txt (https://github.com/CatacombGames/Catacomb3D).
The Catacomb Abyss, developed by Softdisk Publishing. The source code was published by Flatrock Software under the GNU GPLv2 license, see gpl2.txt (https://github.com/CatacombGames/CatacombAbyss).
The Catacomb Armageddon, developed by Softdisk Publishing. The source code was published by Flatrock Software under the GNU GPLv2 license, see gpl2.txt (https://github.com/CatacombGames/CatacombArmageddon).
The Catacomb Apocalypse, developed by Softdisk Publishing. The source code was published by Flatrock Software under the GNU GPLv2 license, see gpl2.txt (https://github.com/CatacombGames/CatacombApocalypse).
ReflectionHLE, developed by NY00123, released under the GPLv2 license, see gpl2.txt (https://github.com/ReflectionHLE/ReflectionHLE).
Nuked-OPL3-fast, developed by Tony Gies, based on the Nuked OPL3 emulator by Nuke.YKT, released under the LGPLv2.1 license, see lgpl2.1.txt (https://github.com/tgies/Nuked-OPL3-fast).
Simple DirectMedia Layer, developed by Sam Lantinga. See SDL3.txt for license details. (http://www.libsdl.org/)
GoogleTest, developed by the GoogleTest team. See GoogleTest.txt for license details. (https://github.com/google/googletest).

Tools
The following software tools have proven to be very helpful in the development of CatacombGL.

Microsoft Visual Studio 2019 (https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/)
Wolf3D Data Compiler, by Adam Biser (http://winwolf3d.dugtrio17.com).
Dr. Memory, Memory Debugger for Windows, Linux, and Mac (https://drmemory.org/)

Credits
CatacombGL is developed by Arno Ansems.
Special thanks goes to:

Id Software and Softdisk Publishing for developing the Catacomb 3D games.
Flatrock Software for releasing the source code of the Catacomb 3D games.
GOG.com and catacomb.games for providing a platform to obtain the Catacomb 3D games.
Roland Ansems for playtesting every level and reporting various bugs.
NY00123 for developing the ReflectionHLE source port. The part of ReflectionHLE that handles music and sound effects is reused in CatacombGL.
GoGoOtaku for porting CatacombGL to Linux and CMake.

8f2lqk.title: Delta Sets New Business Class Offerings With Collectible Missoni Kits, Wagyu Burgers and Blanton’s Bourbon on Board
8f2lqk.content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission.

Missoni pillows, a dark chocolate square and a pour of Blanton’s single-barrel bourbon isn’t just reserved for hotel turn-down service anymore — it’s also the new standard for Delta travelers flying in the airline’s Delta One cabin.

The U.S. airline unveiled its so-called “next era” of Delta One last month, with food and hospitality offerings that aim to position Delta as the “industry’s most premium end-to-end travel experience,” according to a release.

The new offerings include a reimagined Delta One menu, with a wagyu brioche burger among the highlights, along with a Hong Kong-style sea bass, Japanese grilled salmon and a “seasonally rotating” risotto dish, all served on new Delta-branded tableware. The airline is also touting its “fresh cracked pepper service,” with flight attendants coming by with a pepper grinder similar to top restaurants and steakhouses.

Delta

Dessert now includes the passenger-favorite ice cream cart, with the added option of a fruit sorbet paired with a splash of Taittinger Champagne. And the wines and spirits list has been fully updated with sommelier-approved bottles, including a Silver Oak Cabernet Sauvignon from Napa, which often retails for upwards of $200 in stores.

Travelers can now also request Blanton’s Single Barrel Bourbon on board, with the beloved Kentucky straight bourbon whiskey served in mini versions of its iconic decanter-style glass bottles with horse and jockey stopper. New Delta One flights to and from Tokyo-Haneda airport, meantime, will have a sake program designed by renowned sake brewer Dassai 45 from Japan’s Yamaguchi Prefecture. The menu on the U.S. to Japan flights will also feature regional cuisine designed in collaboration with Michelin-starred chef, Norio Ueno.

Delta

The most visible upgrades begin as Delta One customers arrive to their seats. While Delta’s next-generation Delta One suites will start rolling out next year, with longer lie-flat seats, larger TV screens and even a glasses hook, the current suites feature new amenity kits from Missoni along with a mini Missoni pillow and compression socks from Bombas. That’s in addition to the existing Missoni bedding and an over-the-seat mattress pad which adds about a quarter-inch of extra cushioning.

The amenity kits have already drawn comparisons to KLM’s keepsake Delft Blue ceramic houses as “in the know” collectibles for frequent fliers. Delta says it’s working with Missoni to release different prints each season, following the vein of the Italian fashion house’s runway collections each year (the Missoni-print pillow is not a take-home accessory unfortunately).

Delta

Delta says the new enhancements were “informed by two decades of customer insights” and part of the airline’s larger $1 billion investment into upgrading its fleet.

Stephanie Laster, Delta’s Managing Director of Onboard Experience, likens it to a “hotel and restaurant [experience] in the sky,” noting that a number of hours were spent perfecting even the tiniest details, like “getting the hot towel right with the temperature and moisture and consistency,” to selecting the “right whipped cream at altitude for our ice cream sundaes.”

The Delta One Wagyu burger, meantime, came from the success of the Delta One Burger in Delta One Lounges across the U.S., and from customers craving some “comfort food” in the air. And the Champagne Sorbet offers a lighter, dairy-free addition to the dessert cart. As for the Blanton’s offering: a Delta rep says whiskey is Delta’s top-consumed spirit category, and after doing customer research on various brands, Blanton’s was rated “most-premium” of all the bourbons surveyed.

Laster says non-drinkers will also have increased options, including new mocktail creations. And with flyers valuing flexibility more and more, Delta has rolled out a “Lighter Later” option, with the ability to pre-select meals that fit your diet (I.e. gluten-free dishes or protein-added salads) and even skip a full breakfast in favor of a to-go coffee and croissant, just before landing (all the better to get some extra shut eye).

Delta SkyMiles Gold American Express $0 intro annual fee for the first year, then $150 ▶ 80,000 bonus miles▶ 2x miles on dining and groceries▶ $200 Delta flight credit▶ Priority boarding and free checked bag

The new overhaul has launched on transoceanic Delta One routes departing from Los Angeles International Airport, and will expand across the full global network in 2027. As for what passengers in premium economy and economy can expect? Laster says the goal is to provide a “premium for all” experience when flying Delta, with the airline hoping to eventually unveil upgrades to the rear cabins as well.

“Luxury is about having the experience designed around you — today’s premium traveler values choice as much as quality,” says Kristen Manion Taylor, SVP – Brand Experience, in a release. “These enhancements offer greater flexibility, ensuring every Delta One customer can enjoy the journey in the way that suits them best.”

images.alt: Delta SkyMiles Gold American Express Card

gh-1462463802.title: GitHub - dalves408/halo2-recomp: Original Xbox Halo 2 (title update 1.5) statically recompiled to native Windows x64. D3D11 at 60 fps, true widescreen (4:3 in Xbox Live), mouse and keyboard, Xbox Live through Insignia with your own console's identity, System Link, in-game DLC downloader, hi-res texture packs. Bring your own disc.
gh-1462463802.content:
Halo 2 static recompilation (Xbox to native Windows x64)
A static recompilation of the original Xbox Halo 2 into a native Windows x64 program,
built on the xboxrecomp toolkit. The x86 game code is lifted to C, and a reimplemented
Xbox kernel, NV2A GPU (Direct3D 11 backend), APU and USB stack run it on a PC.
Version 1.0.7 is out: get Halo2-Recomp-Setup-1.0.7.exe from
Releases. The optional
hi-res texture pack v2 is a
separate download (below).
No game content is in this repository. You need your own retail Halo 2 disc. The
recompiled C (src/recomp/gen/) is generated from your copy of default.xbe and is not
committed.
Installing
Download Halo2-Recomp-Setup-<version>.exe from the latest release and run it. All you need
is your Halo 2 disc (USA, Europe): a disc image (.iso/.xiso, a full Redump image or a
trimmed XISO) or a folder with its files.
Title update 1.5 is included (1.0.3 and newer): the disc's own default.xbe and
downloader.xbe are patched with the included title update patch, and each result must match
the real 1.5 file byte for byte. A folder that already has the update applied works too.
Setup copies the 79 files the game uses (about 4.7 GB) and checks each one against its
pinned size and SHA-256. It fails with a clear message (wrong disc, damaged dump, folder not
writable). No game files (maps, sounds, videos, the disc's
executables) are in the Setup or the release ZIP; the title update patch holds only the
difference between the disc's executables and the update's.

Portable: everything is in the install folder (default C:\Games\Halo 2 Recomp):
the programs, game_files\ (the disc's files) and data\ (settings, key map, saves,
console identity, logs, downloaded content). There is no uninstaller, no Apps entry and
nothing in the registry or your profile; delete the folder and the shortcuts to remove
it. Setup refuses a folder it cannot write to, such as Program Files.
Update or repair: run a newer Setup and choose the same folder. It shows the
installed version and replaces only the program files: no disc needed, and saves,
settings and the identity are kept. The same version offers Repair or Quit; an older
Setup warns before downgrading.
Shortcuts: Start menu entries for the game, its settings program and Insignia Setup,
and an optional desktop shortcut.
Hi-res texture pack: an optional task in Setup (unticked), or its own installer (below).
RecompLauncher: the release also has Halo2-Recomp-v<version>-Windows-x64.zip for
RecompLauncher (level 3). It asks only for the
disc, imports it with halo2_import.exe --prepare (title update 1.5 included), and uses the
same data\settings.ini. Its Big Picture mode always starts the game fullscreen.

Settings
config.exe beside the game (Start menu: Halo 2 Recomp Settings) and F1 in the game edit
the same data\settings.ini and data\keymap.ini:

VIDEO: render scale, fullscreen, VSync, frame rate, anisotropic filtering, FXAA, MSAA,
widescreen, and hi-res textures on or off ("Not installed" when there is no texture
pack; in the F1 menu it applies at once from 1.0.5).
Frame rate (from 1.0.6): Auto (the default) plays at 60 fps and switches to 30 for the
rest of the session when the PC cannot hold 60 in play (an even 30 looks better than an
uneven 40-50); 60 or 30 fixes it. Xbox Live matches run at 30 whatever it says.
CONTROLS: every action with up to three keys or mouse buttons, plus mouse aim,
sensitivity and invert (below).
The F1 menu works with the keyboard, a controller or the mouse: click a tab, a row or its
arrows, the wheel moves between rows, right click steps a setting back or clears a
binding. On a controller, hold Back and press Start to open or close it.
F11 or Alt+Enter switches fullscreen in the game and keeps the choice. Esc asks to quit.
Updates: the F1 menu and config.exe check this repository's latest release (at most
once every two hours) and show an UPDATE banner when there is a newer one. Choosing it
runs Halo2 Updater.exe, which downloads the release ZIP, copies it over the install and
starts the game again. data\ and game_files\ are never touched, so saves, settings,
the key map and the console identity stay.

Reporting a problem
Click Report a problem in config.exe. It opens:

the logs folder (data\logs), with the newest log selected;
a new GitHub issue filled in with the game version, Windows, CPU, GPU and memory.

Describe what happened and drag the log onto the issue (GitHub needs a free account).
The game writes one log per run, keeping the last three and stopping routine lines at
20 MB. The log contains:

a [BUILD] line (version, symbol id, Windows, CPU, GPU, memory);
[VIDEO] lines when it starts and when a setting changes;
a [FREEZE] report with every thread's call stack when no frame comes for 10 seconds;
a [CRASH] report for a fatal error;
[SHADER-KEY] lines (from 1.0.6): the shaders your PC has built that the release's starter
list does not have yet. They hold only the game's own shader settings, no names, paths
or hardware details, and they let the next release build them in the background at the
first start instead of mid-level (scripts/merge_shader_keys.py).

Your Windows user name is blanked out. The .pdb files stay with the developer:
scripts/symbolize_log.py turns the offsets in a report into function names.
Layout

Folder
What it is

halo2-native-tu15/
The game: the 1.5 (title update 5) build. Runtime, D3D11 GPU backend, settings and overlay, installer and lift scripts

xboxrecomp-toolkit/
Vendored toolkit: kernel, NV2A, APU, USB, input and network (NVNET, System Link, the Xbox Live router) runtime, plus the Python lifter (tools/)

Building (Windows)
Requirements: Visual Studio 2022 with the C++ x64 tools, CMake, Ninja and Python 3.

Game files. Point the installer at your retail Halo 2 disc (an .iso/.xiso image, a
drive, or an extracted folder). It checks the retail executable, copies the disc's game
data, and patches it to title update 1.5 automatically, verifying every result by SHA-256:
python halo2-native-tu15\installer\tu15_install.py --disc "<path to Halo 2 disc>" --dest halo2-native-tu15\game
Analyze and lift default.xbe. Copy halo2-native-tu15\game\default.xbe to
halo2-native-tu15\analysis\default.xbe, then run, in PowerShell:
halo2-native-tu15\analysis\run-pipeline.ps1
halo2-native-tu15\analysis\run-lift.ps1
python halo2-native-tu15\analysis\apply-gen-patches.py

This writes the generated C to halo2-native-tu15\src\recomp\gen\ and reapplies the
hand edits to it.
Lift the content downloader (downloader.xbe, the disc's Xbox Live content
installer). Copy halo2-native-tu15\game\downloader.xbe to
halo2-native-tu15\analysis-downloader\downloader.xbe, then run:
halo2-native-tu15\analysis-downloader\run-pipeline.ps1
python halo2-native-tu15\analysis-downloader\apply-gen-patches.py

This writes halo2-native-tu15\src\downloader\gen\.
Build. Run halo2-native-tu15\build.cmd (or
cmake -S halo2-native-tu15 -B halo2-native-tu15\build-ninja -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DXBOXRECOMP_BUILD_TESTS=OFF
then cmake --build halo2-native-tu15\build-ninja --target halo2_recomp halo2_downloader halo2_config halo2_insignia_setup).
Run one of the launchers in halo2-native-tu15\. F1 in game (or
build-ninja\Config.exe) opens the settings.

Launcher
What it is

Launch-Halo2.cmd
Offline: campaign and split screen

Launch-Halo2-SystemLink.cmd
System Link over the LAN, and over Tailscale when it is connected

Launch-Halo2-Insignia.cmd
Xbox Live through Insignia, with your own console identity (below)

The game runs in one window from start to exit, including the hand-over to the content
downloader and back. All saves and settings stay in the install folder: SaveData\,
with the settings in SaveData\settings.ini. Every launcher loads the console identity
when one has been set up, so the game's disk cache matches whichever launcher is used.
The offline launcher has no network; the System Link launcher's internet router is off.
Release (Setup and RecompLauncher ZIP)
python halo2-native-tu15\scripts\build_installer.py --version X.Y.Z builds the player release in
build-release\:

Build settings: the C runtime linked in, a .pdb for every program, the Windows
subsystem, and no developer switches.
Version: it sets the version resources (res\*.rc) and src\version.h.
Symbols: it keeps each program and its .pdb in out\symbols\X.Y.Z (never shipped).
Setup: it draws the Setup's pictures from res\halo2.png (scripts\make_icon.py
makes the icon) and compiles installer\halo2.iss with Inno Setup 6.6 or newer (found by
itself, or --iscc).
ZIP: it writes the RecompLauncher ZIP (scripts\recomplauncher_manifest.py).
Shader starter list: installer\shader_keys.bin, when present, goes into the Setup and
the ZIP beside the game. At the first start (or the first after a release adds 20 or more)
the game pauses behind a "PREPARING SHADERS" panel while every core builds them, then goes
on by itself; Esc, B or a click plays at once and builds the rest in the background. Grow it from players' logs (and data\shader-cache\keys.bin
files) with python halo2-native-tu15\scripts\merge_shader_keys.py <logs or .bin files>.
It is recorded in play, so like the title update patches it is shipped, never committed.

Everything lands in installer\Output with .sha256 files. installer\manifest.h
(sizes and hashes only) comes from installer\gen_manifest.py <game folder> <disc image>.
Both outputs contain code translated from the game, so they are never committed.

Turn on Mouse aim in the F1 menu, or in config.exe (CONTROLS).

Aim: the mouse turns the player directly, with no stick acceleration. The mouse is
added to the arguments of the game's own turn function, so the pitch and vehicle-seat
limits still apply.

Sensitivity and invert are in the same menus. F9 frees the pointer, which is hidden
while you aim.
Relative and absolute mouse input both work (absolute: remote desktop, KVMs,
tablets).

Menus: outside play (intros, menus, cutscenes, pause), left click is Start and
right click is B.
In play: the mouse buttons and the wheel are bindings in the key map. Rebind them
in F1 (applied at once) or in Config.exe.
Keys: keymap.ini has Halo 2 for Windows' layout. The player's copy, with any changes,
is data\keymap.ini (SaveData\keymap.ini in a development tree).
Controller only on Xbox Live: sign-in is never blocked. The mouse turns itself off
(aim, buttons, menu clicks, the captured pointer) when the player picks XBOX LIVE in the
main menu, and back on with Campaign, Split Screen or System Link.

These are entry hooks on the four main-menu choices, matched to the retail functions
the Halo 2 decompilation documents.
An Xbox Live match's traffic also turns the mouse off, for games joined from an
invite.

Widescreen
True widescreen, 16:9 by default. Change it in F1 or Config.exe: Off (4:3), Auto (the
monitor's shape), 16:9 or 16:10. It takes effect at the next start.

3D view: wider (Hor+), with more at the sides and the same vertical view. The
projection's aspect is multiplied in the game's own camera code (a hand patch on the
generated C), and the game itself stays in its 4:3 mode, so nothing is stretched.
HUD, menus and text: kept at 4:3 in the middle of the screen. A geometry shader
squeezes flat 2D triangles drawn into the 640x480 screen with depth testing off;
full-width ones (fades, full-screen effects) are left alone.
Halo 2's own Xbox widescreen mode is not used: it is anamorphic and stretches the HUD.
Xbox Live is played at 4:3, stretched across the screen (anamorphic), so no one sees
more at the sides than players on a 4:3 TV. It switches when the player picks XBOX LIVE
in the main menu, and back to full widescreen with Campaign, Split Screen or System Link.
An Xbox Live match's traffic also switches it, for games joined from an invite (not in
the first minute after sign-in, whose traffic to Insignia looks like a match).
RECOMP_VIDEO_WIDESCREEN=0 forces 4:3 everywhere.

Xbox Live (Insignia)
Xbox Live needs the identity of a console you own. Run Insignia Setup (Start menu:
Halo 2 Recomp Insignia Setup; built from src/insignia_setup.c).

Choose your console's EEPROM.
Choose your console's BIOS image and its MCPX boot ROM. This proves the EEPROM is a
real console's: only that console's BIOS opens its sealed section. It also makes
Halo 2's per-title keys.
Give the hard-drive key, typed or from hddinfo.txt, or let the BIOS fill it in. It
must be the key sealed in that EEPROM.
Save, then recover your account from Insignia (gamertag plus the 16-digit number from
insignia.live), or load the accounts from a dump of your console's drive (raw image or
xemu .qcow2).

Setup writes eeprom.bin, hddinfo.txt, eepromkey.bin and titlekeys.bin to
data\Identity\ (SaveData\Identity\ in a development tree). Save and Recover stay locked until steps 1–3 are verified, and
Setup itself has no network code. Nothing is built in, and no key is ever logged. Only
one copy of a console identity may be online at a time: keep the console, xemu and other
copies off.

Verified identity only: the game checks the identity again at start against the
BIOS key that Setup saved. Without a verified identity its router lets nothing reach
the internet: no DNS lookups and no packets to Insignia. System Link still works.
Account recovery: it runs through the game's own Xbox Live library. The recovery
number goes to the game over a pipe and is never written anywhere.
Downloadable content: the in-game content downloader installs the map packs from
Insignia.
30 fps in matches only: Xbox Live matches run at 30 fps, one frame per simulation
tick, because 60 fps jitters against the 30 Hz network game. The game is back at 60 fps
10 seconds after a match ends. Being signed in alone, System Link and the campaign stay
at 60. RECOMP_HALO2_LIVE_60=1 keeps 60 fps in matches too.

Hi-res textures
For players: the Hi-Res Texture Pack v2
has 4,645 of the game's textures upscaled 4x, with mipmaps. Most are BC7. The scope and
binocular overlays and the Metropolis water masks are uncompressed, and their transparency
is exact: scaled back down, they match the originals.

Install or update: run Halo2-Recomp-HiRes-Textures-2-Setup.exe from that release, or
tick the texture pack task in the game's Setup (1.0.5 offers v2).

Texture pack v1 already installed: Setup downloads only the update
(texture-update-1-to-2.bin, 2.7 MB) and replaces the 34 changed textures, each checked
first.
Otherwise: Setup downloads the four texture-0N.bin parts (3.87 GB), checks each one's
size and SHA-256 and extracts them into <game folder>\textures (6.4 GB).
An interrupted download resumes. .bin files placed beside the Setup are used instead of
downloading.

On or off: Hi-res textures in the F1 menu (at once, from 1.0.5) or config.exe (VIDEO,
at the next start). 1.0.0 has no switch: it loads the folder whenever it is there.
Building the release: python scripts\build_texture_pack.py --revision <n> packs a
folder of DDS files into the .bin parts (each under 2 GB, checked by extracting them
again) and writes their pins to installer\texture_payload.iss. build_installer.py then
builds the addon, installer\halo2_textures.iss. The parts and the addon go on a
textures-<n> release that is not marked latest, so the game's update check never sees it.
Revision 2:
build_texture_pack.py --revision 2 --overlay <remade dds> --patch-from 1

It lays the remade files over the source.
It also builds the update from revision 1, after checking the rebuilt revision 1 file list
against its pinned SHA-256.
It writes installer\texture_patch_files.iss, so Setup recognises a revision 1 folder,
including one whose update was interrupted.
scripts\remake_alpha.py rebuilt those textures on a CUDA GPU. Each 4x4 block of the result
averages to the original texel's alpha. Alpha 0 and 255 stay exact. Edges are cleaned up
with total-variation smoothing.

Making a pack: put DDS replacements in halo2-native-tu15\textures\. Name each one
<hash16>_<W>x<H>_<anything>.dds, keeping the extracted texture's name. A file can be
any power-of-two multiple of the original size (2x, 4x and so on), in BC7, BC1–BC5 or
RGBA, with mipmaps. Cube maps are a single DDS cubemap.

Extract the originals: analysis\textures\tools\extract_textures.py exports every
texture in your maps as PNG, already named.
Distant objects: make_mip_aliases.py writes mip_aliases.txt. Keep it in the pack
folder so the replacement also shows on distant objects, which the engine draws from a
smaller mip.
Build the pack: build_pack.ps1 converts upscaled PNGs to BC7 (needs DirectXTex
texconv).
Switches: RECOMP_TEX_PACK=<dir> uses another folder, RECOMP_TEX_PACK=0 turns the
pack off, and RECOMP_TEX_PACK_LOG=1 logs each texture as it loads.

Status
Campaign boots and plays at 60 FPS (Halo 2's own 30 FPS cadence is lifted; heavy open
scenes can still drop below 60). Resolution scale, MSAA up to 8x, anisotropic filtering
and FXAA are available. Third-party pads work through SDL3.
Recent rendering fixes, each on by default with a switch to turn it off:

Fix
Off switch

Cinematic depth-of-field split (missing hangar marines, see-through drone)
RECOMP_GPU_ZCLIP=0

Hard, flickering edges on light and decal passes
RECOMP_GPU_DECAL_BIAS=0

W-buffer depth stored as on the hardware (patchy fog, depth-correct floors)
RECOMP_GPU_WBUFFER=0

Depth buffer read as a colour texture (patchy fog), only while that memory is still the depth buffer (the loading screen reuses it)
RECOMP_GPU_DEPTH_ARGB=0

Perspective-correct colour and fog interpolation
RECOMP_GPU_AFFINE_COLOR=1

60 FPS frame target (the frame rate setting; this forces 30)
RECOMP_HALO2_SINGLE_VBLANK=0

Visibility tests answered when the GPU has them, not by waiting at each one (1.0.6: about 18% faster on integrated graphics)
RECOMP_GPU_ZPASS=sync

Vertex batches with scattered indices or unaligned layouts repacked for the GPU instead of converted on the CPU (1.0.6)
RECOMP_GPU_VSH_PACK=0

Known issue: the HUD is missing from DEL debug screenshots (development builds) when MSAA
is on.
Licenses
Halo 2 is (c) Microsoft/Bungie. This repository contains no game code or assets. The
release programs are built from code translated from the game's executable; they contain
no game assets, and the game files come from your own disc.
The xboxrecomp toolkit is MIT (xboxrecomp-toolkit/LICENSE, with LICENSES/ and NOTICE
for bundled components). SDL3 is zlib (halo2-native-tu15/third_party/SDL3-3.4.20/LICENSE.txt).
The GPU backend's register-combiner shader generator is adapted from MIT-licensed code
(src/gpu/NOTICE.txt).

gh-1426124038.title: GitHub - NoRain211/doa2u-re: Native Windows port of Dead or Alive 2 Ultimate (Xbox), built by static recompilation with a hand-written runtime. Requires your own copy of the game.
gh-1426124038.content:
A native Windows, macOS and Linux port of Dead or Alive 2 Ultimate (Xbox), built by static recompilation, with the goal of rewriting it into readable source. Now with Xbox Live over rollback netcode.

Download ·
Features ·
Bring-up notes ·
Report a bug
Sister projects: DOA3 ·
DOAXBV

ImportantThis project ships no game files. You need your own legally obtained copy
of Dead or Alive Ultimate (Xbox, USA), Disc 2. It is not affiliated with or
endorsed by the game's rights holders.

About
The DOA2 game executable on Ultimate's second disc is lifted to C with a
static recompiler, then linked against a hand-written runtime that replaces
the Xbox kernel imports and the game's Direct3D 8, DirectSound and input
libraries (XDK build 5849) with native Windows equivalents: Direct3D 11 or
Vulkan, XAudio2 and SDL3. On macOS and Linux the same runtime renders through SDL_GPU
(Metal or Vulkan) and plays through SDL3 audio. The rest of the game still runs
as generated code. The plan
is to replace game logic with readable, hand-written source while the game
keeps running.
Features

The whole game, recompiled. Boot, menus, character select, Story,
Watch and the attract demo run on the original game code, lifted to C.
macOS and Linux. Native Metal and Vulkan builds through SDL_GPU, for
Apple Silicon and Intel Macs, Linux PCs and the Steam Deck, from the same
lifted program and HLSL shaders as Windows. A gamepad settings screen works
in Steam Game Mode. See building on macOS and Linux.
Native renderer. Direct3D 11, or Vulkan through SDL_GPU, at 480p to 4K, the game's own 16:9
widescreen camera and menus (the 3D view also widened to 16:10, 21:9 or 32:9, the HUD and menus kept 16:9), MSAA up to 32x (8x on Vulkan) and SMAA Ultra. Water
reflections render at the output resolution; bloom and lighting follow the
game's own passes.
Xbox-like pacing. Frames flip on the next refresh as on the Xbox, at
60 fps, including heavy rain-stage fights at 4K. VRR: On is for G-SYNC
or FreeSync displays and tears on fixed-refresh ones; it is not yet verified
on a VRR monitor. Frame rate: Display fills a screen at any multiple of
60 Hz from 120 Hz with generated frames, and other rates with VRR on
Direct3D 11. It is experimental and off by default, because it adds about 8
to 15 ms of input delay, which matters in a fighting game; online play turns
it off. See frame generation.
Audio and movies. Music and voices through XAudio2, with 3D voices
through the game's HRTF tables and I3DL2 reverb, in stereo or the game's
own 5.1 surround mix. The intro and story movies play.
Controllers. Xbox, PlayStation and other SDL3 controllers, and the
keyboard for player 1.
Free camera. Take the game's camera in fights and cutscenes and fly it
anywhere, freeze the scene, hide the HUD and save screenshots. Turn it on in
the launcher; see free camera.
Launcher. Launcher.exe picks resolution, anti-aliasing, widescreen, the
renderer, VRR, an optional intro-movie skip, 5.1 surround, the unlock
setting, random CPU costumes, the free camera and the staff-roll dedication
card, and remembers them. DOA2U.exe plays with the same choices. On release
ZIPs after 0.1.10, the settings launcher on each platform can check GitHub
for a newer release and install it from its UPDATE page; Check At
Start turns the start-up check off.
PC Settings in the game. The game's own Options menu has a
PC SETTINGS row after Video, drawn and translated like the game's
rows, with the launcher's settings over four pages: the top Page row
(left, right or confirm) turns between the display, audio, gameplay and
HUD settings. Unlocks, CPU Costumes, Free Camera,
Dedication, Life Bar, Fight HUD, Hit Voices and
KO Replay change at once, and so do Resolution, MSAA and
SMAA, on either renderer; the others say they apply the next
time the game starts. Leaving the page saves them for the launcher too.
Combo damage and critical stun. Outside Sparring, the combo's damage
shows under the game's own hit counter, and while a fighter is in a
critical stun their life bar darkens the damage left before the stun
breaks, as Sparring's bar does. Fight HUD picks Both, Damage,
Stun Meter or Original (the base game's HUD), online too; neither
addition changes the fight's state or timing.
Life bar colour. PC SETTINGS' Life Bar row picks the life bars'
colour from 16, at once, or Custom: any colour, set as
"lifeBarCustom": "RRGGBB" in private\launcher.json.
Hit voices. DOA2U's fighters are silent when hit; with your own copy
of Dead or Alive 4, drop its ISO on the launcher (or choose it with
Import DOA4 Voices on its AUDIO page): it imports the disc's music for
the Jukebox, then the voices, and turns Hit Voices on. No extraction is
needed; on Windows it fetches the ffmpeg it needs the first time. By hand,
python tools/import_doa4_voices.py <DOA4 ISO, extracted disc or snd.afs>
decodes every voice clip of all 15 fighters into
private\doa4-voice-all\<fighter> and fills each fighter's selections
folder from tools\doa4_voice_selections.json, a mapping of which DOA4
clip plays for what (it holds no audio), so every install gets the same
hit voices from its own disc. To pick your own, put clips in that
fighter's selections folder (the importer never overwrites one that has
clips), named ..._HIT_LV1_01.wav, _HIT_LV2_,
_HIT_LV3_ (light, medium and heavy hits) and ..._KO_01.wav, and the game
plays them: grunts follow the damage taken (a heavy hit always, a combo
once or twice), at least 0.7 seconds apart, and a KO always cries, in the
KO replay too. Fighters without a selections folder stay
silent. VoiceEditor.exe (built from tools\voice_editor.cs beside the
launchers) does this for you: pick a fighter, add up to 16 clips to each of its light,
medium, heavy and KO lists from any WAV, play them, and tune how often
they play; a running game picks up changes within a second. Its Save
mapping button (or the importer's --save-selections) writes your picks
back into the mapping file to share them. Hits are
graded by the move's base damage, before combo scaling. It needs an
ffmpeg with XMA support; on Windows the importers and the build fetch one into tools\ffmpeg. PC SETTINGS' Hit Voices
row sets them Off, Quiet, Normal or Loud. Online each player's own row
applies; a rollback's re-run frames stay silent, so a hit is voiced once.
Dynamic KO replay. PC SETTINGS' KO Replay row: with Dynamic
(the default), a few frames after the KO hit the fight stands still and
the game's own multi-angle replay, which DOA2U otherwise keeps for a human
winner's few special moves, shows the hit three times from three cameras,
the last at 85% speed, as Tekken Tag Tournament does; then the fall plays
out live and the round moves on. KOs by the stage (hazards, fences,
falls into another area) get no replay at all. Original keeps DOA2U's
own replays.
Off while logged on to DOA ONLINE.
Quit Game. The main menu ends with a QUIT GAME entry, lettered and
drawn like the game's own, that asks before it closes the game.
Jukebox. A JUKEBOX entry before Quit Game, with its own picture,
opens a page of the game's own Options menu with the game's music:
DOA2U's own 50 tracks from the disc, and the soundtracks of Dead or Alive 3
and Dead or Alive 4 from your own discs. Album and Track choose a
track (left and right) and A plays or stops it; Play Mode is Repeat
One, Play All or Shuffle (which move on after two loops, fading out).
Assign To chooses any of the game's music (a fighter's theme, its
remix, Character Select, the endings and so on) and A gives it the chosen
track, from the next time that music starts; Assigned shows what it
plays, and A there puts its own track back. Assignments are kept in
jukebox\assignments.txt. The game's own sound is muted while a
track plays; leaving the page returns to the main menu. Online the game
plays its own music. To add an album, choose Import Disc on the
launcher's JUKEBOX page, or drop the ISO on the launcher (a DOA3 or DOA4
disc is imported; any other disc is used as the game's disc and built), or
run python tools/import_soundtrack.py <ISO or extracted folder>. DOA3's
tracks are copied as they are; DOA4's are decoded with ffmpeg (on Windows the
import fetches one into tools\ffmpeg) and encoded as ADX with their loops by
recomp_adx_encode from the game's build, so build the game first. Albums
go to a jukebox folder beside the launcher (jukebox\<album>), with the
music of each disc's movies (opening, endings, logos) taken out of the SFD
files in its movie folders as well; the build adds DOA2U's own movies' music
as DOA2U-MOVIES, and the DOA1U album is the Dead or Alive Ultimate
music on DOA2U's disc (DOA1\Sound, from the music list in Doa1.xbe).
JukeboxEditor.exe (Edit Tracks on the launcher's JUKEBOX page;
built from tools\jukebox_editor.cs) lists every album, plays a preview of
any track, renames tracks and albums and picks what each of the game's music
plays. To rename tracks by hand, open jukebox\<album>\names.txt
(jukebox\doa2u for the game's own music): each line is file = name, and
album = ... names the album. The game lists every track there when it
starts, reads the names at start, and keeps them when you import again.
Mods. Files in a mods folder beside the launcher replace the
game's files without touching the disc. Each folder in it is a mod that
mirrors the disc: mods\<mod>\DOA2\<file>.sfd replaces a whole file,
and a folder named after one of the game's archives replaces single
entries in it, by their name in the archive or their number:
mods\<mod>\DOA2\<archive>.afs\<entry>.adx (or <number>.adx). An entry
can be a plain WAV (8 to 32-bit PCM, mono or stereo, any
rate): it is encoded to ADX once and kept in mods\.cache, and loops
where its smpl chunk says or, if the track it replaces looped, over the
whole song. Mods load by folder name, or in the order mods\order.txt
lists them, and a later mod's file wins; a folder whose name starts with
_ is off. The game's log (private\play-logs) lists every mod and file
it serves. Netplay only pairs players whose mods are the same.
Sharper menus. Both renderers redraw the game's 32-bit 2D art (menus,
fonts, the HUD) at four times its size with xBRZ the first time each piece is
shown, so it stays smooth at high resolutions; the Vulkan renderer also
redraws 8-bit alpha art, which Direct3D 11 samples differently and leaves
as-is. RECOMP_UI_UPSCALE=0 turns it off.
Saves. Your profile and unlocks save to private\play-disc; every
character and costume is offered unless you choose Earn on the
launcher's GAMEPLAY page. Your profile only ever saves what you have
earned, so choosing Earn later gives it back as it was. The game's soft reset
(Start + Back + both triggers) restarts it.
Built from your disc. Launcher.exe lifts the game from your ISO and
refuses any executable other than the one the developers tested.

Status
Warning0.4.0 Alpha is bring-up software. Story, Watch and the attract demo play
in development runs on every stage, but many modes and characters have not
been tried. A draw the port cannot render yet stops the game with a message
in the log.

Area
State

Boot, menus, attract demo, character select
Working

Stages
Every stage played

Story endings
Every ending, its credits and epilogue play

Story, Ayane and Gen Fu
Stages 1-6 cleared without a stop in scripted runs; the Tengu fight was lost each time

Watch
Fights played, including Kasumi vs Lei Fang on The Burai Zenin at 4K and 60 fps

Other characters, Versus, Tag, Survival, Time Attack, Sparring
Not yet played through

Tengu's stage, The Miyama
In Stage Select, before Random, outside offline Tag, and in Live Tag and Team Battle; played in Sparring only, other modes and Live not yet played through

Every character and costume
Unlocked by default (the launcher's Earn option leaves them to play); profiles save only what was earned

Native 16:9 widescreen, 16:10, 21:9 and 32:9, up to 4K, MSAA up to 32x, SMAA Ultra
Working, chosen in the launcher; 32:9 tried only in the attract demo and Story character select, on Direct3D 11 and Vulkan

Vulkan renderer on Windows
Working, chosen in the launcher; not yet tested on AMD; MSAA stops at 8x

Audio, including 3D voices and reverb
Working

Intro and story movies
Play; the launcher can skip the intro ones

Xbox and other SDL3 controllers, keyboard
Working; keyboard drives player 1

Free camera, scene freeze, screenshots
Working in the attract demo on macOS; a frozen stage's leaves and branches still move

Xbox Live menus
On by default: the game's own Live pages run on the matchmaker, with rollback fights; logging on switches the run to online mode and back. RECOMP_LIVE=0 turns it off, and the pages then report no account, where Yes quits to the desktop in place of the Dashboard. Test build (Xbox Live)

Hand-written game logic
Not started; the game runs as generated code

macOS and Linux
Boot, menus and the attract demo render at 60 fps through Metal and Vulkan, with MSAA up to 8x and SMAA (building)

Known issues: a demanding moment on The Burai Zenin can still drop a
single frame; the safari stage's heat haze does not ripple yet, and its water
leaves a gap between the elephants' reflections. The game's bloom glows
around bright surfaces as on the Xbox, which reads more strongly on a sharp
4K image.
Play the alpha
On macOS and Linux, including the Steam Deck, follow
building on macOS and Linux instead.
Requirements: Windows 10/11 x64, internet access for the first build, and
your Disc 2 ISO with about 6 GB free. The ZIP carries Python (with Capstone,
Pillow and truststore), CMake and the pinned
llvm-mingw compiler in
tools\llvm-mingw, so there is nothing to install. A source checkout downloads
llvm-mingw (190 MB) there on first build and checks its SHA-256; neither needs
Visual Studio or administrator approval. If tools\llvm-mingw is missing and a
clang.exe with mingw32-make.exe beside it is on PATH (for example winget's
llvm-mingw), the build uses that copy instead, without the version pin or
SHA-256 check.

Download the ZIP from the
latest release and
extract it into a new folder with a short path, such as C:\DOA2U.
Open Launcher.exe and drag your Disc 2 ISO onto it (or choose it on the
GAME page); the build starts at once. Wait for Build complete
(about 10 minutes). The build stops unless it reproduces the exact program
the developers tested.
Pick resolution, MSAA, SMAA, widescreen, the renderer, VRR, the frame rate
and the intro skip on VIDEO, stereo or 5.1 on AUDIO and Earn on
GAMEPLAY to leave unlocks to play, then choose Start Game on the
GAME page. A controller, the keyboard or the mouse all work. Your
choices are remembered, and DOA2U.exe plays with them later.

The first launch copies about 700 MB of the game's disc archives into its
hard-disk cache, which takes a few seconds. Saves and the cache
live in private\play-disc. The package contains tools and source, never a
prebuilt runner or game data. GitHub's automatic source archives lack the
pinned lifter and extractor; use the release ZIP.
Controls: the first connected controller, or the keyboard for player 1:
arrows are the D-pad, Enter is Start, Backspace is Back, Z/X are A/B, A/S are
X/Y, Q/W are White/Black and E/R are the triggers. F3 turns on, or off again,
a readout of the frame rate, the average frame time and the slowest frame of
the last second; it starts off. F11 or Alt+Enter switches between a window and
borderless fullscreen.
To rebind, open Options, Controller, Rebind. This opens the game's
Button Config screen with Keyboard and Controller in its left list.
Choose one, pick a button's plate, press A, then press the new key or
controller button; a press on the other device cancels. The key or button
swaps with the Xbox button that had it. Left/Right turns the plates to Up,
Down, Left, Right, Start and Back. Default restores that device's
defaults, B goes back, and leaving the screen saves. Controller buttons apply
to every controller.
Rebind saves to private/keyboard.json and private/controller.json, which
you can also write by hand with the buttons to change, for example
{"a": "Space", "b": "Ctrl", "start": "Tab"} or {"a": "LB", "white": "A"}.
Buttons are up, down, left, right, start, back, a, b, x, y, white, black,
ltrig and rtrig; keys are A-Z, 0-9, F1-F9, F12, Up, Down, Left, Right, Enter,
Backspace, Space, Tab, Shift, Ctrl and Esc; controller buttons are A, B, X and
Y (by position, so Cross is A), Back, Start, LB, RB, LT, RT, LS, RS, Up, Down,
Left, Right, Misc, P1-P4 and Touchpad. Buttons you leave out keep their keys,
except that a key you give to one button leaves the button that had it. F10
is a Windows system key, and F11 and Alt+Enter are reserved for fullscreen, so
none of them can be bound. The game reads both files when it starts; an
entry it cannot use is named in the session log and skipped. F3 keeps its
readout and, with the free camera turned on, F1, F12 and P keep their jobs,
so a button bound to one of those does both. The free camera's own keys stay
fixed, and while it flies the keyboard is the camera's.
Offline, hold Back for two seconds to quit to the desktop: A quits, B keeps
playing.
Build from source
The public tests need no game files or lifter checkout:
git clone https://github.com/NoRain211/doa2u-re.git
cd doa2u-re
python -m unittest discover -s tools -p "test_*.py"
python tools/public_export.py verify --require-public-tree
cmake -S recomp-runtime -B build/recomp-runtime
cmake --build build/recomp-runtime --config Debug
ctest --test-dir build/recomp-runtime -C Debug --output-on-failure
To also test real PCM consumption on this PC's audio endpoint, configure with
-DRECOMP_NATIVE_AUDIO_TEST=ON. Passing tests does not establish game
compatibility.
To build the game from a clone, initialize the lifter and pass your ISO:
git submodule update --init tools/xboxrecomp
python tools/package_test.py --launchers .
python tools/build_game.py <your-disc-2.iso>
python tools/run_game.py --play
The importer extracts the disc once into private/imported-disc with XboxDev
extract-xiso (on PATH, or bundled
in the release ZIP), selects the game executable by its SHA-256 and leaves
the ISO unchanged. Only that hash is published, in tools/build_game.py.
A different ISO is staged first and replaces that extraction and receipt only if it verifies; a wrong disc keeps the previous import.
After a successful build the disc moves to private/play-disc and the
extraction keeps only its receipt, so the install holds one copy of the disc.
After a runtime change, python tools/build_game.py --build-only reuses the
authenticated lift; --lift-only generates without building. Generated C,
receipts and logs stay in private/.
The lift reads the committed function list in tools/doa2u/functions;
--disassemble rebuilds that list from the executable (about 25 minutes)
after a change to tools/doa2u/seed_functions.json or the lifter pin.
tools/doa2u/function_status.json is the decompilation registry. It records
the Ghidra name for each tracked function and, once it is more than a name,
its status (named, decompiled, bound or tested). A bound or tested
entry also names the host source and symbol; the runtime replacement stays
in recomp-runtime/program_manual.c or the adapter's own manual lookup. Raw
decompiler output, generated C and retail bytes stay under private/.

The initial decompiled entries are the named functions that already carry a
Ghidra comment; the rest stay named until their bodies are worked through.
python -m unittest discover -s tools -p "test_*.py" checks every registry
address against the committed function list and checks bound symbols exist.
Refresh names and tags with tools/doa2u/ghidra

1mo2idb.title: Spain Pitches Co-Productions, Incentives to India at WAVES Film Bazaar
1mo2idb.content:
Spain, the Country of Honor at this year’s International Film Festival of India (IFFI), made its case to Indian filmmakers at WAVES Film Bazaar in Goa, laying out its incentives, locations and crews and pushing for closer co-production ties.

The panel, “Spain: Where Stories Find Their Stage – Incentives, Locations & Co-production Opportunities,” was part of the Knowledge Series at the 20th edition of the market, which runs Nov. 20-24 alongside the 57th IFFI. Variety Asia editor Naman Ramachandran moderated.

“For us, co-production is a key instrument,” said Camilo Vázquez, deputy director of the Institute of Cinematography and Audiovisual Arts (ICAA), the film agency of Spain’s Ministry of Culture. He pointed to better financing, exchanges between technical and artistic teams, and stories that could connect with audiences in both countries, and described the timing as particularly favorable for India-Spain partnerships.

For Indian producers weighing Spain as a filming destination, the offer extends beyond its locations. Usha Jadhav, a National Award-winning actor and producer with Spanish company ACortes Films, highlighted the country’s track record with international productions, its range of landscapes and architecture, and skilled crews used to working on both big-budget and independent films. She also cited eight-hour shifts and quieter shooting environments as practical advantages, particularly for sync-sound productions.

Jadhav said the relationship should not be limited to service work, and made a case for collaborations that bring creative teams together across borders.

“Language is not a barrier, because cinema itself is a universal language,” Jadhav said. “We need human stories.”

Lara Molina, general coordinator of the Spain Film Commission, outlined the tax incentives available to international productions. Miguel Fabián Salazar, Spain’s economic and commercial counselor in Mumbai for the country’s trade and investment agency ICEX, set out what each side brings. India offers production scale, a large consumer market, a global diaspora and strengths in VFX and animation. Spain offers experienced crews, creative talent and access to Europe and Latin America. Partnerships could run from co-production and financing to distribution, post-production and production services.

“These points somehow fit together. They are not exclusive. They all feed into each other,” Salazar said, noting that Spanish films and productions were traveling farther internationally while Indian productions and streaming services were growing fast.

ICEX’s Mumbai office works with producers and distributors on market access, local partnerships, setting up businesses and regulatory requirements. It has also organized business missions involving Indian companies in animation, post-production and gaming.

For Indian producers looking to develop a project with Spanish partners, Guillermo Rodríguez, director of the Valladolid-based cultural institution Casa de la India, said: “The real roadmap is about building connections and building trust.”

India and Spain signed their audiovisual co-production agreement in 2012. Rodríguez said the scheme was being updated and that clear guidelines would be issued.

“If you plan to shoot in both countries or one of the countries, you have to make sure you follow those guidelines precisely. Under the co-production agreement, an Indian producer has to approach NFDC… and the Spanish co-producer has to go to ICAA,” he said.

NFDC is India’s National Film Development Corporation.

The session closed with a showcase of five Spanish projects seeking Indian collaborators. These included “My Parents Grand Bazaar,” the feature debut of Andalusian filmmaker Rakesh Narwani; “Serendipia,” an India-Mexico-Spain romance; “The Dragon Letter,” from Ladakh-born director Stanzin Jigmet, based on his short of the same name, which won gold in the narrative category at the 2026 Student Academy Awards; animated project “Mumu”; and documentary “Aana and Aai – The War to Become an Artist.”

Rodríguez noted that the two countries had largely stuck to familiar markets, with Spain looking toward Europe and Latin America and India toward English-speaking territories.

“Imagine the global Indian industry working with the Spanish-speaking world,” he said. “Because Spain is not just Spain. It’s access to the entire Spanish-speaking world – over 500 million people. So if you can bring those two cultural superpowers together, imagine the potential.”

1kenigj.title: China Box Office: ‘The Hunger Games’ Prequel Opens at No. 1
1kenigj.content:
Lionsgate Films’ dystopian prequel “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” debuted atop the mainland China box office during the Nov. 20–22 weekend, collecting RMB39.3 million ($5.9 million) over its three-day opening frame, according to data from Artisan Gateway.

New Classics Pictures’ crime procedural drama “Traces of Justice” moved to second place after a two-week rebound at the top, grossing $2.1 million in its eighth weekend. Directed by Chen Sicheng (“Detective Chinatown”) and co-written with Zhang Ji and Yan Zijie, the multi-decade investigation epic has amassed $113.6 million since its Oct. 1 premiere. Starring Zhang Yi, Ma Li, and Chen Minghao alongside guest appearances by Karry Wang, Fan Chengcheng, and Chen Feiyu, the drama tracks an elite public security detective solving major criminal cases based on real events.

Constantin Film and Sony Pictures’ horror reboot “Resident Evil” placed third, taking in $1.7 million in its seventh weekend to lift its cumulative gross to $83 million since rolling out on Oct. 5.

Zhijiang Film Media’s suspense thriller “Love Test” debuted in fourth position, pulling in $1.1 million across its two-day opening frame following a Nov. 21 release. Directed by Hou Xiaoyao from a script co-written with Xu Xiaohu and executive produced by Lu Yang and Wang Hongwei, the Chinese remake of the 2011 Colombian-Spanish thriller “The Hidden Face” stars Feng Shaofeng, Chen Yusi, and Li Meng. The narrative follows a concert pianist whose girlfriend stages her own disappearance to test his fidelity, only for his new love interest to move into his mountain villa and uncover unsettling clues behind the vanishing.

Beijing Joy Fun Pictures’ domestic body-swap comedy “Mr. & Mrs. Pardon” rounded out the top five, adding $900,000 in its eighth weekend to push its cumulative haul to $65.5 million since opening on Oct. 1. Directed by Shen Chunyang and written by Ma Duo, the satirical feature stars real-life comedic pair Shen Chunyang and Xiao Shenyang alongside Jia Bing and Yu Yang as an uninspired middle-aged couple forced to navigate marriage and domestic friction after swapping bodies.

Mainland China’s overall weekend box office reached $16 million, remaining locked in a sluggish late-fall stretch. Year-to-date box office revenue stands at $4.8 billion, trailing the same period in 2025 by 29.9%.
